t: Eight rows, from KICK to PERC, and an accent row. Each row has its own mute, solo and level. Pick an electronic kit, or an acoustic one: Jazz, Brush, Room, Orchestra and more. engines
Seven chord keys that follow your key and scale. SLOTS writes a progression with whole chords, 1 to 8 bars each. The sound is TAL NoiseMaker or a soundfont. manual
A mono line on a piano roll with ACCENT and SLIDE lanes, OCT − / +, ♭♯, RANDOM; the 303's WAVE, CUTOFF, RESO, ENV MOD, ACCENT, TUNE as its MODS. engines
Legato and portamento on Calf Monosynth, a ribbon that plays and adds vibrato as it is dragged up, soundfont instruments from Rhodes and vibes to sax, flute, fiddle and bagpipe. engines
Four banks × eight slots, each bank with its pattern; trim, PITCH ±12, REVERSE, record into a slot, the input's effects, CHOP and AUTO CHOP. manual
Sixteen pads on the step keys. Record straight onto a pad, play it once, loop it or reverse it, and hold a pad to latch it. The wave editor cuts a sample into pads. manual
Bass, lead and chords can sound like a soundfont instrument instead of their synth, grouped in the picker with ★ favourites and a SORT; an imported soundfont's presets join at once. manual
The knobs that shape the sound: FILTER, ENVELOPE, MOTION… for a soundfont, the synths' own knobs for a synth. The device knobs drive them, and a project or a preset keeps them. engines
Every machine's chain: DRIVE, COMPRESSOR, REVERB, EQ, PAN, SIDECHAIN, DELAY, each a card with its knobs, switched from the bar or the SELECT key. architecture
DROP, NO KICK, ONLY KICK, CRUSH, LO PASS, HI PASS, STUTTER and LOOP as pads (ALT + step keys 1–8), PHASER, ECHO and HEAVY as sends on ALT + the knobs. manual
Every melodic machine follows the root and scale (a key change snaps the lines); SWING 8 or SWING 16; the tempo on the header, templates and demos setting it. manual
MODE turns the step keys into pads for the machine on screen. ● records what you play, layering loop after loop. A MIDI keyboard plays along too. manual
Every strip at once (✱): level, pan, mute, solo, the step keys picking a strip, the big knob a fine level. manual
A step grid for the drums and samplers, a piano roll for the bass and lead, and a chord roll. Patterns run up to eight bars. LOCK stops a stray tap from changing what plays. manual

h: Features › SELECT and the note knobs
t: Pick notes and move them along the scale or by a step. Knobs 1–3 set their LENGTH, VELOCITY and NUDGE. manual
Save a pattern with its sound and tweaks. Browse by genre, star your favourites, and play presets straight from a USB stick. manual

h: Features › WITH ITS SOUND · MODS · BARS
t: What a preset brings with it: its sound source or kit, its MODS (only the parts it names), its bar count (or laid over the pattern's bars). manual
Twenty-two packs with five presets per instrument. Each pack sticks to one scale, so its parts play well together. Some are in 3/4 and 6/8. the packs
PROJECT ▾ → TEMPLATES: a new project at a tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX; SAVE TEMPLATE keeps the session's own; every pack ships one. manual
Autumn Leaves (a jazz trio and sax), 5AM (dark electronic pop over the changes of 4ÆM) and B3rlin (dark techno), on the image's own soundfonts, never changed by a SAVE. manual
SAVE (the name asked once, AGAIN? to write over), SAVE AS NEW, ★ favourites, DEMOS and MY PROJECTS groups; a new project starts clean. manual
One history for the project (the header's ↶ ↷, ALT + ◀ ▶): patterns, slots and the arrangement, a change over several machines as one step; a machine's own ↶ ↷ undo its changes alone. undo
AUTO records knob moves into lanes per machine; a long press on AUTO clears them. architecture
A whole project built over the remote-control fifo: samples, patterns, sounds and all. scripting
Up to sixteen, each with every machine's pattern. A shorter pattern loops (LOOP) or plays once (ONCE). Sounds, effects, tempo and key stay the same, so switching never drops a note. manual
A pick lands on the next bar, or waits for the section playing to end its pass; in LOOP up to three picks queue, each playing one pass. manual

h: Features › On the bar line, exactly
t: Each machine writes the new pattern into its track's other clip and libzynthbox swaps the two on the bar's first tick: no note drops or doubles (measured). design
ALT + step keys 9–16 pick sections 1–8 from any page. ALT + MODE shows all sixteen in the header. manual
Every section as a key, with a dot for each machine that plays. Rename, colour and reorder them, then line them up into a song with repeats. PLAY FROM HERE starts anywhere. manual
What PLAY plays: the section on screen looped, or the song through, the pages following it, stopping on the bar line after its end. manual
The plate sweeps in the section's colour and the page glows round its frame as a change lands; the keys fill with the section's progress. manual
A mic, a guitar or a line on jacks 4 and 5, with a level meter. Voice effects like ROBOT and TELEPHONE, and amps and pedals for the guitar. manual
On GUITAR: McLeod's pitch method as guitarix's tuner has it, AUTO or MANUAL strings, fifteen tunings, A4 430–450 Hz; it runs only while on screen. manual
ALT + ● records the master as a WAV; a machine's ● records its take; the metronome holds on during a take. manual

A video of the screen or a USB camera, or the sound alone as a WAV you can tag later. Three quality levels and a timer. With a mic plugged in, the music ducks while you talk. When it ends, delete it, rename it or send it. video
Add your laptops or PCs in SETTINGS → COMPUTERS. The password is used once and never stored. Files land in the computer's Downloads folder. video
PHONE · QR CODE: a link served by ravving on the Wi‑Fi, 15 minutes at most, WAITING FOR THE PHONE / SENDING / DOWNLOADED ✓; the way to an iPhone. manual
The USB page lists a stick's samples, soundfonts, presets and projects, ready to IMPORT. FILES → SEND… copies files onto it. EJECT before you pull it out. manual
Everything on the device, sorted by kind, newest first. SEND… or DELETE any file. PHONE · BROWSE opens the same list on your phone, to download from. manual
Speakers and headphones (PLAY THROUGH), files sent to a phone and received from one, pairing with a passkey, the setup a MIKO needs applied by ravving. bluetooth
The jacks, HDMI or a Bluetooth output, fed glitch-free through a loopback while the jacks keep the graph's clock, remembered and put back when the output returns. manual
A loop, a number of bars, or the whole SONG. Save it as WAV, FLAC, OGG or MP3, with its tags and a cover. manual
A .ravv zip of the project with every sample it uses; IMPORT makes a project of one, from the library or a stick. manual
Your tracks full screen, by track, album or artist, with a queue. Keys 1–3 switch views, the big knob sets the volume and knob 1 scrubs. manual
SETTINGS: USER and AUTHOR, credited on every exported track. manual
jalv runs the LV2 synths and effects: TAL NoiseMaker, Nekobi, Calf Monosynth, Dragonfly Reverb, TAP Echo and more. FluidSynth plays the kits and soundfonts. engines
Classic drum machines, a full General MIDI set, guitars, organs, basses and ambient pads. A soundfont from a USB stick works right away. the packs
PipeWire's JACK at 48 kHz and 256 frames: libzynthbox's passthroughs, the jalv inserts wired only while on, FluidSynth told the graph's clock; the clocks, links and xruns checked in one go. routing
Each machine in its own finish: the 909's cream, the 808's dark wood, the 303's lime, POLY‑6's blue, the lead's purple. Every screen follows one set of UI rules. UI rules
A short show as ravving starts. Pick ANIME, GLOW, STILL, ZOOM, ARU (the octopus or the wolf pup waving hello) or OFF in SETTINGS → STARTUP. manual
What's wrong right now, in plain words, worst first, and what to do about it: a sound that didn't start, dropouts, a stick that won't mount, or a full disk. manual

NOTES OUTSIDE THE SCALE, the startup look, SBC‑XQ for Bluetooth, the LANGUAGE, the video's quality, timer, source, mic, voice over and keys, the COMPUTERS list, HELP; each section on its own frame. manual

English, Spanish and Japanese, with the music terms musicians use in each; SETTINGS · LANGUAGE follows the device's own language or picks one, and the screen changes at once. A new language is one catalog to translate, this page included. translations
Built on the device, a setup page over Zynthbox: try it, make it the default, Zynthbox at boot again, remove; nothing bundled but ravving. packaging
CUIA commands and backend calls over the webconf fifo, the test suites and the screenshot tour that keep it honest. testing
Each number key opens a page, and every page is an instrument.

h: Features › Two samplers on one key.
t: Key 5 opens SAMPLE KING or the PAD SAMPLER; press it again to switch.

h: Features › Presets that bring their sound.
t: Twenty-two packs of patterns on a USB stick, written to follow your key.
Up to sixteen sections, each holding every machine's pattern.

h: Features › Record anything. Tune the guitar.
t: Plug in a mic, a guitar or a line, and record while the beat keeps going.

h: Features › Record the session as it happens.
t: Tap LIVE REC in the menu, and the whole session goes to a file.

h: Features › Out of the device, three ways.
t: One SEND… button, wherever there's a file.

h: Features › Export the track. Play it back.
t: PROJECT ▾ → EXPORT writes your track just as the speakers play it.
ravving is open source: a Qt 6 app on libzynthbox, GPL-3.0-or-later.
ravving comes from the store inside the Zynthbox app on your MIKO. It takes a couple of minutes, and you can always go back to Zynthbox.
A MIKO running Zynthbox. An internet connection, over Wi‑Fi or a cable.

Press MENU to open the main menu. Tap Apps , or press 2 . Tap Get New Apps . The store opens. Find ravving and tap Install . Press BACK . ravving now shows up in Apps. Can't find it? ravving may not be listed in the store yet. Check back soon.

In Apps , tap ravving . A setup page opens with four choices: Choice What it does TRY IT Starts ravving now. Zynthbox comes back at the next boot. MAKE IT THE DEFAULT Starts ravving every time the MIKO boots. ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN Zynthbox starts at boot again. ravving stays installed. REMOVE RAVVING Takes ravving off the MIKO. Press it twice. Pick TRY IT the first time. The setup page shows what's installed and what starts at boot.
From ravving, open MENU and press ZYNTHBOX in the power row. Removing ravving keeps your projects, takes and recordings.
When a new version is out, open the store again and tap Update on ravving. Then tap ravving in Apps and pick TRY IT or MAKE IT THE DEFAULT to install the new version.
Your first beat : make a beat in a few minutes.
A preset is a ready-made pattern for one instrument, sometimes with the sound it was written for. Here's how to load one, from your MIKO or from a USB stick.
Open the instrument's page: 1 to 5 . Tap the preset's name in the pattern toolbar, the box beside LOCK. The PRESETS dialog opens on the source your current pattern came from, with that preset marked.
SOURCE shows DEVICE, plus one chip for each USB stick plugged in. Pick a stick to play its presets straight from it, without copying anything. The row only appears when a stick is in.

The three LOAD switches decide what a preset brings: Switch On Off WITH ITS SOUND the instrument switches to the preset's sound your sound stays WITH ITS MODS the preset's MODS are set your MODS stay WITH ITS BARS the preset's own length laid over your bars: a shorter preset repeats, a longer one is cut Turning on WITH ITS SOUND turns on WITH ITS MODS too, since a sound is heard with its MODS. You can switch MODS off again. Your choices are remembered. A preset that carries a sound shows ♪ and the sound's name under its genre, plus "+ MODS" when it has MODS.
GROUP: a chip per genre, or ALL. SORT: AS LISTED or A–Z. ★: hold a preset to make it a favourite. Tap a preset to load it. The dialog closes, and the toolbar shows the preset's name.

Tap ↶ in the toolbar, or press ALT + ◀ . One undo puts your pattern back. The sound isn't part of the undo history, so it stays. To get yours back, tap the nameplate and pick it again. Every pack brings its own groove. Try a few, then undo the ones you don't like.
Sound sources : saving your own presets, and what a preset keeps. The genre packs : twenty-two packs to put on a stick.

h: Turn your loop into a song
p: Turn your loop into a song
t: A loop gets you started. A song needs parts: an intro, a verse, a drop. In ravving, each part is a section , and the song is the order they play in.

p: Turn your loop into a song
t: Press ALT + 1 from any page. Press it again to go back to where you were. Your loop is section 1 , named A. A new project's song already has it as its first part.

p: Turn your loop into a song
t: Tap ＋ . It copies the section on screen: A becomes A′. The copy is now the one on screen, and it joins the end of the song. Press ALT + 1 to go back to your instrument page, and change something. Add a snare, a bass line, or take the kick out. Your edits go into the section on screen only, so A stays as it was. Tap NEW instead of ＋ for an empty section.

p: Turn your loop into a song
t: Press ALT + 1 to open the SONG page again. Tap SONG at the top right, so PLAY plays the song from start to end. LOOP plays the section on screen only. Press PLAY . The page shows the part and bar playing, and the plate shows the part, like "2/2". The song stops at its end.

p: Turn your loop into a song
t: Repeats: pick a block in the song, and set ×1 to ×16 with + and − , or knob 2. Order: pick a block, and move it with ALT + ◀ ▶ . Length: a section lasts as long as its longest pattern. Set LENGTH for a fixed 1–8 bars. Names and colours: double-tap a section to rename it. COLOUR gives it another colour. ▶ PLAY FROM HERE starts the song at the block you picked. Verse, chorus, verse, drop. Now it's a song!

h: Switch by hand while you play
p: Turn your loop into a song
t: In LOOP, pick a section while the music plays. It takes over on the next bar line, exactly on time: tap its key on the SONG page; or press ALT + step keys 9–16 for sections 1–8, from any page.

p: Turn your loop into a song
t: PROJECT ▾ → EXPORT → WHAT: SONG records the whole song in one take.

p: Turn your loop into a song
t: Sections and the song : queueing sections, BAR or SECTION switching, and LOOP or ONCE for each machine.

h: Export a track and play it back
p: Export a track and play it back
t: Turn your project into a song file: a WAV, FLAC, OGG or MP3 with its tags and a cover. Then play it in the music player, or send it somewhere.

p: Export a track and play it back
t: Open PROJECT ▾ in the header and tap EXPORT .

p: Export a track and play it back
t: FILE NAME and TITLE. ARTIST and COMPOSER start from your profile's author, set in MENU → SETTINGS. ALBUM / MIXTAPE and GENRE offer the ones you typed last. The cover is drawn for you from the title and the artist.

h: Choose the format and where it goes
p: Export a track and play it back
t: FORMAT: WAV 24-BIT, FLAC LOSSLESS, OGG or MP3. USB: DEVICE ONLY, or a copy to a stick that's plugged in. COMPUTER: send it to one of your computers too, once it's written.

p: Export a track and play it back
t: WHAT: LOOP plays the section on screen for BARS × LOOPS . Knobs 1 and 2 set them. WHAT: SONG records the whole song, start to end. TAIL adds a few seconds at the end for the echoes to ring out. Knob 3 sets it. The dialog shows how long the track will be.

p: Export a track and play it back
t: Tap EXPORT TRACK . ravving plays your project from its first beat and records it, so keep quiet: the speakers are the mix. A bar shows how far it's got, and CANCEL stops it. When it's done, the dialog closes. The track is in the library's exports, with its cover and details beside it. Your first release! Give it a proper title before you send it out.

p: Export a track and play it back
t: Open MENU → MUSIC PLAYER . Your new track is at the top of TRACKS. ▶ plays a track, and + adds it to the queue. SEND… sends it to a USB stick, a computer or your phone. The big knob sets the volume, and knob 1 moves through the track. BACK leaves the player.

p: Export a track and play it back
t: EXPORT .RAVV saves a bundle: the project with every sample it uses. Another ravving opens it from PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT and plays it exactly the same.

p: Export a track and play it back
t: Exports and the music player : what a track keeps, and how loud it comes out. The music player : every key.
Record what you play as a video: the screen, or a USB camera, with the sound in sync. Or record the sound alone. Either way, the music keeps playing.

Press MENU and tap LIVE REC . Choose WHAT to record: VIDEO: the screen or a USB camera, with the sound, as an MP4 among your VIDEOS; AUDIO ONLY: just the sound, as a WAV among your TRACKS. Choose whether the MIC is in. With it on, your voice goes in over the music. Tap START . The dialog is the confirmation, so a stray tap never starts a recording.

The plate counts down, REC IN 3 , then shows the time: ● REC 00:04 . The menu closes first, so it isn't in the picture. On a video, every key you press is named at the bottom of the screen, so viewers can see what you played.

Press STOP . It ends the recording, and the music with it. LIVE REC stays on afterwards, ready: press RECORD to start another take, from any page. To switch it off, tap the LIVE REC card in the menu again.

The VIDEO SAVED dialog shows the file, how long it is, and its size. DELETE: tap it twice within three seconds. RENAME: give it a name of your own. SEND…: to a USB stick, one of your computers, or your phone. An audio recording also has METADATA… : tag it, draw its cover, and save it as WAV, FLAC, OGG or MP3, like an exported track. Sing along! With the MIC in, the music ducks under your voice.
With the MIC in, the music ducks while you talk, and comes back when you stop. If MIC TOO HOT shows up, turn the RECORDER's GAIN down.
MENU → SETTINGS → VIDEO has the QUALITY, the TIMER before a recording starts, the SOURCE (the screen or a USB camera), and the voice-over mix.
Video recordings and the computer link : every setting, talking over the music, and your computers.

h: Send a file to your phone
p: Send a file to your phone
t: Get a track, a video or a project onto your phone: no app, no pairing and no account. It works with any phone, iPhone included.

p: Send a file to your phone
t: The phone and your MIKO must be on the same Wi-Fi. The dialog tells you if the MIKO isn't on a network.

p: Send a file to your phone
t: Press MENU and tap FILES . Pick a kind on the left, like TRACKS or VIDEOS. Tap SEND… beside the file. Tap PHONE · QR CODE . A QR code appears. Point the phone's camera at it, and open the link. Safari or Chrome saves the file to the phone's Downloads, or Files on an iPhone.

p: Send a file to your phone
t: The dialog shows WAITING FOR THE PHONE , then SENDING with how far it's got, then DOWNLOADED ✓ . A message tells you when the whole file has arrived. The link is also shown in words, if you'd rather type it on a laptop.

p: Send a file to your phone
t: The link lasts while the dialog is open, for up to 15 minutes. Closing the dialog ends it.

h: Good to know › One file at a time
p: Send a file to your phone
t: One file at a time. Given several, it sends the first and says so. SEND… is everywhere: in FILES, after a video, in the music player, and in the presets and sound dialogs. Straight to your pocket. Now go play it to someone!

p: Send a file to your phone
t: PHONE · BROWSE , at the top of FILES, shows a QR code that opens your whole library as web pages. Each file has a DOWNLOAD button.

p: Send a file to your phone
t: Sending to a phone and Files in the manual.

Start with the ISSUES card in the menu. It reads ALL GOOD, or the number of issues lit in the colour of the worst one. Tap it for the list, worst first, each with what to do and a button where one helps, like RESTART RAVVING. Here are the common ones, by what you notice.

Is a machine muted, soloed out or paused? Look at its S, M and ❚❚ on the strip, or open the MIXER with ✱ . Is the master down? ALT + the big knob sets it, from anywhere. Where's the sound going? MENU → AUDIO OUTPUT picks the jacks, HDMI or a Bluetooth device. The sound comes out of one place only. Still nothing? The issues center lists an engine that couldn't start, or audio connections that never appeared.

h: The screen is black or very dim
t: Open MENU and turn knob 1 : it's the BRIGHTNESS slider.

h: A tap doesn't change the pattern
t: While the transport plays, LOCK keeps the note grids from writing, and flashes to tell you why. Tap LOCK in the pattern toolbar to edit anyway, or press STOP.

h: A speaker or headphones won't connect
t: A device that's asleep, waking up or busy with a phone gets called again three more times, over about 35 seconds. Its row reads "waking…" meanwhile. If ravving says NOT ANSWERING, free it from your phone, or turn it off and on, then connect again.

h: Only one plays at a time
t: Connecting a second speaker while another plays hands the sound over to it, and the first one disconnects.
Open the BLUETOOTH dialog and switch SBC-XQ off for that speaker. Each device has its own chip, so your other headphones keep the finer sound.
ravving routes the sound to it again by itself. If that doesn't bring it back, the issues center says the output plays no sound.

Several sticks or partitions? The USB card names each one, and asks which to open. It says read-only? That's a locked stick, or an installer image. Nothing is copied to it. Its page offers FORMAT, which erases the whole stick into one writable RAVVING drive. FORMAT and EJECT both ask for a second press. It wouldn't mount? The issues center says so.

MIC TOO HOT: the mic's peaks pass −6 dBFS. Turn the RECORDER's GAIN down. The music doesn't duck under your voice: the voice over is for a voice. With the RECORDER on GUITAR or LINE, the input is simply mixed in.
Tap RESTART RAVVING in the issues center. If ravving itself won't start, turn the MIKO off and on.
The manual : every page and dialog. Every key : what each key and knob does.
Each number key opens an instrument page. Every page starts with its own engine, and you can swap in another sound from the nameplate. Here's what each one can play.

Three drum machines, DRUMS 1, 2 and 3. Press 1 again to move between them. Engine: FluidSynth, playing soundfont drum kits. To start: a Roland TR909, a TR808 and a LINN9000. Classic drum machines: forty kits, from the Roland CR78, TR606 and TR727 to the SP1200, Simmons, Alesis HR16 and Yamaha RX11. Acoustic kits: Jazz, Brush, Standard, Room, Power and Orchestra, plus cumbia, Latin, folk and rock kits.

Engine: TAL NoiseMaker, a virtual analog synth, with its factory sounds. Zynthbox calls it Noize Mak3r. Or a soundfont: about fifty sounds. Pianos, Rhodes, Wurlitzer, organs, string sections, guitars, pads, and a set of strange "alien" textures.

Engine: Nekobi, a 303-style bass synth. Or: Calf Monosynth as an 808 sub bass. Or a soundfont: upright, acoustic, finger, fretless, picked, slap and synth basses, a sine sub, contrabass, cello, and an organ's low pedal.

Engine: Calf Monosynth, a monophonic synth. Or a soundfont: about forty sounds. Saxes, trumpets, flute, oboe, violin and cello, guitars clean and heavy, harp, celesta, music box, vibes, marimba and more.

Key 5 opens SAMPLE KING or the PAD SAMPLER. Press it again to switch. Engine: libzynthbox's own sampler, playing your samples. SAMPLE KING: four banks of eight slots, to trim, pitch, reverse and chop. PAD SAMPLER: sixteen pads on the step keys, MPC-style.

Every page has a SOUND EFFECTS chain, and the header has the LIVE FX. Effect Engine DRIVE Calf Saturator COMPRESSOR, EQ, PAN, SIDECHAIN libzynthbox's mixer REVERB Dragonfly Room Reverb DELAY TAP Echo CRUSH, PHASER (LIVE FX) Calf Crusher, Calf Phaser STUTTER, LOOP (LIVE FX) ravving's own

Every engine here is open source, and all of them ship with Zynthbox. ravving doesn't bundle any of them: it starts them on your MIKO as it needs them. Engine Licence FluidSynth LGPL-2.1-or-later TAL NoiseMaker (DISTRHO's port) GPL-2.0 Nekobi (DISTRHO) GPL-2.0-or-later The Calf plugins LGPL Dragonfly Reverb GPL-3.0-or-later TAP plugins GPL-2.0-or-later jalv, which hosts the LV2 plugins ISC libzynthbox open source ravving itself is GPL-3.0-or-later.
From silence to a saved project in a few minutes. You'll write a drum beat, add a bass line, play it and save it.
Open PROJECT ▾ in the header and tap NEW. Every page starts empty, with one section, "A".

Press 1 to open the drums. The KICK row is picked already. ▲ ▼ move between the rows. Press step keys 1, 5, 9 and 13 . Each key lights a step on the KICK row. That's a kick on every beat, also called four on the floor.
Press ▼ to move to the SNARE row. Press step keys 5 and 13 : the snare lands on beats two and four. Press ▼ three more times, to the HAT row, and press 3, 7, 11 and 15 for off-beat hi-hats.

Press PLAY . The step keys light up as the playhead moves along the bar. While it plays, the note grids are locked so a stray tap can't change your beat. To edit while it plays, tap LOCK in the pattern toolbar. Press STOP when you're ready to move on.

Press 3 to open the bass. Tap a few cells on the piano roll. Each tap writes a note there; tap it again to remove it. Press PLAY to hear the bass with your drums. Every melodic machine follows the project's key and scale, which you set at the left of the header.
The big knob sets the volume of the machine on screen. ALT + the big knob sets the master volume, from anywhere.

Tap SAVE in the header. The first time, ravving asks for a name and the on-screen keyboard comes up. It suggests a name, and RANDOM picks another; type your own or keep it. After that, SAVE writes over the project. It asks AGAIN? first, so press it twice within three seconds. Your project is now in PROJECT ▾, ready to open next time. You made a beat! Now give it a bass line it deserves, or a whole song.
Sections and the song : turn your loop into a song. Playing and editing : play live, move notes, shape single notes. Sound sources : give the bass and lead another sound, and load pattern presets.
This is the interim manual: what each page, key and dialog does. A friendlier guide with screenshots is on its way.

Hi! Five keys, five pages, eight machines. Let's make some noise. Each of the five number keys on the left opens a page: Key Page What plays (the nameplate shows it) 1 DRUMS 1 · 2 · 3 (press 1 again to cycle) A drum kit each: Roland TR909, Roland TR808 and LINN9000 to start, or any kit from the device's drum machines folder 2 CHORDS TAL NoiseMaker with its factory sounds, or a soundfont instrument (Rhodes, vibes, organ, strings…) 3 BASS DISTRHO Nekobi, a 303-style bass, or a soundfont bass (upright, acoustic, finger, fretless, synth) 4 LEAD Calf Monosynth, or a soundfont instrument (Rhodes, vibes, guitar, sax, flute…) 5 SAMPLE KING · PAD SAMPLER (press 5 again to switch) Four banks of eight sample slots, or sixteen MPC-style pads All five pages share the top bar: key and scale, transport, tempo and swing, the LIVE FX, the instruments and the master volume. Every machine has the same parts: a mix strip; its MODS, the knobs that shape its sound; its pattern editor; a SOUND EFFECTS chain. A song is made of SECTIONS that change on the bar line, and your whole session is saved in a project.

ravving comes from the Zynthbox Store's Apps category as an AppImage. The AppImage opens a setup page over Zynthbox with four choices: TRY IT, MAKE IT THE DEFAULT, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN, REMOVE RAVVING. Projects, takes and recordings stay when ravving is removed.

h: Shortcuts you'll use all the time
t: Press What happens ALT + ▲ Jump to the header, from anywhere ALT + step keys 1–8 Switch the LIVE FX on and off: DROP, NO KICK, ONLY KICK, CRUSH, LO PASS, HI PASS, STUTTER, LOOP ALT + knobs 1–3 PHASER, ECHO and HEAVY ALT + big knob Master volume MODE The instrument on screen goes OFF → LIVE → STEP + LIVE → OFF STOP, while stopped Panic: every held note ends Long press on a machine's S Solo that machine alone While you hold ALT, the step keys light up orange and the LIVE FX pads show their key numbers.

Turn LIVE on with MODE, and the step keys become something you can play: Bass, lead and the chords' NOTES tab: the scale is spread over all 16 keys. ▲ ▼ shift the octave. The chords' CHORDS and SLOTS tabs: you get the seven chord keys of your key.

STEP entry writes what you play at a cursor. ◀ ▶ move the cursor a step. Keys you hold together land in the same step, so a chord goes into one column. With the transport stopped, SELECT writes the selected row at the cursor: a note, or the chord on CHORDS. With both LIVE and STEP on, ▲ ▼ walk the rows instead of the octave. Each row sounds as you reach it, so you can find the note by ear first.

One finger drags sideways to page through the bars. On a piano roll it also drags the rows up and down; past eight semitones, the octave shifts. Two fingers pinch to zoom. A tap still toggles a note. The pointer only shows while a mouse is plugged in.

The first SAVE asks for the project's name, and the on-screen keyboard comes up. Later saves write over it. Press SAVE twice within three seconds (it asks AGAIN?). SAVED means nothing has changed since; the button wakes up with your next edit. SAVE AS NEW asks for a new name. PROJECT ▾ lists your projects and the demos. Tap one to open it. If you have unsaved changes, tap it a second time to confirm. A long press or ★ makes a project a favourite. The row at the bottom always works on the project you have open: NEW, TEMPLATES and IMPORT, then SAVE AS NEW, then EXPORT.

The header's ↶ ↷ step the whole project back and forth. ALT + ◀ ▶ do the same on the machine pages. A change that touched several machines at once counts as one step: CLEAR ALL, or a key change that moved both the bass and the lead. A machine's own ↶ ↷, in its toolbar, undo only that machine's changes. What comes back: Patterns and slots. The arrangement: a removed section with its content, a rename, a colour, a length, and edits to the song. What doesn't: sounds, the mix and the project's settings. Picking a section isn't a step either. More in Undo and redo .

h: LOCK: keep a stray tap from changing what plays
t: LOCK is the first button of every pattern toolbar. While it's on, the note grids don't write anything. Taps on cells, step keys, STEP entry, SELECT's moves and the note knobs are all refused, and LOCK flashes to tell you why. You can still scroll, page and listen. PLAY turns LOCK on. STOP turns it off again. Tap LOCK while playing to edit anyway. It then stays unlocked after you stop. Tap LOCK while stopped to lock the grids. It then stays locked. There's one LOCK for every page, and a take (●) still records. Headbang all you want: while it plays, LOCK keeps your beat safe.

h: SELECT: move notes after you've written them
t: SELECT sits in the pattern toolbar of the bass, lead and chords, beside ♭♯. While it's on, a tap on the grid picks a note instead of writing one. Tap again to unpick it. A tap on a held note's tail picks that note. ▲ ▼ move every picked note one note of the key up or down. With ♭♯ on, they move a semitone. Length, accent and slide come along. Each move is one undo step. On the chords page, the CHORDS view picks chords and moves them a degree. The NOTES view picks single notes. A held chord always moves as one. A long press on SELECT picks every note (or chord) in all the bars, so you can move the whole pattern at once. Turning SELECT off drops the picks.

On the bass and lead, pick notes with SELECT, then turn knobs 1–3 to change them together. A readout at the top right of the grid shows the first picked note's values, with the knob badges. Knob Setting Range One detent 1 LENGTH (the lighter cells) 1 step to 4 bars a step 2 VELOCITY 1–127 4 3 NUDGE , from where the swing puts the note half a step early to half a step late a 16th of a step A long press on a cell also sets a note's length. The ACCENT lane's cell fills to the velocity, bright red when accented. A tap there still flips the accent: full, or back to the plain velocity. A LIVE take with Q off records a nudge for each hit. These settings move with the note, each detent is one undo step, and they're kept with the project and in a saved pattern preset. The big knob stays the volume, and a focused group of dials keeps its own knobs.

On the chords page, SLOTS lets you compose chord by chord: Tap a slot. Play a chord key. The next slot arms itself. Set each slot's length: 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars. All slots together never pass the pattern's eight bars; the "n / 8 BARS" readout keeps count. The slots write the chord pattern, and PLAY plays them in order with the current slot lit. ＋ adds four more slots, up to eight, and − takes them away. If you change the pattern in the CHORDS or NOTES view, the view says PATTERN CHANGED and dims the slots. Editing a slot then rebuilds the pattern from the slots. Undo brings your edits back.
The header across the top is shared by every page. ▲ from a page's strip lands on it, ◀ ▶ walk its groups, and ▼ or BACK go back to the page.

ROOT and SCALE, at the left, set the project's key. Every melodic machine follows them: the bass, the lead and the chords play in that key, and a key change moves their lines with it. Notes from outside the scale have their own setting (Notes outside the scale, below).

BPM: the tempo. With the TEMPO group focused, knob 1 sets it. When another device clocks ravving, it shows that device's tempo and can't be changed here. SWING: knob 2, from 50 % (straight) to 75 % (the heaviest shuffle). Tap its caption to swing the 8ths (SWING 8, for jazz) or the 16ths (SWING 16, for house and hip hop). Templates and demos set both when they start a project.

Eight pads that change the whole mix while you play. Tap them in the header, or hold ALT and press step keys 1–8. Pad What it does DROP While held, the kick cuts out and a high-pass sweeps up. Both come back on release. NO KICK, ONLY KICK Silence every kick, or everything but the kicks. One switches the other off. CRUSH The mix through a bit crusher. LO PASS, HI PASS A filter sweep: down to 300 Hz, or up to 950 Hz. STUTTER While held, the current 16th repeats. LOOP While held, the current beat repeats. NO KICK, ONLY KICK, LO PASS and HI PASS switch on with a tap and off with another. DROP and CRUSH act while held; hold one for half a second and it stays on, until the next tap. Dragging on CRUSH, STUTTER or LOOP changes how much: fewer bits, or a shorter or longer repeat. PHASER, ECHO and HEAVY sit beside the pads. Hold ALT and turn knobs 1–3 to set them from anywhere.

ALT + ● records everything the speakers play, from any page, as a WAV among your recordings. The RECORD light turns red. Press ALT + ● again to stop. You'll find the file in the music player. Only one recording runs at a time: while this one runs, the RECORDER can't take.

✱ opens the MIXER: every instrument at once, each on its own strip with a meter. Press ✱ or BACK to go back, or a number key for that page. Pick a strip with ◀ ▶ or a step key. The step lights show the strips: muted ones dim, the picked one white. Knob 1 sets its level, knob 2 its pan, and the big knob a fine level. SELECT mutes it, and ALT + SELECT solos it. A tap on a nameplate opens that instrument's page.

Page 5 holds two samplers. Press 5 again to swap between SAMPLE KING and the PAD SAMPLER; ravving remembers which one you used. SAMPLE KING gives you four banks (A to D) of eight slots, and each bank has its own pattern. The bank on screen is the one that plays.

Pick a slot (its row in the grid) and tap LOAD to choose one of your samples. Or record one: ● REC records the device's input straight into the slot, and ● again stops. The take lands in the slot, trimmed to its last burst of sound. INPUT sets up what's plugged in, the gain and the monitor.

Drag the start and end handles on the waveform. Once the waveform has the focus, knobs 1 and 2 move them too. Set PITCH up to 12 semitones up or down. Flip REVERSE to play it backwards. A slot plays one-shot: hitting it again cuts the last hit off.

h: Chop and play it › Chop it
t: Chop it. CHOP and AUTO CHOP open the wave editor and spread the pieces over a bank's slots (see the wave editor ).

h: Chop and play it › Play it
t: Play it. Each row of the step grid is a slot, with an accent row underneath. Knobs 1–3 set the selected row's mute, solo and level, just like the drums.

h: Chop and play it › Play it live
t: Play it live. Turn LIVE on and step keys 1–8 play the slots, with key 9 held for accents. A MIDI keyboard plays them too.
Sixteen pads in four banks (A to D), laid out like an MPC. Pick a pad on screen and its sample, its tools and its settings show up beside the pads; its 16 steps sit underneath.

LOAD picks a sample for the pad. ● REC records the input into it. With SMART on, the take stops by itself once the sound goes quiet. Either way, the pad gets it trimmed to its last burst. COPY copies a pad onto another. CLEAR empties it. ERASE removes the pad's hits from the pattern.

NOTE ON plays the pad only while you hold it. With it off, a tap plays the whole sample (one-shot). LOOP loops it from the loop point. REVERSE plays it backwards. MUTE silences it, and UNMUTE ALL brings every pad back.

The tabs put three settings each on knobs 1–3, and ◀ ▶ switch tabs: Tab Settings TRIM start and end MIX volume and pan AMP ENV attack and decay TUNE semitones, then fine PLAY mono or poly, and a mute group FILTER type, cutoff and resonance

Turn LIVE on and the 16 step keys become the 16 pads. A tap plays a pad. Hold one for half a second and it latches, looping until you tap it again. STOP ends every latched loop. PAD FX: while a pad plays, hold ECHO, TAPE STOP, SCRATCH, STUTTER, SKIP or REVERSE to throw an effect on it. Let go and it's back to normal.

Switch 16 LVL on and all sixteen pads play the pad you had selected, spread by TYPE: VELOCITY: soft to hard. TUNE: a semitone per pad. SCALE: up your project's scale. The kit's MODS set the kit's volume and tuning for every pad.

Both samplers share it. CHOP cuts a sample into pieces three ways: REGIONS: equal slices. THRESHOLD: at the hits louder than a level. MANUAL: tap the wave to add a cut, and tap a cut to remove it. AUTO CHOP opens the editor straight on the hits. In the editor: ◀ ▶ change the chop type, and the big knob sets the slices or the threshold. NORMALISE raises the sample to full level. TRIM cuts the silence at both ends. APPLY sends the pieces to a bank's slots or to the pads.

The project has one history. The header's ↶ ↷ (and ALT + ◀ ▶ on the machine pages) walk it back and forth, and a toast names each step ("UNDO · CHORDS + BASS"). A machine's own ↶ ↷ on its pattern toolbar undo that machine's last change only, wherever it is in the history. What is undone: every machine's notes, steps, chords, slots, accents, slides, lengths, automation and live timing, and the arrangement: which sections there are, their order, names, colours and lengths, and the song. A section removed comes back whole, in its place. What is not: the sounds, the mix, the effects and the project's settings (tempo, swing, key). Picking a section is not a step either. One step: a change that touches several machines at once is one step, like CLEAR ALL or a key change that moves the bass and the lead. So are quick changes in a row (a knob turning, a handle dragged) and a whole recorded take. The history keeps the last 100 steps, and starts afresh when a project is opened or a new one begins.

The bass, lead and chords don't have to sound like their own synth. Tap the nameplate to open the machine's sounds: Its own engine first: the 303 on BASS, Calf Monosynth on LEAD, TAL NoiseMaker and its factory sounds on CHORDS. Then soundfont instruments , played by FluidSynth from the device's own soundfonts: an upright and other basses, Rhodes, vibes, organ, strings, sax, flute and more. Picking one swaps the engine for the other. A soundfont sound has MODS of its own: FILTER, ENVELOPE and MOTION. Your choice is saved with the project.

h: Acoustic sounds for jazz and friends
t: Machine Sounds CHORDS Grand piano (Fazioli), Upright piano (Kawai), Jazz guitar LEAD Alto sax , Tenor sax , Grand piano BASS Upright The drum machines' kit picker has an ACOUSTIC group too. These are General MIDI kits from the FluidR3 soundfont: Jazz and Brush (with the ride and the hi-hat foot on their rows, or with the crash), Standard and Room . Two more things help jazz feel right: A bass or lead note can last longer than a step. Long-press a cell to stretch the row's note up to it. Tap the header's swing caption to swing the 8ths (SWING 8) or the 16ths (SWING 16).

CHORDS also has the image's pad soundfonts, grouped by name in its picker: Strings: Ensemble, Fat, Digital, Rise, Bowed, Piano. Organ: Phaser, Pipe 16+8+4, House, Extreme. Alien, from the "Ambients & Drones" fonts: The Thing, Strange voices, Crystal voice, Glassy, Winds, Chaos, The Pulse. They suit a sustained, polyphonic machine: the chords hold while the voicing lasts, and the key keeps them in tune with the bass and lead. The sound pickers group their lists with GROUP chips, ★ for your favourites (the star, or ALT + SELECT) and SORT, as listed or A–Z. They remember the group and the sort per instrument.

Open PRESET on a pattern toolbar. SAVE CURRENT AS NEW keeps the pattern together with the machine's sound: its source or factory sound, and its MODS. On the drums it keeps the kit and the kit's MODS. Every pack brings its own groove, and the sound it was written for. When you save, two switches decide what goes in. Both are on each time the dialog opens: WITH ITS SOUND: the source or kit that's playing. WITH ITS MODS: the MODS you've set. A knob nobody turned is left out. With both off, only the pattern is saved. A preset that carries a sound shows ♪ and the sound's name under its genre, plus "+ MODS" when it keeps MODS.

Three switches at the top of the presets dialog decide what a preset brings along: WITH ITS SOUND (off by default) switches the machine to the preset's sound. WITH ITS MODS (off by default) sets the preset's MODS, only the parts it names. A preset without MODS leaves yours alone. WITH ITS BARS (on by default) brings the preset's own bar count. Off, the preset is laid over your bars from the first one: a shorter preset repeats, a longer one is cut. Turning SOUND on turns MODS on too, since a sound is heard with its MODS. You can then switch MODS off again. MODS on alone brings a preset's MODS to the sound already playing. With all of them off, only the pattern loads. Your choices are remembered. If the device doesn't have a preset's source or kit, that part of the sound stays as it is. The samplers' presets keep no sound, because their sound is in their banks. The presets that come with ravving keep no sound either. A preset copied to a stick carries its sound in its file.

The presets dialog works like the sound pickers: A GROUP chip per genre , and SORT: as listed or A–Z. ★ favourites: long-press a preset, tap the ★ in its corner, or press ALT + SELECT. Favourites are kept per instrument by the preset's name, so a stick's preset and the same one copied to the device share their ★. The dialog opens on ALL when the group you last viewed would hide the preset on screen.

A template is how a project starts: its tempo, swing, key (root and scale) and LIVE FX knobs (PHASER, ECHO, HEAVY). Open PROJECT ▾ → TEMPLATES, beside NEW. Pick SOURCE: the device, or a USB stick (read straight from its ravving/presets/templates/ folder). Choose a template. It starts a new project with those settings. With unsaved changes, it asks first, just like NEW. SAVE TEMPLATE keeps your current session's settings as a template on the device, and DELETE removes one. The USB dialog's PRESETS copies templates both ways. Every genre pack comes with a template, and some packs have one for each key.

NEW, with or without a template, puts every page back to its defaults: an empty pattern on each machine, with no preset loaded; each machine's own engine with the default sound, mix, MODS and SOUND EFFECTS; one section, "A"; the LIVE FX at rest. A template only adds its tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX knobs on top. The demo patterns only come back through a project or a preset.

ravving comes with a few demo projects, in PROJECT ▾ → DEMOS. They use only the image's own soundfonts, so they sound the same on any MIKO. Open a demo like any project. SAVE keeps your changes as your own project under the demo's name; the demo itself never changes and can't be deleted.

A song is more than one loop. A section holds every machine's pattern at once (an intro, a verse, a bridge) and which machines rest in it. The sounds, effects, levels, tempo and key belong to the whole project, so changing section never restarts an engine. Sections are live: the one on screen is the one you edit, and your edits stay in it when you pick another. You can have up to 16, and they're saved with the project.

ALT + step keys 9–16 pick sections 1–8 from any page. They light up in the sections' colours while ALT is held. ALT + 1–8 stay the LIVE FX pads. X and Y , the two keys beside the big knob, go to the previous and next section from any page or dialog, wrapping round. Press again before the switch lands to move the pick further instead of queueing another. With only one section, a message tells you to add more on the SONG page. The SONG page (below) has a key for every section. While the music plays, a pick takes over on the next bar line, exactly on time: no note drops or doubles, and machines whose part doesn't change just keep playing. When stopped, a pick is immediate.

h: When a switch lands: BAR or SECTION
t: The SONG page's SWITCH setting is saved with the project: BAR: a section you pick takes over on the next bar. SECTION: it waits for the section playing to finish its pass, then switches on that bar line. Its key blinks meanwhile, and the playing one stays lit. Pick the playing one again to cancel; stop to switch at once. A one-bar section ends every bar. A switch always lands on a bar line, never mid-bar.

In LOOP you can line up to three picks. Each plays one pass, then the next takes over, and the last one keeps looping. The keys show their place in the queue: 1 blinking means next. Pick a queued key again to take it out of the queue. Pick the playing section to empty the queue. A fourth pick is refused with QUEUE FULL. Stopping puts the first one in place and drops the rest. In SONG, one pick waits at a time, and a new pick replaces it.

h: LOOP or ONCE for each machine
t: Each machine's strip has a LOOP | ONCE button beside ❚❚, saved per section like ❚❚. A section lasts as long as its longest pattern, or as long as you set its LENGTH. A shorter pattern LOOP s through it by default: two bars of drums play twice under a four-bar lead. On ONCE , it plays its own bars once and rests until the section starts again. The rest starts exactly on the bar line, and a ringing note finishes naturally. While it rests, no playhead shows, and a hit you play live is heard but not written.

The plate: the header's project plate shows the section on screen as a square key with its number, in its colour. It blinks while it waits for the bar line. Tap it to open the SONG page. When a section changes, the plate sweeps in its colour and the instrument page glows round its frame, once. The section keys fill up with the section's progress, here and on the SONG page.

Long-press the project plate, or press ALT + MODE , to swap the LIVE FX pads in the header for the section keys. Do it again to bring the pads back. MODE lights orange while ALT is held; MODE alone still cycles the entry mode. Tap a key to pick it (on the next bar while playing). ▶ marks the one sounding, and its progress fills it. Swipe a key up to remove that section. It follows your finger and flies off past half its height. The last section can't be removed. Swipe sideways when there are more than fit. The strip also slides to the section that becomes current, or that the song reaches. ＋ stays pinned at the end of the strip. With the keys in the header, ALT + 1–16 pick sections 1–16. While the header's section group has the focus (◀ ▶ onto it), the step keys alone pick them.

Open it with ALT + 1 from anywhere, and press it again to go back. It sits under the header, like the MIXER. The sections are square keys with their number and name, eight to a row. The first row matches the ALT keys. Each key has a dot for every machine that sounds in it. Tap picks a section, double tap renames it, hold and drag moves it. × deletes it, after a second tap. ＋ copies the section on screen (A becomes A′). A new section, empty (NEW) or copied (＋), joins the end of the song and becomes the one on screen. The row above the sections has RENAME, NEW (an empty section), COLOUR, LENGTH (1–8 bars, or AUTO for the longest pattern), MOVE and ADD TO SONG. The song is a strip of blocks, each as wide as its bars times its repeats. Pick a block to move it, set its repeats (×1 to ×16) or remove it. Key On the SONG page ◀ ▶ Walk the keys or blocks ▲ ▼ Move between the section keys and the song SELECT or a step key Pick ALT + ◀ ▶ Move the picked key or block Knob 1 Length Knob 2 Repeats BACK Leave

LOOP | SONG on the SONG page sets what PLAY plays: the section on screen, looped, or the song from start to end. In SONG, each part is ready on time, and the song stops on the bar line after its end. The playing block shows its progress, and the plate shows the part, like "6/9".

h: Play the whole song › The instrument pages follow the song
t: The instrument pages follow the song. Their note grids are locked while it plays, as always while music plays (see LOCK). Unlock them to edit, and your edit goes into the section playing. ▶ PLAY FROM HERE starts the song at any block. Picking a section by hand while the song plays jumps to that section's first part. A section the song doesn't use switches back to LOOP. To record it all, EXPORT → WHAT: SONG records the whole song in one take, plus its tail. LOOP records BARS × LOOPS instead.

ravving speaks English, Spanish and Japanese, with the words musicians use in each: BATERÍA, BOMBO, COMPÁS; ドラム, キック, 小節. Pick one in MENU → SETTINGS → LANGUAGE. SYSTEM, the default, follows the device's own language. The screen changes at once. The keys printed on the device (MENU, ALT, SELECT…) and the machines' names stay as printed. The webpage has Spanish and Japanese pages too, with a switcher in its top bar; the docs are in English.

ravving shows its logo while it starts, then plays a short show into the page. Pick the look in MENU → SETTINGS → STARTUP. It applies from the next start: Look What it does ANIME Fast cuts through the five flow-lens logos into the glow one GLOW One at random, its halo swelling STILL One at random, a fade ZOOM The fluid logo rushing out past the screen ARU The pixel octopus or the wolf pup, at random, waving hello and jumping OFF No show While the studio loads, the splash is a still picture, so the start stays quick.
PROJECT ▾ → EXPORT saves your project out of the device, into the library's exports/ folder. There are two kinds.

The whole production as the speakers hear it. ravving plays the project from its first beat for BARS × LOOPS bars, plus a TAIL for the echoes, and records it cut to the sample. Formats: WAV 24-bit, FLAC, OGG Vorbis or MP3. Tags: title, artist, album or mixtape, genre, composer, comment, date and BPM. A cover, drawn for it from the title and the artist, with MADE WITH RAVVING. A JSON file beside it with the same details. The master's level is kept as it is. A track that would go over full scale is pulled down to −0.1 dBFS, and the JSON file says so. The ARTIST and COMPOSER start from your profile's author (MENU → SETTINGS: USER and AUTHOR). The ALBUM and GENRE you typed last are offered again.

A .ravv zip of the project with every sample it uses, so another ravving plays it exactly the same. PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists the bundles in exports/ , and in the library's main folder where transfers land, and turns one into a project.

MENU → SETTINGS → INTERACTIONS has NOTES OUTSIDE THE SCALE , on by default. It decides what happens when you play a note outside your key, for example on a MIDI keyboard, on the lead, the bass or the chords' NOTES: On: the note sounds and is recorded, in its own row on the piano roll. Off: it's muted there and never recorded. The drums, the samplers and chords played by degree ignore this setting.

h: Video recordings and the computer link
t: The control center's LIVE REC card records your session.

Tap LIVE REC. A dialog asks WHAT to record: VIDEO: the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, saved as an MP4 in the library's videos/ folder. AUDIO ONLY: just the sound, a 24-bit WAV among your TRACKS in the exports folder. Choose whether the MIC is in. Tap START. The dialog is the confirmation, so a stray tap never starts a recording. While LIVE REC is on, the device's RECORD key starts a recording and STOP ends it, from any page. The music keeps playing. A new project switches LIVE REC off.

SETTINGS · VIDEO has: QUALITY: three levels, none of which costs the sound anything. TIMER: a countdown before a recording starts. SOURCE: the screen or a USB camera. MIC: puts the RECORDER's input in the video's sound. VOICE: the voice-over mix, below. They also apply to a recording that's already running.

With the MIC in, ravving mixes your voice over the music: Sing along: the music ducks under your voice and comes back when you stop. While you talk, the music ducks under your voice: DUCK −6, −12 or −18 dB, −12 by default. Your voice is lifted by +6 or +12 dB and made clearer, with a low cut and a presence lift. ravving tells your voice apart from the speakers leaking into the mic, so the beat doesn't duck itself. A limiter keeps the mix from clipping. The mic's LEVEL is shown from the moment VIDEO is on, in SETTINGS and on the project plate. MIC TOO HOT means its peaks pass −6 dBFS: turn the RECORDER's GAIN down. With the RECORDER on GUITAR or LINE, the input is mixed in as it is.
VIDEO SAVED or LIVE REC SAVED offers: DELETE, on the left. A second tap within three seconds confirms.

RENAME. The file keeps its extension. SEND… to a USB stick, one of your computers or your phone. METADATA… for an audio recording. It opens the export dialog over the file to tag it, draw its cover and save it as WAV, FLAC, OGG or MP3. The same SEND… is on the music player's tracks, in FILES and in the presets dialogs. The export dialog can also send a new track or bundle to a computer as it's written.

SETTINGS · COMPUTERS holds any number of laptops or PCs on your network. Tap ADD A COMPUTER. Enter its host, your user name and your password. The password is used once, to install the device's key on that computer. Files you send land in that computer's Downloads folder. Each computer has CHANGE (set it up again), TEST and FORGET.

Every SEND… button has a third destination, beside the USB sticks and the computers: PHONE · QR CODE . You'll find SEND… in FILES, VIDEO SAVED, the music player, the presets dialogs and the sound picker. It works with any phone, iPhone included, with no pairing, app or account. Make sure the phone is on the same Wi-Fi as the device. The dialog tells you if the device isn't on a network. Tap PHONE · QR CODE. A QR code appears. Point the phone's camera at it and open the link. Safari or Chrome saves the file to the phone's Downloads (Files on an iPhone). The dialog shows WAITING FOR THE PHONE, then SENDING n %, then DOWNLOADED ✓, and a message tells you when the whole file has arrived. The link is also shown in words, if you'd rather type it. The link works while the dialog is open, for up to 15 minutes. Closing the dialog ends it. It sends one file at a time. Given several, it sends the first and says so.

h: The ravving page on your phone
t: The same server also carries the ravving page : the instructions, the features and every shortcut. The device has no browser of its own, so SETTINGS → HELP → OPEN shows the page as a QR code for a phone, or an address for a laptop. The QR code points at the public page, https://ravving.github.io/ , which works from anywhere. The device's own address sits under it ( http://<device>:8098/help/ ), for a Wi-Fi without internet.

The control center's FILES card shows everything in your library by kind, newest first: projects, templates, presets, samples, takes, the RECORDER's takes, recordings, tracks, bundles, soundfonts, MIDI files, videos and received files. Each file has SEND… (a USB stick, one of your computers, or your phone) and DELETE . FILES is the one place where files leave the device or get deleted. The PROJECT dialog opens, saves and exports, and the USB page brings a stick's files in.

PHONE · BROWSE , at the top of FILES, shows a QR code that opens your library as web pages on a phone or laptop on the same Wi-Fi: every kind, with how many files it has; each kind's files, with their details, size and date; a DOWNLOAD button for each file. Projects, and anything else that is a folder, are listed as "on the device". The link stays open until 15 minutes pass without the phone asking for anything, even with the dialog closed. After that, the phone says the link has run out.
Plug a USB stick in and ravving mounts it when it needs it. When you're done, press EJECT (in the export dialog or on the USB page) and pull the stick out once it's safe.

Exports: a stick shows up as a USB row in the export dialog. Your track or bundle is saved on the device as always, and also copied to the stick's ravving/exports/ or ravving/projects/ folder. A saved project: send it from FILES. SEND… packs it into a bundle for the stick. Opening a project from a stick: PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists the bundles on every stick plugged in, next to the ones on the device.

The drawer's USB card opens the USB page. It has two sides: ON USB lists what's on the stick by kind: SAMPLES, SOUNDFONTS, PROJECTS, TRACKS and MIDI FILES. Tap IMPORT to copy one to the device; it then reads ✓ ON DEVICE. FROM DEVICE lists your library, each file with TO USB. IMPORT ALL, next to the folder path, copies every new file of the folder on screen in one go. A whole sample pack is one tap, with a progress readout and a STOP button. Files you import land here: Kind Where Samples samples/imported/<stick>/ , keeping the stick's folders Soundfonts soundfonts/ MIDI files midi/ Tracks exports/ , where the music player finds them Projects imported as a bundle On the device's keys: ◀ ▶ switch the kind, ALT + ◀ ▶ switch the side, ▲ ▼ pick a file, SELECT copies it, and EJECT sits in the header.

Open a pattern toolbar's PRESET. With a stick in, a SOURCE row appears: DEVICE, or USB · . Pick the stick to see its presets for that machine and play one straight from there, without copying it. One undo step puts your pattern back. The dialog opens on the source your current pattern came from, with that preset marked.

A soundfont you import works right away: If it looks like a drum kit, it joins the kit picker under IMPORTED. Every preset in it becomes a sound for the chords, bass and lead, listed as " · " and grouped by font.

h: More than one stick, or a locked one
t: With several sticks or partitions plugged in, the USB card names each one and asks which to open. A read-only stick (a locked stick, or an installer image) says so. Nothing is copied to it, and its page offers FORMAT. FORMAT erases the whole stick into one writable FAT32 partition called RAVVING. EJECT and FORMAT both need a second press within three seconds.
MENU → BLUETOOTH lists your devices: the connected ones first, then the paired ones, then the ones in range. A paired device you aren't connected to reads "paired · not connected".

Switch Bluetooth on. Tap SCAN. It's a short scan for speakers, headphones, phones and computers. Tap the device to open its row, then tap PAIR. Confirm the passkey, or type the PIN, when ravving asks at the top. SCAN doesn't start on its own while a speaker plays, because a scan makes a Bluetooth sound stutter on the device's shared radio. VISIBLE lets a phone find the device for three minutes, so it can send you a file.

h: What a device's row offers › CONNECT / DISCONNECT
t: CONNECT / DISCONNECT. SEND… sends an exported track or bundle; the progress runs along the bottom. PLAY THROUGH sends the whole studio's sound to a speaker or headphones. DEVICE OUTPUT brings it back. The same choice is in the drawer's AUDIO OUTPUT card, with the jacks and HDMI. SBC-XQ picks the sound quality for this device: on for SBC-XQ, finer sound with more data; off for plain SBC, sturdier on a weak link. Devices you haven't set follow SETTINGS. If a speaker sounds crunchy on SBC-XQ, switch it off for that speaker. FORGET unpairs it. Files a phone sends you land in the library's incoming/ folder. A bundle shows up in PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT, and a track in the music player under "Received".

A speaker that's asleep, waking up or busy with a phone gets called again three more times over about 35 seconds. Its row reads "waking…" meanwhile, and DISCONNECT stops trying. If it still doesn't answer, ravving says NOT ANSWERING: FREE IT FROM A PHONE, OR TURN IT OFF AND ON. Speaker dozing off? ravving calls it three more times before giving up.

h: One audio device at a time
t: Only one speaker or pair of headphones plays at a time. Connecting a second one while another plays hands the sound over to it, and the first one disconnects. When Bluetooth comes on, ravving reconnects the output you picked last, once, if nothing else is playing. If a Bluetooth output goes silent while music is sent to it, ravving routes the sound to it again by itself. If that doesn't bring the sound back, the issues center tells you. Zynthbox, as it ships on MIKO, needs a little setup for Bluetooth, and ravving's setup takes care of it.

MENU → MUSIC PLAYER is a full-screen player for your exported tracks and your ● recordings. DASHBOARD takes you back. On the left: TRACKS, ALBUMS and ARTISTS. On the right: the cover, the transport, the position and the volume, over the QUEUE. Key What it does 1, 2, 3 Switch the views ▲ ▼ Pick a track SELECT Play it PLAY Pause STOP Stop Big knob Volume Knob 1 Position in the track BACK Leave Opening the player stops the beat, and leaving it stops the player.

MENU → AUDIO OUTPUT picks where the studio's sound goes: the device's jacks, the default; HDMI; any Bluetooth speaker or headphones connected in the BLUETOOTH dialog. The sound comes out of one place only, without glitches. The list updates while the dialog is open, as things are plugged in. The music player follows the output you pick too.

When the output goes away, for example headphones turned off, the sound falls back to the jacks. It switches back to your output as soon as it's there again, after a restart or a reconnection. For a Bluetooth output, ravving keeps its address so Bluetooth can reconnect it when it comes on. Picking the jacks forgets your choice.

The drawer's OUTPUT slider (knob 2) sets the level: the amplifier's on the jacks, or the output's own level otherwise. The drawer's BRIGHTNESS slider (knob 1) sets the screen's brightness. A black screen is often just this one turned all the way down. SBC-XQ: each paired speaker or pair of headphones has its own SBC-XQ chip in the BLUETOOTH dialog. Off plays it on plain SBC, which is sturdier on a weak link. Devices without their own choice follow SETTINGS. If an output goes silent while music is sent to it for six seconds, ravving routes the sound again once. If it's still silent, the issues center tells you.
MENU → RECORDER is a full-screen page for recording what you play into the input, as you play it. The beat keeps going, so you can record a take over it.

The input: a tab for MIC, GUITAR or LINE. MONITOR and its LEVEL, so you hear yourself. GAIN, with a meter, and lights for the jacks. ● REC, beside a graph of the incoming level. KEEP TAKES IN decides where takes go: SAMPLES ( samples/recordings ), where the samplers' browsers find them; TRACKS (the library's recordings ), where the music player finds them. A take is kept exactly as it came in: no compression, no trimming, no SMART stop.
The EFFECTS row has effects made for the input. On GUITAR you get amps and pedals: AMP, OVERDRIVE, FUZZ, TUBE, WAH and HOT AMP.
On the right are the RECORDINGS from both places, newest first. Each one has:

▶ PLAY. TRIM and NORMALISE, which make a new recording beside it. TO SAMPLE KING / TO PADS, into a slot or a pad. CHOP…, onto SAMPLE KING's bank or the pads, through the wave editor. TO TRACKS / TO SAMPLES, RENAME and DELETE (twice).

On GUITAR the page has a TUNER. It listens to the input before the effects and shows the note and how many cents off it is, on a ±50 scale. The tuning's strings are buttons. AUTO goes through the strings from the lowest. Hold a string within 3 cents for 0.8 s and it's ticked ✓, then the next one comes up, until ALL STRINGS IN TUNE. MANUAL stays on the string you tap. TUNING picks a tuning, and A4 sets the reference pitch (430–450 Hz). Instrument Tunings Guitar standard, half and full step down, drop D and C, DADGAD, open D, G, E and C Bass 4 and 5 strings, drop D Ukulele GCEA, baritone The tuner only runs while it's on screen.

The ISSUES card in the menu, beside MUSIC PLAYER, SETTINGS and the USB card, tells you what's wrong on the device right now, in plain words, with what to do about it. ALL GOOD when nothing is wrong. Otherwise, the number of issues, lit in the colour of the worst one. Tap it for the full list, worst first. Each issue has its details, a suggestion, and a button where one helps, like RESTART RAVVING. New errors and warnings also pop up as a message. What it watches: the sound engine missing, or an engine that couldn't start; audio connections that never appeared, and audio dropouts; the device's keys stopping responding; the music player unable to play; Bluetooth unavailable, or an output that plays no sound; an export that failed, a USB stick that wouldn't mount, storage nearly full. Under the list are the last warnings ravving printed.

ravving keeps to its own folders: it reads the device's sample library and writes only to these places: Root On the device What config ~/.config/ravving settings (the input set-up, the UI's choices) state ~/.local/state/ravving the live session ( session.json , the sequence); removed by a purge cache ~/.cache/ravving rebuildable: reversed samples, raw takes, the LV2 port cache library /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving the user's work, kept across reinstalls: projects/ , presets/ , samples/ (takes in samples/takes/ , the RECORDER's in samples/recordings/ , imported bundles' samples in samples/imported/ ), recordings/ (the master's and the RECORDER's TRACKS), exports/ On a desktop the library is ~/.local/share/ravving .

Twenty-two packs of pattern presets, ready to load from a USB stick. They don't come installed with ravving. Each one is written in a style, often after the bands and records that define it. Group Packs Genres Classical, Hip-Hop, Pop, Rock, Trap, Reggaeton, Punk, Tropical, Cumbia, Folk, Heavy Metal, Black Metal, Post-Punk Moods and eras Gregorian (old gothic), Vuelo (nu-disco after Flight Facilities), Hollywood (Lana Del Rey's beats under old-Hollywood strings) Soul R&B (after Jorja Smith and Snoh Aalegra), Droon (after Sonder) Solos Solos (ballads after Coltrane's Ballads and Chet Baker), Bebop (fast horn lines after Parker, Coltrane and Baker) Others Jazz, and Piig, a smaller style pack Most packs have five presets each for the drums, the bass, the lead and the chords. Solos and Bebop have six, and Piig has three.

Copy the pack's ravving folder to the root of a USB stick. Plug the stick into your MIKO. Open a preset dialog and pick SOURCE · USB . The presets play straight from the stick. The USB page can also import them, so they stay on the device.

The notes are written as scale degrees, so a pack plays in whatever key and scale you set. Each pack sticks to one scale, so its four instruments play together: Natural Minor: Hip-Hop, Trap, Reggaeton, Piig, Heavy Metal, Black Metal, Post-Punk, Vuelo, R&B, Droon, Hollywood. Major: Classical, Pop, Rock, Punk, Tropical, Cumbia, Folk, Solos, Bebop. Dorian: Gregorian. Tropical's minor styles (salsa, bachata) and Cumbia's (villera, chicha) sit on degree 6, the relative minor. That keeps each pack in one key: in C major, they play in A minor. Notes from outside the scale use ALTER, like rock's ♭3 and ♭7 or trap's ♭2. Chords from outside the key use chromatic voicings.

A pattern doesn't store its tempo or swing. The tables give each preset's tempo in quarter-note BPM on the 16-step grid. Every preset plays straight (SWING 50), except these: Preset SWING Hip-Hop · Golden Era Swing 58–62 Hip-Hop · Boom Bap, Lo-Fi Lazy and their bass, lead and chords 54–60 if you like; straight works Hip-Hop · Jazz Rap, Jazz Rap Walk 60–66 Rock · Half-Time Shuffle about 66, the triplet shuffle Piig · every preset 56–60, the lazy MPC swing Solos · every preset 54–58 on the EIGHTHS, a ballad's lilt; straight works Bebop · every preset 58–64 on the EIGHTHS; Trane Countdown and Trane Drive straight to 54 R&B · every preset 54–58 on the sixteenths, the lazy pocket Droon · every preset 56–60 on the sixteenths; the Care set 60–64 on the EIGHTHS Hollywood · every preset 52, a hair of lazy swing under the strings; straight works Set the same swing on every machine that plays along.

Each pack comes with a template, and some with two. A template starts a new project at the tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX its presets sound best with. Find them under TEMPLATES in the projects dialog. The tempo is the middle of the pack's tempos. The key is the one the pack was written for, or a usual key for the style. Notes can carry their own velocity and nudge, like SELECT's knobs 2 and 3 set them. The packs use that for feel: palm-muted chugs and tremolo strokes, a fiddle's bow and a chant's swell, grace notes snapped in early, a dub bass sitting behind the beat.

Some presets are in 3/4 or 6/8, like Classical's waltz trio (Waltz, Waltz Oom and Waltz Pah-Pah). Three 16-step bars hold four 12-step bars, so they loop together. The tempo counts a quarter as four steps, so a jig at a dotted quarter of 110 reads 165.

Each pack is built by a script, and a checker tests every pack against ravving's own readers. data/secret/<genre>-presets/build.py the generator (python3 build.py) data/secret/<genre>-presets/ravving/presets/<drums|bass|lead|chords>/patterns/<Genre> · <Name>.json data/secret/patternkit.py shared by the genre build.py files (not the jazz one) data/secret/validate.py checks every pack against ravving's parsers Each preset file is {"ravving": "preset", "type": "pattern", "library": "<x>-presets.json", "preset": {"name", "genre", "chart", "sound"}} . chart : the pattern, in the shipped libraries' format. sound : the sound it was written for. That's {"soundSource": …} for the bass, lead and chords, and {"kit": …} for the drums. Velocity and nudge: patternkit writes them from a note's @64 and <10 / >10 tokens (10 % of a step early or late). They land in the chart's VELOCITY and NUDGE lanes. Length: a note's _ steps, in the chart's HOLD lane. Templates: pack.template(…) writes ravving/presets/templates/<genre>.json , and a second one under its own name= . The stick's presets reach the dialog through PresetExchange::stickPatterns and loadStickPattern .

Every preset says which sound it was written for, and loads it when WITH ITS SOUND is on. All of them are already on your MIKO: nothing needs installing. Drums: the drum machine kits, plus acoustic kits picked from a General MIDI soundfont. Some, like the orchestra, cumbia and Latin kits, map their rows to other instruments: the orchestra kit's TOM and HAT are timpani, and the Latin kits swap in congas, bongos, güiro and cowbell. Bass, lead and chords: soundfont instruments, and "808 · Monosynth", a sub bass on Calf Monosynth that glides between notes. Drum kits don't follow the key, so the orchestra kit's timpani sound best in C. Soundfont sounds don't glide: a SLIDE only overlaps the notes. That's why the 808 lines use "808 · Monosynth".

h: Piig: Natural Minor, with the Dorian IV and the harmonic V
t: After the candle-lit lo-fi hip-hop and neo-soul of Biig Piig's early EPs: Big Fan of the Sesh , A World Without Snooze and No Place for Patience . Lazy 2- and 4-bar loops. Muted drums: rim, shaker, brushes and soft kicks. A round, legato bass. Rhodes and jazz-guitar 7th and 9th chords, with saxes in the background. Play it in D minor at 79 BPM , with SWING 56–60. That's the key and tempo of 24K (songbpm.com). Chord sites that say 150 count it in double time. Three families, one preset of each instrument in each. A family's four presets share their chord changes, so they play together; the 2-bar drums loop under the 4-bar parts. Made for D Dorian (SCALE Dorian, ROOT D), the chant's first mode. The Dies Irae: 13th century, in the public domain. It's the three phrases of the mfiles.co.uk MIDI: F E F D E C D D | F F G F E D C E | F E D A C D D. Organum Above (lead) and Organum Below (bass) sing it a perfect fifth above and a perfect fourth below, note for note. That's organum's parallel fifths and fourths, after the Musica enchiriadis . Any two of the three loop together. Dead Can Dance: In Power We Entrust the Love Advocated's i v VII IV (Am Em G D). Also: a saltarello in 6/8, the drone under the chant, and a 90s-style breakbeat under it. The chant's notes swell towards the middle of each phrase, and lean a hair early or late. h: Solos: Major (ballads after Coltrane's Ballads and Chet Baker)
t: Made for Eb major , a tenor's ballad key. The minor moods sit on degree 6 (C minor), and Devotion vamps on degree 2 (F Dorian). The lead's degree 1 is Eb4, so each horn has its own range: Horn Range Tenor "5-" to "1+", crying up to "2+" Soprano "5" to "3+" Trumpet "7-" to "6" Six original ballad solos for the LEAD, each with the brushes, bass and chords it's heard over. They're moody, long-breathed and passionate, with no fast passages. The model is the John Coltrane Quartet's Ballads (Impulse!, 1962–63, with Tyner, Garrison and Jones), plus Chet Baker's slow trumpet. Nothing is quoted: the album's standards and the recorded solos are copyrighted. Every line, progression and rhythm is new.

Tempo 56–70. Long held notes, 6–12 steps, with a beat or half a bar of air between phrases. A swell written across each phrase in velocities: @60 rising to @100–110 and falling back. The MODS soften each note's attack (ATTACK +2400 timecents on the sax, +3600 on the trumpet) and lengthen the release. Every long note sits 8–16 % of a step late, the rubato lean. Flurries only as ornaments: three or four sixteenths pushed early and climbing into a long note. A scoop or slur (~) into a long tone.

Chords: Tyner-style rootless 9ths and 13ths, So What fourths, fourths planed over a pedal, Lydian clusters, the minor iv (Abm6) and the backdoor Db9. Each is held a bar or half a bar, then re-voiced. h: Bebop: Major (horn solos after Parker, Coltrane and Baker)
t: Fast horn solos and their comping, in their own group ( Bebop · … ). Made for Bb major , the horn key. The lead's degree 1 is Bb4, so each horn has its range: Horn Range Alto "1-" to "7" Tenor "5-" to "4" Soprano "1" to "4+" Trumpet "6-" to "7" Six original solos for the LEAD, each with the chords, bass and drums it's heard over. Nothing is quoted: the players' recorded solos and tunes are copyrighted. Every line, progression and rhythm is new.

SWING works on the EIGHTHS here, and the templates set it. The ride's "ding ding-a" and the bebop eighths sit two steps apart on the 16-step grid. Parker: lines in eighths on the chord tones, with chromatic approach notes and enclosures. The off-beats are a touch louder, the approach notes snap in early, and the blue ♭3 scoops into the 3. A motif is stated, then displaced a beat, with a breath between phrases. Coltrane: sheets of sound, sixteenth 1-2-3-5 cells up and their mirror down on every chord, each run swelling to its top. The modal solo, on soprano, is pentatonic cells and stacked fourths up to the Eb6, with a high note cried four times. Baker: few notes, long and soft, every one behind the beat, with a scoop and room to breathe. The trumpet's cutoff is down a little and its release longer. h: R&B: Natural Minor (after Jorja Smith and Snoh Aalegra)
t: Made for E minor , the key of Be Honest, Teenage Fantasy and Fool For You on their chord sheets (Ultimate Guitar). The template sits at 86 BPM with a lazy 16th swing, the middle of the songs' 84–94. R&B · Slow Jam is Fool For You's 75.

Drums lay back by where the hits sit, and by the swing. A drum chart has no per-hit velocity or nudge, so the backbeats are its accented steps and the ghost notes its plain hits. A kick lands on the "a" of two, and a ghost a 16th after the snare drags it. Bass and lead sit 6–14 % of a step late, and grace notes snap in early. The vocal lines run pentatonic melismas into long notes, scoop, and swell. The MODS: dark kits (TONE), a longer 808 tail, soft-attack strings and voices, Rhodes and pad releases, and chorus on the Rhodes. h: Hollywood: Natural Minor (Lana Del Rey under old-Hollywood strings)
t: Made for F minor , the key of Blue Jeans and Honeymoon. The contrabass's and cello's low F and C sit under the strings, and the orchestra kit's timpani reach F. Lana Del Rey's beats and progressions, from Born to Die to Norman Fucking Rockwell! , with an old-Hollywood orchestra: violins, cellos, string sections, harp, celesta and timpani. Vintage, cinematic and melancholic.

Her progressions come from the chord sheets, set on the scale's degrees: Video Games' i III v VI (F#m A C#m D). Born to Die's VI i VII VI (C Em D C). Blue Jeans' i VII IV (Fm Eb Bb, the major IV a chromatic chord here). Summertime Sadness' VI i VII iv (A C#m B F#m). Honeymoon's i VI iv6 V7, in three. Venice Bitch's minor plagal C C7 F Fm6, in the relative major (III III7 VI vi6). The old-Hollywood scoring adds the minor line cliché (Fm, Fm(maj7), Fm7, Fm6, the Bond theme's "suspense motif") with the lament bass walking down under it, the half-step sigh, tremolo strings swelling, and harp sweeps. Nothing is quoted: her songs are copyrighted, so the style was studied ( tools/genre-research/hollywood.md ) and every line, melody and rhythm is new.

Slow: 56–88, the half-time beats written at their felt tempo. Velocity swells across each bowed phrase, and long holds. The strings and the cellos 6–10 % of a step late. A written tremolo: sixteenths of one note swelling from @40 to @104 and back. Harp sweeps rising in velocity to a held top note. The celesta's grace notes snapped in early (<12), and slides on the 808 sub. The MODS shape the sound: the strings' ATTACK slowed (2400–4800) and their RELEASE lengthened, for the hall; the FILTER pulled down, for the vintage tone; a little VIBRATO on the solo strings; the drum kits darkened (TONE), and the SP1200 tuned down two semitones.
