When it needs something zynthbox-qml does in Python, that piece is ported to C++ under src/ , and the class doc names the Python it came from.

h: Input flow: the Hardware attached property
t: The device's keys and knobs reach QML the way the keyboard does through Keys : as events delivered to the item with active focus , bubbling to its parents until a handler accepts them. device button ─► HardwareSwitches (zyncoder poll, 20 ms) └► MidiRouter.enqueueCuiaCommand("SWITCH_STEP3_RELEASED") MIDI-mapped CUIA ─► MidiRouter ─► cuiaEvent ─► ZynthboxBridge ─► Ravving::handleCuia ─┐ device knob ─► HardwareKnobs (zynpot poll) ─► Ravving::handleKnobTurn / handleKnobMove ─┤ keyboard (dev) ─► Main.qml Shortcuts ─► ravving.simulateCuia / simulateKnob ────────────┤ ▼ HardwareEvent ─► Hardware::dispatch(window): activeFocusItem, then each parent, until one accepts it import Ravving FocusScope { Hardware.onKnob1Up: event => level += event.delta // knob 1 clockwise Hardware.onBigKnobDown: event => select(index - 1) Hardware.onKnob2Moved: event => cutoff = event.value // Z2_V5B fixed pot, 0..1 Hardware.onStepPressed: event => grid.toggle(event.index) Hardware.onUpPressed: event => { if (atTop) event.accepted = false } // bubble on } Signals: knob1Up/Down … knob3Up/Down , bigKnobUp/Down , knob1Moved … knob3Moved , generic knobTurned / knobMoved , up/down/left/right/select/back/menu/play/stop/record/metronome Pressed , stepPressed (index 0–15), numberPressed (index 0–4), and pressed for anything else. As with Keys , the specific signal goes first and the generic one gets whatever is still not accepted. A handler that runs accepts the event unless it sets event.accepted = false .

The open page (a RavePage , i.e. a FocusScope) has the focus. ▲ at a page's top edge is left unaccepted, bubbles to Main.qml , and focuses the header's first group. In the header, ◀ ▶ move between the KnobGroup s, and ▼ / BACK return to the page. Step keys always go to the page. A number key nobody handles still switches the page (C++ fallback). ▲ ▼ walk one vertical order per machine, owned by MachineModule : header → strip → SOUND MODIFIERS cards (only while open) → the editor → SOUND EFFECTS cards (only while open). The sections move the focus themselves ( ParamCardRow.released(dy) ), coming back to the card last used with enter() . A page calls focusUp() / focusDown() when its editor has no further to go: the drums past the top row or the ACC row, the bass roll past its top or bottom note row. focusUp() returns false from the strip, so ▲ bubbles to the header. ▼ from the header lands on the page's focusTop() , the strip.

A KnobGroup (FocusScope) hands its targets to the knobs: knob n → targets[n], and the big knob → targets[3], or fine steps on targets[0]. It can also hold navItems , which its navKnob steps through and SELECT activates. The navKnob is the big knob by default, and knob 1 for INSTRUMENTS. Targets show a KnobBadge : a tiny knob icon with the knob number and a value arc, pulsing while a Z2_V5B pot waits for pick-up. Inside a page, the big knob is always the volume of the machine on screen ( RavePage.module , MachineModule.nudgeLevel() ), and the fader wears the big-knob badge. Groups in a page ( ParamCard , the machine strip) set ownsBigKnob: false , so it passes through to the page. Popups and the header, outside the page, keep using it. A machine's strip (role, PAN knob, VOL RaveFader ) is a KnobGroup . Tap it, and knob 1 pans and knob 2 sets the level. BACK or a tap in the grid give the knobs back to the rows ( StepGrid.knobsActive is off while the strip has them).

RECORD on an instrument page records that machine's take: the strip's ● shows ●, the count-in beat, …, then ■. RECORD with the header focused, or ALT + RECORD anywhere, is the global recording: the header's ●, and a red RECORD LED. The metronome is libzynthbox's (SyncTimer audibleMetronome ), with zynthbox-qml's tick/tock wavs. ZynthboxBridge::setMetronomeSounds() builds the two ClipAudioSources through the exported constructor, since no meta-object factory exists. SamplerSynth's global-sketch1 outputs are wired to the master.

It plays the machine on screen, on every page, through the same path as the step keys, so REC records it. LIVE, which may be left on another machine, is the step keys' only. GM drum notes 35–59 map by role ( DrumKit::roleForGmNote ). Any other note cycles through the rows from C2. A velocity of 100 or more is an accent. Plugging one in or out shows a Toast : a dark pill, bottom centre. Debug: QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.midi.debug=true" .

Main.qml 's ledColors : Key Light ▲ ▼ SELECT BACK ALT MENU always a soft white ( navigationLight ); ALT white while held, MENU while the menu is open ◀ ▶ lit while they switch something on the open page ( RavePage.sideKeysLit ): the CHORDS views with the editor focused, the drum machines, the sampler banks PLAY dim green when stopped, bright while playing STOP dim when stopped, lit while playing RECORD dim red when ready, red while recording (global, or a sampler take), a machine's colour during its take

ALT is a modifier held in C++ ( Ravving.altHeld ). ALT + big knob is the master volume, wherever the focus is ( masterTurned , never dispatched), badged on the MASTER dial. ALT + knobs 1–3 go straight to Ravving.altKnobTarget , the header's FX SENDS (PHASER, ECHO, HEAVY): a KnobGroup borrowed while ALT is held, with its badges, frame and pick-up. ALT + ◀ / ▶ undo and redo along the project's history ( studio.history ), like the header's ↶ ↷. ALT + ▲ gives the focus to the app header at once, from wherever it is (a page's rows, a section's cards, the strip): Ravving.headerRequested , raised in C++ before any dispatch. ALT + 1 opens the SONG page from anywhere, and again goes back to the page ( Ravving.songRequested , raised in C++ before any dispatch, its press swallowed too).

MODE switches LIVE on the open page's instrument, from anywhere. The MODE LED shows it. ✱ ( starPressed ) opens and closes the MIXER (below). MENU opens the control center ( ControlCenter , in the drawer): MIXER, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, MIDI and SYSTEM cards, the power row, and OUTPUT and BRIGHTNESS sliders on knobs 2 and 1. ◀ ▶ walk the actions, and SELECT runs one. REBOOT and POWER OFF need a second press within 3 s. The header's INSTRUMENTS chips light the machine on screen only. None lights while the MIXER, the SONG page, the music player or the RECORDER covers the pages ( Session.pageCovered ).

MixerPage is the StackLayout's sixth view ( Main.mixerOpen ). A number key leaves it for that page. In it: ◀ ▶ or step keys 1–9 pick a strip; knob 1 is its level, knob 2 its pan, and the big knob the fine level; SELECT mutes, and ALT + SELECT solos; BACK or ✱ go back; the step LEDs show the strips: muted dim, picked white.

AUTO: the header's AUTO arms recording ( Studio.recordAutomation ). While playing, a SOUND MODIFIERS or SOUND EFFECTS knob turned is written into its machine's pattern at the step playing. These are Machine automation lanes, step → value: undoable, and saved. The toolbar's AUTO plays them back. It's lit, with "•" while there are some, and a long press clears them. SOUND EFFECTS cards, open: SELECT switches the focused card's effect on or off. BACK closes the section, and the focus goes back to the editor above ( ParamCardRow.selectAndBack ). Closed: ▼ past the editor lands on the bar ( FxChain.focusBar() ). ◀ ▶ ring the chips, SELECT switches the ringed effect, ▼ opens the section on its card, and ▲ / BACK go back up. By touch: a tap on the ▸ SOUND EFFECTS heading opens it on the effect last touched. The heading is the one way in by touch; the bar has no OPEN button.

Dialogs ( RavePopup : ChoicePopup, InputPopup), drop-down lists and the menu darken the page behind them ( ModalDim ). A dialog takes the keys while open, and gives the focus back. Dialogs wear one card look: a gradient #1e1c24 → #131118, a hairline border, radius 16, and a DialogHeader with a spaced title, a hint and the ✕. The menu drawer is a settings panel: a gradient #211f28 → #16141c, hairline-split sections under small captions, and flat wells that light yellow (#f0c832).

h: Pausing, LIVE and the bar loop
t: ❚❚ pauses a machine's written pattern ( DrumMachine.paused → Sketchpad.setTrackPaused ). Its clip stops in PlayfieldManager and is left out of the launch at play; resuming rejoins on the next bar. It stays playable live. LIVE (one machine at a time, Session.liveMachine ) turns the step keys into pads: Hardware.onStepDown on the press, and onStepPressed on the release. On the drums, keys 1–8 play the rows, and key 9 held makes accents. With REC on while playing, a hit is written at the nearest step ( Machine::recordLive , timed against the measured step length). In STEP entry while stopped, it's written at the cursor ( writeAtCursor ). The LEDs show the pads (rows in the machine's colour, key 9 red, white while held) and drop the playhead ( RavePage.stepKeysArePads ). libzynthbox's own live recorder isn't used: it only hears controller ports, and pads sent through SyncTimer arrive as sequencer traffic.

Q off ( Machine.quantise ): a hit keeps its distance from its step as the subnote's delay , in SyncTimer ticks (negative when early), so it plays back as played. The machine keeps these offsets itself ( timing in its state), and puts them back whenever its model rewrites the pattern ( syncTiming ). ⟲ ( Machine.loopBar ) plays only the bar on screen. The pattern's playback window moves to it ( bankOffset = that bar, patternLength = one bar), while bars keeps the real length. Paging with ‹ › moves the loop. It isn't saved; attach and restore put the window back.

libzynthbox doesn't install headers, and its headers pull in all of JUCE. So ZynthboxBridge : dlopen s libzyncoder.so and calls init_zynlib() . libzynthbox needs zyncoder's MIDI router first, the same order as zynthbox-qml. dlopen s libzynthbox.so and resolves three symbols: Plugin::instance() , Plugin::initialize() and Plugin::registerTypes() . Gets the MidiRouter QML singleton and connects to cuiaEvent through the meta-object system. Both libraries are opened with RTLD_LOCAL . RTLD_GLOBAL lets libzynthbox's bundled JUCE/tracktion symbols interpose on libraries loaded later, and the app crashes in Kirigami's platform-plugin lookup.
See building.md , testing.md and debugging.md (tools/: deploy, keys, screenshots, MIDI, measuring, logging) and extending.md (new machines, engines, controls, effects).

ravving ships as a Store AppImage that bundles ravving, the data and ravving-setup ( setup/ ), the page the AppImage opens over zynthbox-qml to install ravving and pick the UI the device runs; both lean on tools/default-app.sh . See packaging.md .

ravving wears one theme, set in code. RAVVING_THEME in the top-level CMakeLists.txt names the folder under data/plasma/desktoptheme/ that ships with the app: ravving-theme , the Miko theme. The app makes its bundled config/plasmarc its only plasmarc. Neither zynthbox-qml's theme chooser ( ~/.config/plasmarc ) nor any user file can change it. The journal line ravving: theme … says what a run wears. To change the look, change the theme folder or RAVVING_THEME , and rebuild.

Nothing of ravving's goes into zynthbox-qml's folders, and nothing of zynthbox-qml's is written: ravving reads the device's sample library and writes only to its own places ( src/backend/paths.h ), following the XDG base directories: Root On the device What config ~/.config/ravving settings (the input set-up, the UI's choices) state ~/.local/state/ravving the live session ( session.json , the sequence); removed by a purge cache ~/.cache/ravving rebuildable: reversed samples, raw takes, the LV2 port cache library /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving the user's work, kept across reinstalls: projects/ , presets/ , samples/ (takes in samples/takes/ , the RECORDER's in samples/recordings/ , imported bundles' samples in samples/imported/ ), recordings/ (the master's and the RECORDER's TRACKS), exports/ On a desktop the library is ~/.local/share/ravving . Files of an older layout are moved into this one at start ( Paths::initialise() ), and the session's and projects' sample paths with them.

StartupSplash (qml/Splash.qml and SplashLook.qml) shows the logo from the moment libzynthbox is up until the page is ready, then plays a short show into the page. MENU → SETTINGS → STARTUP picks the look, from the next start: ANIME, GLOW, STILL, ZOOM, ARU or OFF. While the studio loads , the splash is a still picture. A moving one keeps the screen redrawn every frame and slows the start. The show plays in the page's own window, since kwin keeps a full-screen window above a "stay on top" one. The logos are the effect SVGs drawn without their backgrounds (data/branding/make-splash.sh). ARU's frames, the pixel octopus and the wolf pup, are drawn by data/branding/make-aru.py from data/branding/aru/. The album art's wordmark is data/branding/ravving-wordmark.svg.

h: The phone share and the help page
t: FileShare ( share ) is ravving's one-file HTTP server, on port 8098 or the next free one. It serves three things: SEND… → PHONE · QR CODE offers one file, at a path of 128 random bits, for as long as the dialog is open: 15 minutes at most. FILES → PHONE · BROWSE serves the library as pages ( FileShare.openBrowse ), at a random path that lives until 15 minutes pass with no request. The webpage ( site/ , installed as share/ravving/site ), at http://<device>:8098/help/ . SETTINGS → HELP shows it as a QR code ( get share helpUrl ). Over the fifo: call share offer /path/file , get share url , get share status , get share browseUrl , call share stop . tools/share-test.sh checks it from the laptop ( testing.md ).

Backend classes : every class of src/backend/ . QML components : the shared base types, the pages and their parts. The undo history : what is undone, steps, the History API, making a feature undoable. Bluetooth : devices, pairing, files and audio output. Live recordings : video and audio recording, the voice over, the computer link.

Every class of the backend library ( src/backend/ ), what it does and how the others use it. Each class has its full reference in the API reference. The drums play through libzynthbox's sketchpad tracks, patterns and synth slots, with ravving's C++ objects in the places where libzynthbox calls back into its host: Class Role Stands in for / ports Studio backend root ( studio in QML): builds the machines from data/kits.json , transport (play/stop, tempo, swing, step), saves the sequence after edits; a preview clock on a desktop; the sampler's browser ( sampleFiles() : kits.json sampleFolders , folders labelled short) and hold-to-hear previews ( previewSample() / stopPreview() : a one-shot clip on SamplerSynth's global lane) sketchpad song + transport glue Machine the base of every machine: track (level, pan, effects, mute, ❚❚, kick cuts), pattern (bars, view bar following the playing bar while playing: follow , off when a bar is picked mid-play, back on when stopped; playhead, STEP cursor), presets, LIVE play/record, UNDO / REDO of the pattern ( canUndo , undo() , canRedo , redo() : every edited whose content differs is a step back, 50 deep, changes within 0.5 s of the last joining its step (a knob turned, a handle dragged); the mix, sound and effects are left out, and so are a subclass's viewKeys() such as the sampler's bank; beginEditGroup() / endEditGroup() make a take one step; a project open starts it afresh); subclasses give steps, sound and velocities; SECTIONS: sectionContent() (the pattern part less soundState() 's keys and the viewKeys() , plus ❚❚ and ONCE) and applySectionContent() (laid over the machine's own by withSection() , the history started over; an empty map empties the pattern), sectionBars() / sectionSounds() ; the samplers keep their banks' hits, not their samples ( SamplerBanks ) Its own length ( bars , m_bars ) is kept apart from what its clip plays: applyPlayLength() is the one place that sets the clip's patternLength and bankOffset , from playedBars() : one bar under ⟲ (the bar on screen), the section's span under ONCE ( once , setSpan() from the studio; the bars past its own emptied by clearRest() ), else its own; while it rests the playhead hides and a live hit is not written. new MonoMachine a mono line (one note per step) with ACCENT and SLIDE (the note lasts 1.5 steps and a legato engine glides into the next): page 3's AC 303 ( bass , DISTRHO Nekobi: accent velocity 127 vs 80, Nekobi accents above 90) and page 4's THERE LEAD ( lead , Calf Monosynth, legato + portamento); base note and velocities from kits.json; presets in scale degrees ( bass-presets.json , lead-presets.json ), RANDOM, octave; follows the header's key: a ROOT or SCALE change snaps every note to the nearest note of the new key (upwards on a tie), and the line's key is saved with it new ChordMachine page 2's POLY-6 on TAL NoiseMaker (6 voices, Juno chorus); a custom voicing is scale degrees, or chromatic (semitones from the chord base, chart letter c ) when a note is outside the key, so a chart can carry a C7 in E♭ major; setStepNotes(step, "48,52,55,58") for scripts; live keys below 1000 are chord degrees, from 1000 on single scale degrees ( noteKey , noteKeyForNote , noteOfKey : the NOTES tab's LIVE, written one note into the step's voicing by a take or STEP entry): each step holds a voicing, a diatonic chord (a degree stacked in thirds from the scale, triad or seventh per degree by the chord set: Classic, Triads, Sevenths) or a custom set of scale degrees (built in NOTES); a run of one voicing is one held chord; everything is in scale degrees, so a key, set or octave change revoices it all. Three views: CHORDS ( setChord ), NOTES ( noteSets , toggleNote ), SLOTS (four chordSlots of 1/2/4/8 bars, armedSlot , assignSlot , cycleSlotBars , clearSlot : editing one rebuilds the steps in order). LIVE keys and the chord keys play whole chords, a keyboard note plays its degree's chord; presets chord-presets.json ("1111666633337777", "x" + VOICINGS for custom) new SoundPresets an LV2 plugin's factory presets read from its bundle's presets.ttl (name, category from TAL's prefix, port values); a machine's kits.json soundPresets {file, keep} gives it soundPresets / soundPreset / loadSoundPreset() : the ports are set (but keep ), the SOUND MODIFIERS take the values ( adopt() ), the name is saved, and an engine restart sends the sound again before the knobs new SoundControls a machine's SOUND MODIFIERS driving its engine's own ports, built from the machine's sound in kits.json (owned by Machine ): cards of knobs, 0..1 mapped onto min..max linearly or with "curve": "log" ; a knob with choices is a switch (snaps to i / (n − 1), ParamCard draws it as a WaveCycler ) whose choices can each set several ports (TAL's JUNO wave: waveform + pulse width + levels). Bass: WAVE · FILTER (CUTOFF RESO ENV MOD) · VOICE (DECAY ACCENT TUNE); chords: FILTER (CUTOFF RESO LFO) · SHAPE (ATTACK LENGTH GLIDE) · TONE (WAVE SAW/JUNO/SQR/TRI, SPREAD, CHORUS OFF/I/II); lead: WAVE (SAW SQR SIN TRI) · FILTER (CUTOFF RESO ENV) · VOICE (GLIDE LENGTH). Machine::setExpression() plays kits.json expressions live (the ribbon's vibrato = Calf lfo2pitch ) new JalvPlugin , JalvEngine one LV2 plugin in jalv (effects, and instruments with MIDI in); JalvEngine makes an instrument a machine's SoundEngine (a mono output feeds both sides) zynthian_engine_jalv.py DrumMachine one drum machine: kit rows, steps as subnotes of its track's PatternModel, accents, presets, per-row level/mute/solo (as velocities), level (track gain), pan (track passthrough), mute, audition, kit switching and reset new TakeRecorder a machine's REC ( studio.take ): a fresh take of what is played LIVE, counted in by the transport's first bar (stopped) or punched in at the loop's restart (playing), overdubbing loop after loop; holds the metronome on for the take new MidiInput external controllers ( studio.midiIn ; devices : the connected ones' names): notes from MidiRouter's hardware port (raw controller notes parked on unused track 9; every device's channels reset to the current track; bridge duplicates dropped), plug-in/out notices zynthbox-qml's MIDI controller handling (subset) VideoRecorder LIVE REC ( video , "Live recordings" below): a video of the screen (x11grab) or a USB camera (v4l2) with the master's sound, or ( mode "audio") the sound alone as a 24-bit WAV among the exports (finished with tags through Exporter::finishRecording ), encoded by ffmpeg (libx264, two threads, nice 10; three quality tiers) into videos/<project> - <date>.mp4 ; the sound comes from AudioTap , the sync from the wall clock on both inputs ( -copyts , -itsoffset = the tap's first-sample moment), the file goes to Matroska first and is remuxed once to MP4 with its head cut to the first frame; states off / ready / countdown / starting / recording / saving, takesKey gives it RECORD and STOP while VIDEO is on ( Ravving::handleCuia ); VIDEO SAVED sends it on ( ComputerLink , a USB stick) new AudioTap ravving's JACK client ravving-video (stereo in): the master's last outputs copied on the audio thread into a 2^20-frame ring (21 s), drained by a plain thread into a named pipe ffmpeg reads as raw float; the first sample's CLOCK_REALTIME from jack_get_cycle_times ; frames the ring could not hold are counted, never lost quietly; the mic inputs mixed in, plain or as a voice over ( setVoiceOver(duckDb, liftDb) : a 120 Hz high-pass and a +4 dB shelf from 3 kHz on the mic, its envelope followed, the master ducked while it speaks, the sum through a peak limiter at −1 dBFS, never clipped) new FileBrowser the FILES browser ( files , FilesPopup ): the library by kind ({key, label, about, usbKind, count}; projects through Projects , presets and templates through PresetExchange , the rest by folder and suffix from filesuffixes.h , shared with UsbLibrary ), entries(kind) newest first, presetFile(id) to send a preset as one JSON file, remove(entry) through the owner (Projects, the preset library, the machine, Templates) or the file new Computers the user's computers over SSH ( computers , SETTINGS · COMPUTERS): any number of ComputerLinks, each in its own settings group computers/<id> (a single-computer set-up of an older version moved into c1 ), add(host, user, password) (the same user@host set up again, not added twice), send(id, files) , byId , current (the last added or set up), busy / phase , the links' sent / notify / setupFinished passed on with the id new ComputerLink one computer over SSH (a Computers entry): the device key ( ~/.config/ravving/ssh/id_ed25519 ) installed on the computer with ssh-copy-id and the password through SSH_ASKPASS (used once, never stored), ravving's own known_hosts , the Downloads folder asked with xdg-user-dir , send(files) by scp one at a time; statuses unset / setting-up / ready / unreachable / refused / failed new FileShare a file offered to a phone ( share , SEND… → PHONE · QR CODE): a one-file HTTP server on QTcpServer (GET / HEAD at /d/<128 random bits>/<name> , Content-Disposition attachment, Range → 206, 64 kB chunks as the socket drains, 404 for anything else, port 8098 or the next free one) bound on every interface, the URL on the Wi-Fi address; offer(path) → the URL, stop() , 15 minutes at most; statuses idle / waiting / sending / done, sent , downloads , downloaded(name) ; the QR code is drawn by QrCodeItem (src/, Nayuki's qrcodegen vendored in src/backend/thirdparty) in QrPopup.qml . The same server carries the ravving page: setHelpFolder(dir) (the installed site/ ) keeps it listening for good and serves GET /help/<file> from that folder (index.html for /help/ , no path above it, text types with a charset, pages no-cache and the rest cached 10 minutes), helpUrl = http://<address>:<port>/help/ , what HelpPopup.qml (SETTINGS → HELP) draws as a QR code; and the library for a phone ( openBrowse() → browseUrl , /b/<32 hex>/ , 15 minutes after the phone's last request, closeBrowse() ): the FileBrowser's kinds and entries as small self-styled pages ( respondBrowse ), a file served as an attachment from the path the browser lists, looked up by kind and name, never from the URL new MixRecorder the global recording ( studio.mix ): the master (GlobalPlayback) to recordings/ravving-<date>.wav through AudioLevels (refused while a sampler take records: AudioLevels runs one recording at a time); the music player lists these under "Recordings" new PadSamplerMachine page 5's PAD SAMPLER ( studio.machines.pads , kind "pads"): 4 banks × 16 pads, each loaded pad one ClipAudioSource set up from the pad's params[tab][knob] (TRIM start / end / loop point, MIX pan, AMP ENV attack and decay / release, TUNE semi + fine, PLAY mono / mute group as exclusivity groups) and flags (NOTE ON = NonLooping, LOOP = Looping from the loop point, REVERSE = a reversed copy, MUTE; 16 LEVELS kept); pads 1–10 on track 7, 11–16 on a second track (kits.json secondTrack 8) whose pattern the machine mirrors (hits, length, loop, swing, mute) and whose live notes go out on it, both tracks' sample outputs wired into track 7's lane ( JackWiring::setSampleOutputs(track, samples, laneTrack) ); level as velocity; FILTER = the clip's equaliser bands (one, two for the 4-pole types, cutoff and Q from the knobs); the kit's knobs ( PadKitControls , the SOUND MODIFIERS: KIT volume / semi / fine, 16 LEVELS type and switch); 16 LEVELS: the selected pad becomes the source, every pad plays it by velocity ramp or on sixteen level slices (notes 64–79, transposed by root note per TUNE semitones or the header's SCALE from pad 4), the hits meanwhile are the bank's level hits; audition = one pass; latch = the note held with the slice looping, unlatched after a short delay so the note-off is not ignored; PAD FX held on the pad played last ( heldFx , fxPad ): ECHO = the track's echo throw, TAPE STOP / SCRATCH = sweeps of the clip's speedRatio (a QVariantAnimation), STUTTER = a sixteenth-of-the-tempo retrigger, SKIP / REVERSE = the pad restarted with its start moved on / its reversed copy from the point reached, restored on release; erase pad, halve / double, UNMUTE ALL; presets pads-presets.json ("1"–"16"); playing and playPositions (per pad: whether its clip sounds and where it is in the file, from the clip's isPlaying / position signals) feed the grid's beam and the screen's playhead the MPC Sample SamplerMachine page 5's SAMPLE KING ( studio.machines.sampler , track 6, "sample-trig"): 4 banks × 8 slots, each slot one ClipAudioSource (made through the bridge's exported constructor) on its track's sample slot i % 5 , row i / 5 , set up on its root slice: key zone = root note = baseNote + i , one-shot (a retrigger chokes it), PITCH = slice pitch, trim = start/length samples, 8 ms release; REVERSE plays a reversed copy rendered once in a worker ( AudioFile::writeReversed , cached by path hash). Steps, accents and row mix as the drums (velocities); presets sampler-presets.json ("1"–"8": x/X). Break one and libzynthbox crashes or stays silent: SketchpadTrack.samples must hold ten entries (PatternModel reads sample slots 0–9). SamplerSynth makes a track's channel_N-sampleM ports only while a clip is registered on that slot: wire exactly the loaded ones, again whenever they change. AudioLevels starts every recorder set to record: a take turns the master's writer off ( setRecordGlobalPlayback(false) ), the mix turns the port recorder off. AudioLevels' own capture meter ( captureA/B ) reads the speakers under PipeWire (it takes the first system: outputs, the monitor): meter the input through the port recorder. PipeWire has a second "Built-in Audio Stereo" (the Dummy card): its ports get a number suffix ( capture_FL-17167 ); the plain names are the HiFiBerry's. PlayGridManager's zlSketchpad must be set before playing (SyncTimer dereferences it). A pattern only plays while PlayfieldManager has its clip in PlayingState, and stopping resets every clip: the clips are re-launched from Sketchpad::startPlayback() . Never call Plugin::shutdown() ; exit with _exit() (see the exit row below).

data/kits.json holds every machine: drumMachines : track, Zynthian channel, engine, default kit and preset. machines , by kind : mono (bass on track 3, lead on track 5) and chords (track 4). Each has its engine (type, LV2 URI, fixed controls ), its sound (SOUND MODIFIERS), a presets file, defaultPreset , baseNote and velocities. The kit folder: the 40 drum-machine soundfonts in zynthian-data. Studio builds the machines generically and publishes the non-drum ones as studio.machines.<key> . A new engine type is one SoundEngine subclass plus a line in SoundEngine::createEngine() .

Grid rows aren't written by hand: DrumKit reads them out of the kit, since the soundfonts aren't General MIDI (the 909's clap is on 50, the Linn's on 39). A tap on a machine's nameplate opens ChoicePopup with every kit. DrumMachine::loadKit() moves each hit to the new kit's note for its role, keeping accents. The engine reloads the soundfont ( SoundEngine::reconfigure ), and the session keeps the choice ( session.json ). A double tap on the nameplate goes back to the default kit ( resetKit() ).

Factory beats that replace the pattern: House, Techno, Electro, Breaks, Hip Hop, Groove and Empty. They're drum charts written per role ( "KICK": "X...x..." , X = an accented hit), so every preset plays on every kit. The toolbar's PRESET button shows the loaded preset (• once edited) and opens a ChoicePopup by genre. SAVE CURRENT AS NEW stores the pattern as "My Beat N" in Paths::presets()/drum-presets.json , and DELETE removes a user preset. The other machines save the same way into their own file, named by the factory file's userName : "My Bassline N", "My Progression N", "My Melody N", "My Pattern N".

Each row's level, mute and solo are kept per role, so they survive kit changes. They live in the hits' velocities: level 0.8 → velocity 100, and an accent hits ×1.27 harder; a muted or soloed-out row gets velocity −1, PatternModel's "do not play". The machine keeps the accents and saves them in the session with the row mix. They're never read back from velocities. The session lives in Paths::state() ( ~/.local/state/ravving ; an explicit path: libzynthbox's MidiRouter renames the application to "zynthbox-qml" while it initialises).

The pattern interface. StepGrid and PatternToolbar only draw and forward to a pattern object: rows, stepCount, steps, accents, playhead, bars, viewBar, presets, presetName, presetEdited, canSavePresets, rowLevels, rowMuted, rowSoloed, toggleStep(), toggleAccent(), clear(), loadPreset(), saveAsPreset(), removePreset(), setRowLevel(), setRowMuted(), setRowSoloed(), audition() . The studio's DrumMachine and SamplerMachine implement it; PatternState.qml implements it in memory for pages whose backend is still to come (the melodic toolbars).

The QML components in qml/ : the shared base types, the pages and their parts. They follow the UI rules . Studio machines are shown by MachinePanel : a MachineModule backed by a Machine. It keeps the level, pan, ❚❚, effects, sound, REC and takes, the STEP cursor, the LIVE pads and the keyboard bookkeeping. MachinePage is the page around any panel: it forwards the step keys, ▲ ▼, the header hand-off and an external keyboard to its panel . BassPage , LeadPage and ChordsPage only declare their panel.
The step grid. In LIVE, the pads are the rows and key 9 adds the accent.

A mono PianoRoll with pattern: machine . LIVE: all 16 step keys play the scale up from the root, and ▲ ▼ shift the octave. STEP on: ▲ ▼ walk the rows, each one heard ( previewSelection ), and SELECT writes the row ( writeSelection / selectionKey , shared in MachinePanel ). The lead's Ribbon ( showRibbon ): its notes take the same LIVE path. A slide starts the next note before ending the last, so the engine glides, and dragging up adds vibrato.

The nameplate shows the loaded TAL sound's title, or POLY-6 for its own. A tap opens the sound picker. A double tap rebuilds its own sound from TAL's start-up sound, the engine's controls and the default knobs. CHORDS / NOTES / SLOTS tabs: ChordRoll , a poly PianoRoll on the same steps, and ChordSlots . ◀ ▶ switch them while the editor has the focus ( moveView , viewCount ). The step keys and ▲ ▼ work on the view on screen. CHORD SET , and the chord keys played as pads, which also fill an armed slot. LIVE follows the tab: on CHORDS and SLOTS, pads 1–7 are the degrees' chords. On NOTES, all 16 pads play single scale notes, and ▲ ▼ change the octave. With STEP on, ▲ ▼ walk the rows and SELECT writes the chord or note.

SampleScreen : the slot's waveform and trim handles, and a KnobGroup itself. A tap on it, or ▲ from the grid's top row, gives knob 1 to the start handle and knob 2 to the end. ▼ gives the knobs back to the rows. Buttons: LOAD (with hold-to-hear previews), ▶, CLEAR, REVERSE, ● REC, INPUT ( InputPopup ) and PITCH. The step grid over the bank's slots, with BANK A–D chips and ◀ ▶. LIVE: pads 1–8 are the slots and key 9 the accent. Knobs 1–3 are the selected row's mute, solo and level. All of qml/ is one QML module, Ravving , built into the binary by qt_add_qml_module . It's compiled with qmlcachegen (bytecode, and typed bindings as C++), and loaded with loadFromModule("Ravving", "Main") . Hardware and HardwareEvent join it through QML_ELEMENT . Every file imports Ravving ; there are no relative imports. For development, RAVVING_QML_DIR makes QmlSourceOverride , a URL interceptor, serve the .qml files from a source tree. QML edits then need only a restart. How ravving undoes and redoes edits: the History class, what is recorded, and how a new feature becomes undoable. The classes are in the API reference. Ravving has one undo history for the project, History ( src/backend/history.* ), published to QML as studio.history . Everything that can be undone goes through it; nothing keeps an undo stack of its own.

The patterns : every machine's notes, steps, chords, slots, accents, slides, lengths, automation, live timing and its preset's name ( Machine::historyState() ). Not the sound (source, factory sound, MODS), the mix (level, pan, mute), the effects or the project's settings (tempo, swing, key). Anything can join by becoming a participant (below). And the arrangement ( Sections::historyState() , "SECTIONS"): which sections there are, their order, names, colours and lengths, and the song. A removed section is put aside with its content ( Sections::m_removed ). Undoing the removal brings it back whole, in its place and in the song. Redoing it hands over to the neighbour, as REMOVE did. Not in it: the section on screen, and the machines' content (they have their own). A pick is no step, so an undo never switches what plays. The one exception is a section added and then undone: the first section takes over. Opening a project forgets the removed sections.

What it undoes Where The timeline the project's last step, whichever machines it touched the header's ↶ ↷, ALT + ◀ ▶ on the machine pages; a toast names it ("UNDO · CHORDS + BASS") One machine that machine's last change only, wherever it is in the timeline the pattern toolbar's ↶ ↷ ( machine.undo() / redo() , machine.canUndo / canRedo ) A machine can go back on its own because the participants' states are independent of each other: putting back the bass's last pattern cannot break the chords'.

h: What becomes one step › One turn of the event loop
t: One turn of the event loop. Everything recorded before control goes back to the event loop is one step. An action that changes several machines at once is undone in one go without any call: CLEAR (every machine), a key change that snaps the bass and the lead into the new key.

h: What becomes one step › Quick changes of one participant
t: Quick changes of one participant. A change within History::MergeMs (500 ms) of the same participant's last one joins its step: a knob turning, a handle dragged, a SELECT move repeated.

h: What becomes one step › A group
t: A group. Everything between begin(label) and end() (they nest), for an action spread over several turns. Machines also have their own groups for a recorded take ( Machine::beginEditGroup() / endEditGroup() ): the take is recorded once, at its end. A step stores, for each participant it touched, the state before and after; nothing else. The history keeps History::Depth (100) steps.

forget(participant) : its state is replaced wholesale, so its steps go (a section picked: undoing into a section that is not on screen would be a surprise; an engine attached again). clear() : a project opened or NEW ( Studio::applyProjectState() ).

C++ ( History ): add(p) / remove(p) register a participant (its state now is where it starts) / take it out record(p) after each change: a step, or part of the open one, when its state differs forget(p) , clear() see above undo() , redo() , canUndo , canRedo , undoText , redoText the timeline undoIn(key) , redoIn(key) , canUndoIn(key) , canRedoIn(key) one participant begin(label) , end() a group signals changed() , undone(what) , redone(what) QML: studio.history.undo() , .redo() , .canUndo , .canRedo , .undoText , .redoText , .begin() , .end() , .clear() ; a machine's own: machine.undo() , .redo() , .canUndo , .canRedo .

Implement HistoryParticipant (four functions): historyKey() : a name unique among the participants ("bass", "song"); historyLabel() : how the user reads a step of it ("BASS", "SONG"); historyState() : its state as plain data, equal when nothing that matters changed (leave out what only says what is on screen: a bar shown, a tab); applyHistoryState(state) : become that state (it may emit its change signals as usual: the history does not record what it puts back). Register it: studio.history → history->add(this) once it exists (Studio does it for the machines, Machine::setHistory() ). Call history->record(this) after each change the user makes (a machine does it on its edited() signal). Changes that are not the user's (a state restored, a project loaded) call forget(this) instead. Its own ↶ ↷, if it has any, call history->undoIn(key) / redoIn(key) ; their enabled state is canUndoIn(key) / canRedoIn(key) , refreshed on changed() . Nothing else: the timeline, the grouping, the toasts and the header's buttons come with it.

historyState() is computed after every change, so keep it cheap (a map of the content); the machines' is their contentState() less the sound and the view. One machine's undo clears the timeline's redo, since what it would redo doesn't match what's there. A timeline undo of a step a machine was part of can be redone by that machine's ↷ too: it falls back to the timeline's redo.

How ravving uses BlueZ and PipeWire for Bluetooth: devices, pairing, file transfer and audio output. The classes are in the API reference; the system setup is on Running on a Zynthbox. Ravving's Bluetooth does what a phone's does: pair, connect, send a file, play through a speaker or headphones, receive a file. What a Zynthbox needs for it is in packaging.md ("Bluetooth on a fresh device"), the tests in testing.md and the troubleshooting table in debugging.md .

Bluetooth ( src/backend/bluetooth.* , QML bluetooth ), on BluezQt. The UI is BluetoothPopup , from the control center's BLUETOOTH card. The adapter: power, discovery, and discoverable for three minutes. The devices: connected first, then paired, then by signal. Phones with a private address and no name stay hidden until paired. Pairing: an Agent (DisplayYesNo). A passkey to confirm or a PIN to type lands in pairing , answered with answerPairing . Then pair → trust → connect, or forget. Files: OBEX Object Push sending ( sendFile , progress in transfer ), and an ObexAgent accepting pushes into the library's incoming/ folder. Audio: the switch to a Bluetooth output ( useAsOutput ).

The Pi has one radio for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and an inquiry breaks up a playing A2DP link. So a scan lasts 12 s ( DiscoverySeconds ), and only starts on its own while no audio device is connected. It scans classic devices only ( setDiscoveryFilter {Transport: bredr} ). A dual-mode speaker paired from its LE advertisement gets no A2DP sink, and the Pi's firmware has no LE Audio.

When an audio device connects, WirePlumber makes a sink node bluez_output.<address>.1 , plus an input (capture) node for HFP. useAsOutput hands it to AudioOutputs ( outputs , also the control center's AUDIO OUTPUT card). AudioOutputs doesn't make it the default sink. That would clock the whole JACK graph by the Bluetooth transport, in 256-frame chunks (glitches), and leave the master's links to the jacks in place (sound from both). Instead: The jacks keep the clock. ravving starts its own pw-loopback , ravving-out : a virtual sink whose playback stream targets the Bluetooth sink, with a 2048-frame buffer. The master's two output ports are linked to it with pw-link . Its inputs have no JACK name, so libzynthbox's JackConnectionHandler can't. The jacks are muted, not unlinked. An unlinked jacks sink would suspend, and the Bluetooth transport would become the graph's clock. Off, on disconnect, forget or exit, the loopback stops and the jack links come back. A device connected on the headset profile only ( playback_MONO ) gets a mono mix-down.

PipeWire offers a2dp-sink-sbc_xq beside plain SBC, since ravving's WirePlumber drop-in sets bluez5.enable-sbc-xq . But WirePlumber connects with plain SBC. SETTINGS · BLUETOOTH · SBC-XQ ( AudioOutputs.preferSbcXq , on by default) switches the output in use to SBC-XQ when it offers it, or back to plain SBC. That happens once per connection ( wpctl set-profile ). Each paired device can override it with its own chip in the BLUETOOTH dialog ( AudioOutputs.sbcXqByDevice , setSbcXqFor() ). A device may advertise the bitpool and still not sustain it. A codec switch replaces the sink node under the same name. AudioOutputs notices the node id change and routes to the new one. A Bluetooth output gets its codec first, and is routed to once its new sink is there.

While another output plays, OutputWatch listens to what goes into the loopback and what comes out. If music goes in and silence comes out for six seconds, it routes again once, with a fresh loopback. If it's still silent, the issues center says the output plays no sound.

h: One audio device at a time
t: BlueZ keeps one local A2DP endpoint per codec, shared by every device, and a local endpoint carries one stream. PipeWire registers one SBC source, which SBC-XQ reuses. So while one device streams SBC, a second SBC device can't set up its audio ( Unable to select SEP , br-connection-create-socket ). When a device you're connecting answers but can't connect while another audio device is connected, ravving: shows SWITCHING FROM · the other ; disconnects the other one; waits 1 s for BlueZ to free the endpoint, and connects again. ravving's own reconnect never takes the link from a playing device.

A page timeout ( Host is down ) is retried after 2, 5 and 10 s. With BlueZ's 5.12 s page, that's about 37 s, while the row reads "waking…". Disconnecting or forgetting stops it. After that, it reads COULD NOT CONNECT, with the hint NOT ANSWERING: FREE IT FROM A PHONE, OR TURN IT OFF AND ON. PLAY THROUGH's sink poll (15 s) starts once the connection is made.

AudioOutputs keeps the Bluetooth address of the output picked. When Bluetooth comes on, at a start or with the switch, that device is connected once, 3 s later, if it's paired and nothing else plays. Never in a loop: paging a speaker in standby wakes it up.

Sending opens an OBEX session ( Target: opp ) and pushes the file. Receiving needs the device VISIBLE (discoverable and pairable, for three minutes). Files land under library/incoming/ . PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists them as "received", and the music library as the album "Received".

How LIVE REC records the screen or the sound: the JACK tap, FFmpeg, the microphone and voice over, the keys shown on a video, and the computer link. The classes are in the API reference. LIVE REC records the session. It makes either: a video: the screen or a USB camera, with the master's sound, as one MP4 in the library's videos/ folder ( Paths::videos() ); the sound alone: a WAV among the TRACKS ("Audio only", below). The code: src/backend/videorecorder.* ( video ), src/backend/audiotap.* , src/backend/computerlink.* ( computer ), qml/components/ComputerPopup.qml , LiveRecPopup.qml , VideoSavedPopup.qml , and the LIVE REC card in ControlCenter.qml . The rule it's built on: the sound comes first. A video may cost the audio nothing it can hear, and the audio in the video must never drop.

h: 1. The sound is tapped, not recorded through AudioLevels
t: AudioTap is ravving's own JACK client ( ravving-video , stereo in), connected to the master's last outputs. That's what the speakers get, LIVE FX inserts included, which the header's ● WAV recording misses. Its process callback copies each cycle into a ring of 2^20 frames (21.8 s at 48 kHz), and touches nothing else. A plain thread drains the ring into a named pipe ( $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ravving-video-<stamp>.pipe , with 1 MB of kernel buffering), as raw 32-bit float stereo. ffmpeg reads the pipe as -f f32le . Why not the other paths: libzynthbox's AudioLevels (the WAV recorder's and the exporter's path) runs one recording at a time. A video session must leave the header's ● and the samplers' record-to-pad free. ffmpeg's own -f jack input has a ring of 16 periods: 85 ms at 256 frames. An encoder or SD-card stall longer than that drops sound. This ring holds 21 seconds, and anything it can't hold is counted ( audioDroppedMs , a warning in the issues center), not lost quietly.

x11grab of the display ( -draw_mouse 0 ), or v4l2 of the camera, encoded with libx264 on two threads at nice -n 10 . The Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 encoder: ffmpeg lists h264_v4l2m2m , but the Pi 5's V4L2 nodes are its ISP and HEVC decoder. The tiers ("Limits", below) all run with 0 xruns.

ffmpeg stamps every grabbed frame with the wall clock ( -use_wallclock_as_timestamps 1 ; on this ffmpeg, x11grab's default stamps are the wall clock too). The tap takes the wall-clock moment of its first sample on the audio thread, from the cycle's own start. jack_get_cycle_times says the cycle began now − (jack_get_time() − cycle_usecs) ago. ffmpeg is told that moment with -itsoffset on the audio input. With -copyts , both streams sit on the same absolute clock in the file, to the millisecond.

The recording goes to .recording-<stamp>.mkv . A Matroska is readable even if ravving or ffmpeg dies; an MP4 without its index isn't. On STOP: The tap closes the pipe, so ffmpeg's audio input ends. ffmpeg gets SIGINT, and finishes its file. ffprobe reads the two streams' start times. The audio began while ffmpeg was starting, about 0.45 s before the first frame. ffmpeg -ss <video start − audio start> -i rec.mkv -c copy -movflags +faststart cuts the head to the first video frame. It writes the MP4 with its index up front and its title and date tags, and the Matroska is removed. The remux copies packets, so it takes a few seconds for a long recording ("SAVING" on the card and the plate). If the remux fails, the Matroska is kept under the final name.
SETTINGS · VIDEO · MIC mixes the RECORDER's input into the video's sound, as it's set up there: MIC, GUITAR or LINE, the jack in use, its GAIN and its effects.

h: A microphone in the sound › Nothing of the input is repeated for the video
t: Nothing of the input is repeated for the video. InputRecorder::setListener(ports) adds the tap's two mic ports ( ravving-video:mic_l / mic_r ) as one more destination at the end of the input chain. That's JackWiring::setInputChain 's listeners , beside the monitor lane and the take recorder; a mono input feeds both. The input counts as in use while a listener is set, so its effects run. The audio thread adds the ports to the master's sound, as the video hears it.

h: A microphone in the sound › The master itself is untouched
t: The master itself is untouched. The speakers get the mic only with the RECORDER's MONITOR on. Then the video hears it twice, louder, so use one or the other. tools/video-test.sh records once with MIC on and checks the link. tools/video-mic-check.sh is the listening test: a recording with the music stopped while someone speaks, then the file's audio measured.
With MIC on, the tap mixes the master and the mic as a voice over ( AudioTap::setVoiceOver , SETTINGS · VIDEO · VOICE). A plain sum leaves a voice at a normal distance some 25 dB under the master.
The mic is made crisp: a 120 Hz high-pass, and a +4 dB high shelf from 3 kHz (RBJ biquads on the audio thread). Then VOICE LIFT lifts it: +6 dB by default, +12, or flat.

The mic's envelope is followed, with an instant attack and a 250 ms release. While it's above the voice threshold, the master turns down to VOICE DUCK: −12 dB by default, −6 or −18, and 0 is off. It ducks in 20 ms, and comes back over 600 ms once the voice stops. So the music sits in the background exactly while someone speaks. With DUCK and LIFT both 0, the mix is the plain sum, still through the limiter.

The threshold is at least −34 dBFS, and 12 dB over what the speakers are expected to leak into the mic right now. That expected leak is the master's envelope, as ducked, times a leak ratio the tap learns as the mic's level over the master's. The ratio moves down within a second and up over 8 s, never past −26 dB of the master. It starts at 0.02 (−34 dB), from the moment VIDEO is on, since the mic is wired then. Against the expected leak, only a voice counts, so the beat doesn't duck itself through a mic near the speakers. The learning is slow upwards, so a steady tone under the threshold doesn't become "leak". The limits: a mic that hears the speakers louder than −26 dB of the master (in front of the speaker) still ducks itself. A leak between the start value and the cap ducks the beat for a second or two at its start, until the ratio has climbed. The RECORDER's GAIN scales the voice and the leak alike, so the ratio holds when it's turned.

The sum goes through a look-ahead peak limiter: 1 ms ahead, a ceiling of −1 dBFS, and a 150 ms release. The mix runs through a 1 ms delay line. The loudest sample in the line sets the gain, which comes down over a quarter of the line. So a hot mic over a loud beat is turned down before the peak comes out: never clipped, and never with the click of a gain step. The 1 ms sits inside the 3 ms of audio offset. The master without the mic isn't delayed.

The RECORDER's GAIN still sets how hot the voice comes in, and the recorder watches it. While VIDEO is on with MIC, the input is wired into the tap at once, not only while recording. Its peak is metered ten times a second ( micLevel , before the lift). SETTINGS · VIDEO shows it on a LEVEL bar with a −6 dB mark. The project plate carries it standing in its right corner while VIDEO is on: red while hot, with a blue dot at its foot while the music ducks. micHot : a peak over −6 dBFS within the last two seconds. The bar turns red, and the settings say MIC TOO HOT: turn the GAIN down. A mic peaking around −12 dBFS leaves the mix room and the limiter idle.

The voice over is for a voice. With the RECORDER on GUITAR or LINE, the input is summed as it is, through the limiter, and nothing ducks under a guitar; the VOICE rows say so. The settings apply at once, on a recording under way too.

tools/video-voice-check.sh measures the voice over: The music: a steady 300 Hz tone at −12 dBFS into the tap's master ports, so the measure doesn't depend on the project open. MUSIC=project plays the project instead. The voice: a 1 kHz tone in bursts (tools/tone.py, −20 dBFS; TONE_DB for another level) into the tap's mic ports. Second by second, the music must be DUCK dB quieter while the tone is on, and the tone must come out LIFT dB louder. No clipping: the file's peak under −0.5 dBFS, and no run of samples stuck at the ceiling. The meter must read the tone: video.micLevel near −20 dBFS while a burst plays, with micHot false. A −3 dBFS burst sets micHot .

A tap on the control center's LIVE REC card opens the LIVE REC dialog ( LiveRecPopup.qml ): WHAT: a VIDEO (the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, an MP4 among the VIDEOS), or AUDIO ONLY (the sound alone, a 24-bit WAV among the TRACKS, below); MIC: the RECORDER's input in the sound; START: switches LIVE REC on, and begins after the TIMER. The dialog is the confirmation, so a stray tap never starts a recording. The drawer closes first, so it isn't in the picture, and the TIMER counts down on an overlay that isn't recorded either, since ffmpeg starts after it. ◀ ▶ pick WHAT, ▲ ▼ toggle the MIC, and SELECT starts.

It reads LIVE REC · READY, REC IN n, REC mm:ss or LIVE REC · SAVING, and is lit while LIVE REC is on. A tap while it's on ends the recording and switches LIVE REC off. A new project (NEW in the project menu) switches LIVE REC off too, saving a recording under way first ( Projects::created ).

While VIDEO is on, RECORD and STOP are the video's, before any page sees them ( Ravving::handleCuia → VideoRecorder::takesKey ): RECORD starts when idle. When already recording, a toast says ■ stops it. STOP ends the recording, and stops the music with it: the session is over. During the countdown, it cancels. STOP with nothing recording is the transport's again. The header's ● and ■ do the same ( Session.toggleRecording / Session.stop ).

The project plate shows the video's state while VIDEO is on: VIDEO READY · ● RECORDS, VIDEO IN 3, ● REC 01:23, VIDEO · SAVING. The RECORD LED glows dim red when ready, orange during the countdown, and red while recording. STOP lights while there's something to end. The keys pressed: while a video records, every device key pressed is named in a short red notice at the screen's bottom ( Ravving::keyShown → Main.qml's second Toast), so the video shows what was played. ALT combos read "ALT + MODE", and knob turns "KNOB 1 ▲" or "BIG KNOB ▼". Turning it off: SETTINGS · VIDEO · KEYS ( video.showKeys , on by default). An audio recording shows none: there's no picture to explain.

VIDEO SAVED or LIVE REC SAVED shows the file, its length, size and picture size. DELETE , at the left, is a ConfirmButton: a second tap within three seconds removes the file ( VideoRecorder::remove ). RENAME and SEND… , at the right. SEND… opens the SendPopup: a USB stick's ravving/videos or ravving/exports , a computer, or the phone. METADATA… , for an audio recording (below). A failure is a toast, an issues-center entry and video.error : ffmpeg missing, no space, the encoder giving no frames in 12 s, or ffmpeg dying. What ffmpeg wrote before dying is still saved when it has frames.

LIVE REC's AUDIO ONLY ( video.mode "audio", VideoRecorder::audioOnly ) is the same recorder without the picture. The command has no video input and no encoder. The tap feeds ffmpeg as for a video, and ffmpeg writes -c:a pcm_s24le -f wav into .recording-<name>.wav in the exports folder ( Paths::exports() , the TRACKS the music player and FILES list). Nothing is encoded, and nothing has to be lined up: no -copyts , no -itsoffset . The first bytes out (ffmpeg's out_time_us in the progress report) stand for the first frame. Stopping renames the WAV to <project> - <date>.wav . There's no remux and nothing to cut: the sound begins where it began. The MIC, the voice over and the limiter apply as for a video. The key notices aren't shown.

When it ends, LIVE REC SAVED offers METADATA… beside DELETE, RENAME and SEND…. It's the export dialog over the file ( ExportPopup.openForFile ), the same form without WHAT and the lengths, with SAVE WITH TAGS. It calls Exporter::finishRecording(rawFile, metadata) : The WAV is written whole in the FORMAT chosen (WAV 24-bit, FLAC, OGG, MP3), under the NAME given, in the exports folder. It's tagged with the TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, GENRE, COMPOSER and COMMENT. Its cover is drawn and saved beside it, and its sidecar JSON written. The raw WAV is removed, and the files are copied to the stick or sent to the computer picked. That's the track export's own finishing ( Exporter::writeAndTag , one path for both), so a live recording and an exported track are the same kind of file afterwards. The tagged track then stands for the recording in LIVE REC SAVED ( VideoRecorder::adopt ), so RENAME and SEND… act on it. Without METADATA…, the plain WAV stays, playable and listed like any track.

SETTINGS · COMPUTERS holds the laptops or PCs that exports and videos can be sent to, over SSH. There can be any number: Computers ( computers ) is a list of ComputerLink s, each its own group computers/<id> of the settings file. An older version's single-computer set-up moves into c1 .
ADD A COMPUTER asks for the host name or address, the user there, and that user's password. A computer already in the list as the same user@host is set up again rather than added twice.

h: Adding a computer › The password is used once
t: The password is used once. It opens the first connection, so the device's own key ( ~/.config/ravving/ssh/id_ed25519 , made on the first CONNECT) can be installed with ssh-copy-id . It's never written to the settings. It reaches ssh through SSH_ASKPASS : a helper script of ravving's that prints a file readable by root alone, made for the set-up's seconds and removed after. SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force means no terminal is involved. The computer's host key is kept in ravving's own known_hosts : accepted on the first connection, and refused if it changes. FORGET removes that computer's entry with ssh-keygen -R ; the others stay.

The destination is the computer's Downloads folder: xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD , else ~/Downloads . Files go there with scp , one at a time ( busy / phase / progress ), and sent(ok, count, label) ends it with a toast. The statuses: unset, setting-up, ready, unreachable, refused (the computer refused the key: CONNECT AGAIN with the password), and failed. error says why it failed: a wrong password, a name that doesn't resolve, SSH refused or no answer, or a changed host key.

One standard SEND… button ( SendPopup ) offers every writable USB stick's ravving/ folder (through RemovableDrives::copyFiles ), each computer, and a phone by QR code ("Sending to a phone" in the manual). It's in: the FILES browser, for every kind: a project is bundled for the destination by Exporter::exportProjectFile , and a preset written out as one JSON file by FileBrowser::presetFile ; VIDEO SAVED, each track in the music player, the pattern presets dialog and the sound picker. The export dialog also has a COMPUTER row, a chip per computer with one lit. It sends a new track or bundle as soon as it's written ( Exporter::sendToComputer , with the metadata's computer set to the computer's id).
It needs an SSH server: Linux openssh-server (Arch: systemctl enable --now sshd ), or macOS "Remote Login". Windows' OpenSSH server has no $HOME/Downloads in its default shell, and isn't supported.

Stopping: recordings end with SIGINT, once; a second signal makes ffmpeg quit without its trailer. -t is never used, since it compares against the absolute timestamps -copyts keeps. Probing: the pipe input isn't probed ( -probesize 32 -analyzeduration 0 ), or ffmpeg would read 5 s of raw audio before opening the output. The video input's queue is 64 frames. The system clock: a step during a recording puts a jump in the video's timestamps. The Pi has no RTC, and timesyncd steps the clock on the first network sync after boot, so start recording once the device has been online for a moment. What's in the picture: exactly what's on the display. A dialog opened during the recording is in it; the countdown overlay and the drawer aren't. USB cameras are found in /sys/class/video4linux : the node with index 0 on a USB device. The capture size follows the tier: 640 × 480 for LOW, 1280 × 720 otherwise.

SETTINGS · VIDEO · QUALITY, with AAC audio at 192 kb/s: Tier Picture Encoder HIGH full screen, 30 fps veryfast, crf 21 MEDIUM (the default) full screen, 15 fps veryfast, crf 23 LOW 640 × 400, 30 fps veryfast, crf 26 All three run with 0 xruns on a Pi 5. tools/video-encode-impact.sh measures them; mirror any change to the encoder arguments there.

What ravving relies on for each engine and where each fact comes from. The port facts come from the engine mods' research (each mod's docs/RESEARCH.md , decoded from the engine's own source); read the mod before changing an engine's engine.controls in data/kits.json or its MODS profile in data/engines.json .

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json)
t: What a page lets you tweak of an engine belongs to the engine , not the machine. That's its SOUND MODIFIERS, the MODS cards, and its expressions, such as the lead ribbon's vibrato. There's one profile per engine in data/engines.json , found by the engine itself: its type , and for jalv the plugin uri ( EngineProfiles ). Every source that plays an engine shows its knobs, on any machine: Profile Engine Shown for tal-noisemaker TAL-NoiseMaker (jalv) CHORDS' own synth nekobi Nekobi (jalv) BASS' own synth calf-monosynth Calf Monosynth (jalv) LEAD's own synth, BASS' 808 · Monosynth source fluidsynth FluidSynth every soundfont source (one set for all of a machine's soundfonts: its knobs are offsets to the preset's own sound)

A source starts its knobs where its own engine.controls put those ports , so loading a source never changes its sound. The 808's cutoff of 400 Hz shows as the CUTOFF knob at 400. Without such a control, a knob starts at the profile's default . The project keeps each set apart: sound (the own engine's), sourceSound (the soundfonts'), sourceSounds (each other plugin source's, by name); AUTO lanes are sound/… , source/… and sources/<source>/… .

h: How the knobs behave › An engine with no profile shows no MODS
t: An engine with no profile shows no MODS. A machine or a source that brings its own sound in kits.json keeps it (a special case; the profile is the rule).

h: Checked against the engines' real ports, twice
t: On the laptop, tools/check-engines.py ( ctest -R engines ) checks every knob, choice, expression and kits.json control against the plugins' ports, ranges included, from tests/data/lv2-ports.json . After adding an engine or upgrading plugins, run tools/check-engines.py --refresh to read them again from the device's lv2info . On the device, SoundEngine::hasControl() checks the playing source's MODS when an engine starts. A knob on a control the engine lacks shows in the issues centre, as "BASS MODS: Calf Monosynth lacks 1 of their controls". Adding an engine's MODS: Add its profile to data/engines.json . The cards are as SoundControls reads them: symbol , min , max , default 0..1, "curve": "log" , or choices for a switch. Refresh the ports if it's a new plugin, and run tools/check-engines.py . Hear each knob on the device: device.sh call <machine>.activeSound setValue CARD KNOB 0..1 .

http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi , a TB-303 clone. Research: nekobi_acid_mod . Fact What ravving does waveform : the plugin's own labels are wrong : 0 renders a square, 1 a sawtooth WAVE switch: SAW = 1, SQR = 0 decay is a rate : higher % = shorter (τ 2.3 s at 0 %, 42 ms at 100 %) DECAY runs 100 → 0, so turning it up lengthens notes accent is velocity > 90 (forced short decay, filter "wow" from resonance) plain 80, accent 127 glide is always on (τ ≈ 13 ms) when notes overlap SLIDE = the note lasts 1.5 steps cutoff 0–100 % ≈ 0–5 kHz (capped ~6.5 kHz), resonance 0–95 %, env_mod , accent , tuning ±12 CUTOFF, RESO, ENV MOD, ACCENT, TUNE as LV2 ranges volume is linear ( v/100 ); Zynthbox's jalv wrapper pins it, ravving's jalv does not volume 100

http://kunz.corrupt.ch/products/tal-noisemaker . Research: noizemakr_mod . Fact What ravving does every port is a bare 0..1; enums quantise as floor(v·(n−1) + 1.5) (1-based): write i/(n−1) voices 1 (6 voices), portamentomode 1 (On: chords glide too), lfo1destination 1/7 (Filter), lfo1waveform 0 (sine), transpose 0.5 (0 oct), filtertype 0 (LP 24 dB; its den is 11) osc1waveform : Saw, Pulse, Noise; osc2waveform : Saw, Pulse, Triangle, Sine, Noise WAVE: SAW, JUNO (pulse, osc1pw 0.75), SQR (pulse 0.5), TRI (osc 2) lfo1amount is bipolar and cubic: (2(v − 0.5))³ , 0.5 = none LFO knob spans 0.5 … 1 lfo1rate = (e^(0.2 + 3v·ln20) − 1) / 19 Hz 0.3 ≈ 0.9 Hz, a slow sweep envelopes are one-poles, very steep: release 67 ms at 0.3, 0.5 s at 0.45, 1 s at 0.5, 3.5 s at 0.6, 12 s near 1; attack 16 ms at 0.15, 0.77 s at 0.45 (computed with the mod's own formulas; its summary table is off) ATTACK spans 0 … 0.55 (3.6 ms … 3.2 s), LENGTH 0.15 … 0.65 (10 ms … 5.8 s) chorus1enable , chorus2enable (the Juno chorus I / II) CHORUS switch OFF / I / II detune , cutoff (log inside the engine), resonance , portamento SPREAD, CUTOFF, RESO, GLIDE volume 's curve is undocumented; measured steeper than linear (0.55 → 0.51 RMS, 0.25 → 0.068) volume 0.25 256 factory presets in the bundle's presets.ttl (78 leads, 53 basses, 34 FX, 28 drums, 26 pads, 15 arps, 13 keys, 7 chords: the name's prefix), each with its port values next to the JUCE state (the mod's research reached them only through the programs extension, which jalv does not surface) SOUND ▾ on CHORDS loads one by setting its ports ( Machine::loadSoundPreset ), keeping voices , volume , transpose ; the SOUND MODIFIERS follow it ( SoundControls::adopt )

http://calf.sourceforge.net/plugins/Monosynth . Research: calf_monosynth_mod (+ its engine-symbols.txt ). Fact What ravving does two envelopes: EG1 → cutoff ( env2cutoff , default 8000 cents), EG2 → amp ( adsr2_amp = 1) LENGTH drives adsr2_r ; adsr2_s 1 (a held note sustains); ENV is env2cutoff 0 … 4800 cents logarithmic ports: cutoff, every EG time, portamento, LFO rates CUTOFF 300 … 9000 Hz, GLIDE 1 … 400 ms, LENGTH 10 … 3000 ms with "curve": "log" o1_wave 16 waves: 0 Sawtooth, 1 Square, 3 Sine, 4 Triangle… WAVE: SAW, SQR, SIN, TRI; o12_mix 0 (osc 1 only) legato 0 Retrig, 1 Legato, 2/3 finger modes; pbend_range up to 2400 cents legato 1 (overlapping notes glide), pbend_range 1200 one LFO1 drives lfo2pitch and lfo2filter vibrato only: lfo_rate 5.5 Hz, lfo2pitch played by the ribbon (expression vibrato , 0 … 60 cents) master 0..1 (Zynthbox's wrapper pins it; ravving's jalv does not) master 0.3

FluidSynth 2.4.4 (a process, not an LV2), one per drum machine with its kit's soundfont. Research: fluidsynth2_mod . Fact What ravving does level CCs (7, 11) and velocity attenuate as 40·log10(v/127) dB, twice the usual law row levels go through velocity (level 0.8 → velocity 100 ≈ −4 dB; accent ×1.27 → 127) reverb / chorus CCs are sends of at most 20 %; the effects' settings have no CC none sent: with FluidSynth's own reverb and chorus on or off, a snare's tail is silent either way (CC 91 stays 0 and the 909 kit sends none): the drums carry no hidden reverb started like zynthbox-qml: -g 1 , synth.polyphony=64 , MMA bank select the same command line The drums' SOUND MODIFIERS are the kit's own (engines.json's kitSound , EngineProfiles::resolveKit): Card Knobs TONE CUTOFF, RESO SHAPE ATTACK, LENGTH (the release) PITCH TUNE in semitones, FINE in cents They're SF2 generator offsets sent as NRPNs, like the soundfont sources' MODS. A kit is one soundfont on one channel, so they act on the whole kit. Per-drum settings would need a channel per row. Acoustic kits inside a General MIDI font (kits.json presetKits , the picker's ACOUSTIC group): The path may name one preset of a soundfont, <file>#<bank>:<program> , then choose a row's key: ?CYMBAL=51&HAT=44 . FluidR3's kits sit at bank 128 (Jazz 32, Brush 40, Standard 0, Room 8) and keep the General MIDI map. A key whose sample name says nothing, like "Md Studio" for its toms, takes its GM role. "Jazz · ride" and "Brush · ride" put the ride (51) on CYMBAL and the hi-hat foot (44) on HAT, shown as PEDAL. The plain "Jazz · crash" keeps the crash, for breaks. FluidSynth gets the file, the bank and the program. A project saves the path with its choices.

libzynthbox's own sampler: no process, clips (ClipAudioSource) played in the audio thread. Facts from libzynthbox's source ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp , ClipAudioSourceSliceSettings.cpp , AudioLevels.cpp ). Fact What ravving does a slice's envelope defaults to {attack 0, decay 0, sustain 1, release 0} only the release is set (8 ms, the choke's fade) a stock libzynthbox fades every voice in over ~165 ms (started at gain 0, ramped 0.0001 a frame) needs a patched libzynthbox (a voice starts at its gain; only aftertouch changes ramp) a one-shot retriggered on the same clip and slice stops its previous voice ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp:392 ) the slots choke themselves; no exclusivityGroup needed one-shots cannot play backwards (only loops and granular do) REVERSE plays a reversed copy of the file a track's channel_N-sampleM ports exist only while a clip is registered on that slot wired per loaded slot ( setSampleOutputs ) ClipAudioSource::play(…, velocity) : 64 is unity gain previews play at 64 on the global lane AudioLevels' track gain (a machine's VOL) runs −40…+20 dB, 0 at gainAbsolute 0.667; the lane's sends leave before it the sends are scaled by VOL's gain in ravving ( TrackEffects::setSendLevel )

h: The audio input (HiFiBerry DAC+ADC Pro, PCM1863)
t: Fact What ravving does the five jacks, left to right: 1 headphones, 2–3 line outputs (speaker icon), 4–5 inputs (mic icon); jack 4 is the left channel (ADC input VINL1), jack 5 the right MIC and GUITAR record the jack with the signal ( activeJack : picked between takes when one jack is 10 dB over the other and above −45 dBFS; mixing both added the empty input's noise, audibly), so either jack works; LINE is stereo; INPUT lights each jack's level (AudioLevels' capture meter, rewired to the real inputs); monitor on headphones in jack 1 the HiFiBerry's JACK capture ports are named like a Dummy card's, and which gets the serial suffix changes between boots found by the card each start ( InputPorts ) input noise is mostly the room around the cables (a ground loop through a USB-Ethernet link to a charging laptop is the usual suspect); screen brightness, mic bias, one or two ADC inputs make no difference — the ADC's input mux is ADC Left/Right Input ; ADC … Capture Source does not change what is heard the selection is left as Zynthbox sets it PGA −12…+40 dB in 0.5 dB steps ( PGA Gain Left/Right ), mic bias on/off; Zynthbox selects VINL2 + VINL1 MIC +30 dB with bias, GUITAR +10 dB (a strummed electric peaked −5 dBFS at +18), LINE 0 dB; the selection left as Zynthbox sets it the open input's noise is −69 dBFS at +30 dB a take under −50 dBFS is refused, not normalised into noise input → monitor ≈ 11–16 ms (256 frames at 48 kHz); the capture node follows the output's clock (no resampling) MONITOR through track 9's lane with its own LEVEL

Ports from lv2info on the device; the chains are in the presets file. A silent mic at +40 dB PGA picks up noise in bursts, mostly under 300 Hz: CLEAN cuts it with a 24 dB/octave high-pass and a gate. Plugin Facts the presets rely on Calf Compressor stereo; threshold is linear (0.06 ≈ −24 dBFS), ratio 1–20, attack / release ms, makeup 1–64 (×) Calf Saturator stereo; drive 0.1–10, blend −10…10, mix 0–1, pre/post high- and low-pass in Hz Calf Multi Chorus stereo; amount (wet) and dry 0–4, voices 1–8, mod_rate Hz, mod_depth ms Calf Vintage Delay stereo; timing 0 = BPM (from the bpm port), subdiv 4 with time_l / time_r 3/4 = a dotted eighth / a quarter; amount (wet) 0–4, feedback , medium 1 = tape Calf Ring Modulator stereo; mod_freq 1–20000 Hz (20–600 for a robot), mod_amount 0–1, mod_mode 0 = sine Calf Filter stereo; mode 4 = 24 dB/octave high-pass, 7 = 12 dB band-pass; freq Hz, res 0.707–32 Calf Gate stereo; threshold linear (0.01 = −40 dBFS), range the most it closes (0.03 = −30 dB), ratio , attack / release ms Dragonfly Plate stereo; dry_level and its wet level (the port is named early_level ) 0–100, decay s, predelay ms, low_cut / high_cut Hz MaPitchshift (DISTRHO) mono in , two outs; ratio 0.25–4 (0.5 = an octave down), window ms, blur ; no dry mix SwankyAmp stereo, its own cabinet ( cabonoff ); every port 0–1 ( preampdrive , powerampdrive , inputlevel , outputlevel …) A mono plugin in the chain takes both sides summed and feeds both sides of what follows ( JackWiring::setInputChain ). Each plugin of a chain is a jalv process of its own, about 1–2 % CPU each.

Calf Saturator (DRIVE), Calf Crusher (CRUSH), Calf Phaser (PHASER), Dragonfly Room (REVERB), TAP Echo (DELAY) have no mods; their ports come from lv2info and were calibrated by measurement ( tools/lv2probe.sh , see debugging.md ). The beat repeat (STUTTER, LOOP) is ravving's own JACK client.

What ravving wires, how to look at it and how to measure it. The graph is PipeWire's, seen by libzynthbox and the engines through PipeWire's JACK library ( pw-jack ), as zynthbox-qml also uses it. tools/graph-check.py (run with tools/device.sh graph … ) does the checks below in one go.

JackWiring (src/backend/jackwiring.*) asks libzynthbox's JackConnectionHandler for every link and retries until the ports exist (engines and passthroughs make their ports a moment after they are requested). Per machine (z: its Zynthian channel, t: its sketchpad track): ZLRouter:Zynthian-Channel{z} ─MIDI─> ravving-<key>-midi:midi_00 (FluidSynth) ravving-<key>:<lv2 midi in> (jalv) ravving-<key>:output_FL/FR ──> [DRIVE insert] ──> SynthPassthrough:Synth{z+1}-input{L,R} SynthPassthrough:Synth{z+1}-dryOut ──> TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-input TrackPassthrough lane dryOut ──> AudioLevels:Channel{t+1} ──> GlobalPlayback:input TrackPassthrough lane wetOutFx1 ──> ravving-reverb ──> GlobalPlayback:input (send 1) TrackPassthrough lane wetOutFx2 ──> ravving-delay ──> GlobalPlayback:input (send 2) SamplerSynth:channel_{t+1}-sample{n} ──> the track's lane (the samplers' slots) SamplerSynth:global-sketch1 ──> GlobalPlayback:input (the metronome's ticks) GlobalPlayback:dryOut ──> ravving-repeat ──> ravving-crush ──> ravving-phaser (the master inserts: LIVE FX) ──> system:playback_1/2 (or ravving-out, a loopback, when the sound goes to Bluetooth / HDMI: [architecture.md](bluetooth.md)) jacks 4/5 (the HiFiBerry's capture, HardwarePorts) ──> [input inserts] ──> a track's lane (monitor) and / or AudioLevels:SystemRecorder (record); AudioLevels:SystemCapture meters the input The link PipeWire makes on its own from every new engine to the speakers is removed, as zynthbox-qml's autoconnect does, so all sound goes through its track (level, mute, FX). Clock: every JACK client (libzynthbox's nodes, jalv) runs at the graph's rate and period, 48000 / 256 on a Zynthbox. FluidSynth's audio goes through its PipeWire driver, a stream whose node can run on its own clock. So ravving tells it the graph's rate and period ( AudioGraph , read once through a throwaway JACK client), and it isn't resampled.

ravving never trusts a hardware port's JACK name. pipewire-jack names a device's ports after its node's description, or system: for the default device. Two cards sharing a description take turns at the plain name and a -<serial> one, from one start of PipeWire to the next. On a Zynthbox, the kernel's snd-dummy and the HiFiBerry are both "Built-in Audio Stereo". A name alone can point the input at the silent Dummy. The device: data/wireplumber/50-ravving-hardware.conf hides the Dummy from PipeWire. The HiFiBerry is then the only "Built-in Audio Stereo", and the system: device on every start (by its priority, 10000 against 1000). libzynthbox and zynthbox-qml wire that name too. ravving: HardwarePorts finds a card's ports by the card. In pw-dump , each port's port.alias is " : " (kits.json input.portsCard ). Its JACK name is the JACK port whose UUID carries that port's object serial. pipewire-jack makes a port's UUID as (1 << 32) | (serial + 1) . The input ( captureOf ) and the speakers ( playbackOf , JackWiring::setSpeakers ) are found that way at start. The input is found again each time it's armed, when the RECORDER or INPUT opens. Seeing it: compare pw-jack jack_lsp -U (the UUIDs) with pw-dump (the serials and aliases). The journal says ravving: input ports … and ravving: speakers … .

Tool What it shows Use pw-top -b -n 2 every node: driver (no + ) or follower, QUANT/RATE it runs at, WAIT/BUSY per cycle, W/Q B/Q (fractions of the period), ERR (xruns), format the first thing to look at; tools/graph-check.py parses it pw-dump the whole graph as JSON: nodes with props ( node.rate , node.latency , api.alsa.* ), ports, links, devices with profiles scripting; pw-dump ID for one object pw-dot + dot -Tpng the graph as a picture pw-dot -o /tmp/g.dot; dot -Tpng /tmp/g.dot > g.png (graphviz on the laptop) pw-link -l / -o / -i links by PipeWire names (the only names some nodes have: the loopback's inputs) pw-link A:out B:in , pw-link -d to remove pw-jack jack_lsp -c / -l JACK names with connections / latency ranges ravving's and libzynthbox's names pw-mon events as they happen (nodes, links, params) watching an engine start or a link appear pw-metadata -n settings 0 the defaults ( clock.quantum 1024, clock.rate ) and forced values NOT the running clock: that is the driver row in pw-top pw-cli info ID one node's params (Props: channelVolumes…) volumes, formats wpctl status / inspect / set-profile WirePlumber's view: devices, profiles, defaults the sound card's profile (below) pw-jack jack_iodelay round-trip latency through a cable from an output jack to an input jack the only true end-to-end audio latency measurement pw-jack jack_midi_latency_test MIDI round trip through a loopback (a cable between a MIDI out and in, or a2j's Midi Through) MIDI path latency and jitter pw-jack jack_bufsize / jack_cpu_load the period, the DSP load JACK sees tools/mididump.py the MIDI an engine really receives on a port silent-engine investigations tools/meter.py RMS on any ports is sound passing a link tools/graph-check.py rates/periods vs the graph, xrun deltas, linked-but-idle nodes, the ravving links the routine check

rates : every audio node's rate and period against the running driver's. A node at another rate is resampled; a node with a larger period is buffered by that much. idle : nodes with links that are not running: a link that passes no data looks like this (an engine linked while still registering: re-make the link). xruns -s N : each node's ERR counter now and N seconds later. Compare idle vs playing, and before vs after a change. links ravving : what is linked, grouped by output port, to check against the map above.

FluidSynth is started with -r <graph rate> -o audio.period-size=<period> -o audio.periods=2 : its node runs at the graph's rate, not resampled, buffered by two periods (48000 / 512, 10.7 ms). The ring is what keeps a busy engine from starving the graph. Thread priorities ( graph-check.py threads ): Thread Priority PipeWire's data loops FIFO 88 (the daemon), 83 (the clients: libzynthbox's, jalv's, FluidSynth's) FluidSynth's render thread ( fluid_pipewire ) not realtime: its audio.realtime-prio 60 covers the synth thread only jalv's main thread not realtime: it does no audio work libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread FIFO 99, once the transport has run RAVVING_GDB=1 runs ravving under gdb -batch , which stops the whole process at every fork and thread start or exit. The graph then counts 20 to 40 xruns a minute. It's for crash hunts only. On a device in use, run systemctl --user unset-environment RAVVING_GDB and restart. tools/device.sh deploy warns when it finds it set. The same goes for any debugger or profiler attached to zynthbox-qml.
