With nothing attached the graph has room to spare: a full project playing runs with 0 xruns, the busiest node (TrackPassthrough) at about 6 % of the period.

Sequenced notes: libzynthbox's SyncTimer schedules them on the JACK frame clock and ZLRouter puts each machine's on ZLRouter:Zynthian-Channel{z} , linked to the engine's MIDI input (above). tools/mididump.py PORT SECONDS prints what a port carries. External keyboards: MidiRouter's hardware pass-through ( MidiInput , port 3) feeds the LIVE machine; raw notes reach no engine on their own (the current sketchpad track is parked at 9). Midi Through arrives twice, through a2j and through PipeWire's Midi-Bridge, so copies closer than 4 ms are dropped ( architecture.md ). Bluetooth MIDI: bluez_midi.server is PipeWire's BLE MIDI node, idle unless a BLE MIDI device connects. Latency: MIDI round trip: pw-jack jack_midi_latency_test between a hardware MIDI out and in, joined by a cable. a2j 's Midi Through measures the software path alone. Audio round trip: pw-jack jack_iodelay , with a cable from an output jack into input jack 4 or 5.

The sound card's playback node is the driver ( priority.driver 10000 from /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/99-default-soundcard.conf ). It stays the driver whatever output is picked. With the sound routed to Bluetooth or HDMI, the master's links to the jacks stay in place and the jacks are muted. An unlinked playback node would suspend, and another node would become the clock: the card's capture, or the Bluetooth transport.

ravving speaks English, Spanish and Japanese. Every text on its screen goes through KI18n , KDE's gettext layer, and the webpage (site/) is translated from catalogs of its own. The docs stay in English. Language App catalog Webpage catalog Spanish (es) po/es/ravving.po po-site/es/ravving-site.po Japanese (ja) po/ja/ravving.po po-site/ja/ravving-site.po

The domain. Localization (src/backend/localization.cpp) sets the application domain ravving right after the QGuiApplication is made, as the KI18n guide asks. It also adds the build tree's locale/ folder, so a build runs translated before it's installed. The catalogs install to /usr/share/locale/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/ravving.mo , through CMake's ki18n_install(po) . The AppImage's default-app.sh install copies them too.
QML. KLocalization::setupLocalizedContext(&engine) (KF 6.8 and later) puts i18n , i18nc , i18np and i18ncp on the root context, so QML calls them bare.
SETTINGS · LANGUAGE. SYSTEM (the default) follows the device's own language; English, Español and 日本語 pick one. The choice is kept in the profile settings ( ui/language ).

Live switching. A change sets KLocalizedString::setLanguages , sends QEvent::LanguageChange to the application and calls QQmlEngine::retranslate() . Every binding that calls i18n… runs again, so the screen changes at once. C++ models whose rows carry display text (the video tiers, FILES, the USB page, the audio outputs) catch LanguageChange , as the Qt guide does for plain QObjects, and emit NOTIFY.

h: How it works › Numbers and dates
t: Numbers and dates. C++ formats them through KI18n ( subs(value, 0, 'f', 1) ); QML uses Rave.num(value, decimals) , the locale of the language picked. Dates use QLocale of the first language KI18n uses.

Only display text is translated, where it's drawn. Text that's stored, compared, sent or looked up stays English: the machine roles, preset and kit names, scale names and group names; the effect and knob names in data/engines.json; the menu ids, the fifo names and the CUIA names. QML: Rave.kli18nc(context, key) marks a key for extraction and returns it unchanged (the QML side of KI18n's kli18nc , as Qt's QT_TR_NOOP ). The helpers translate at draw time: Rave.group , Rave.drumRow , Rave.param , Rave.paramGroup , Rave.effect , Rave.choice , Rave.tuning , Rave.stringInstrument , Rave.inputMode . Menus dispatch by id , never by the text shown. C++: tables of display text are KLazyLocalizedString ( kli18nc ), turned into text with .toString() when read, so a language change shows at once. A message with values is a KLocalizedString template ( ki18nc(…).subs(…) ) passed on and finished where it is shown. List models carry a display role beside the key, as Qt's QAbstractListModel examples do: the key for the logic, the display text for the screen.

Data. tools/i18n-data.py writes the data files' vocabulary as i18nc calls into the extraction, as KDE's rc.cpp does, under the helpers' contexts. That's the drum rows, the engines' knobs and cards, effects, scales, tunings and groups.

Every call is i18nc with a context saying what the text is, starting with a KDE UI marker: @action:button , @option:check , @option:radio , @label , @title:window , @title:group , @item:inlistbox , @info , @info:status , @info:placeholder . The context names the music meaning when a word has several ("SONG" the page, "SONG" the PLAY mode). All sound vocabulary shares one context, so a knob name is translated once. Names printed on the device stay English in every language: MENU, ALT, MODE, BACK, SELECT, PLAY, STOP, RECORD, X, Y. So do product and machine names (SAMPLE KING, PAD SAMPLER, POLY-6, the engines and kits), MIDI, USB, HDMI, SBC-XQ and LIVE FX. tools/check-ui.py 's text-translatable rule finds a display text that skips i18n… ; its keep list holds these.

The translations use the words musicians and producers use in each language. English Spanish Japanese DRUMS BATERÍA ドラム BASS BAJO ベース CHORDS ACORDES コード LEAD LEAD リード SAMPLER SAMPLER サンプラー PADS PADS パッド SONG CANCIÓN ソング SECTION SECCIÓN セクション PATTERN PATRÓN パターン PRESET PRESET プリセット KICK / SNARE BOMBO / CAJA キック / スネア SCALE / ROOT ESCALA / TÓNICA スケール / ルート BAR / STEP COMPÁS / PASO 小節 / ステップ LIVE REC REC EN VIVO ライブ録音 RECORDER GRABADORA レコーダー TRACK PISTA トラック SETTINGS AJUSTES 設定 knob / big knob perilla / perilla grande ノブ / 大ノブ Japanese uses katakana for the studio words (ドラム, リバーブ, スケール) and kanji for plain ones (保存, 削除, 設定). Spanish has two plural forms, Japanese one.

Spanish runs about a third longer than English. ActionButton and Chip shrink their text to fit, down to 75 % of its size; a text still too long is elided. Look at every page in Spanish after adding text.

sh tools/i18n-extract.sh # sources → po/ravving.pot and po-site/ravving-site.pot, merged into every catalog # translate what it marked: empty or fuzzy entries (Lokalize, Poedit or a text editor) python3 tools/check-translations.py # the ctest translations-current python3 tools/site-i18n.py render # po-site → site/es/ and site/ja/ check-translations.py fails when: a template is stale, or a catalog doesn't compile ( msgfmt --check ); a text is untranslated or fuzzy; a translation drops a placeholder ( %1 ) or a markup tag ( <b> , <a> ); the rendered pages are older than their catalogs.

tools/site-i18n.py extract collects the text of site/index.html, site/features.html and the user guide's pages (site/docs/get-ravving.html, machines.html, first-beat.html, as tools/build-site-docs.py renders them) into po-site/ravving-site.pot: every block of text (a heading, a paragraph, a row's words), with its inline , and
; the alt , title , aria-label and placeholder attributes; site.js's captions and marks. render writes site/ /index.html, site/ /features.html, site/ /docs/ (the guide's pages) and site/ /site.js. A link to a translated page stays in the language; any other goes to the English one, so the manual and the developer docs stay English. The language switcher in the top bar links the three languages. Text sitting loose beside other elements (

Five keys. …

) can't become a message: extract warns about it, and the page wraps it ( Five keys. ). , and anything marked translate="no" stay as they are. The page's catalogs live in po-site/, not po/: ki18n_install compiles every catalog in po/ into the device's install.

msginit --no-translator --no-wrap -l <lang> -i po/ravving.pot -o po/<lang>/ravving.po , and the same from po-site/ravving-site.pot into po-site/ /ravving-site.po. Translate both, following the glossary above (add a column for the new language). Add the language to the Languages table in src/backend/localization.cpp, by its own name. Add its link to the switchers in site/index.html and site/features.html, and their hreflang alternates. Run the workflow, then look at every page in the new language on the device.

Before every release, someone who reads the language reviews what changed in each catalog since the last release: new and changed texts, and the screens they appear on. Run git diff v<last> -- po po-site , take the screenshot tour in each language, and check that ctest -R translations-current passes. A release does not ship with fuzzy or untranslated texts.

ravving's screens share one look: machines with side rails and a face in their own finish; controls grouped on strips; work areas recessed in wells; a dark header band on top. These rules keep every new screen in it. tools/check-ui.py checks them over the QML, as a laptop test ( ctest -R ui-rules ) and in tools/static-analysis.sh ui . tools/ui-rules.json holds the rules and their exceptions, and is where a new rule goes.

Use the component; never redraw it. What Component Where it is A page's body: the rails and the face in its finish Chassis every page ( MachineModule wears it for the machines) The top band of controls (row 1: transport, plate, ✕; row 2: the deck) PageHeader the dashboard ( RaveHeader ), every full-window page The recessed display in a header's first row HeaderPlate the project name, the track playing, the take A row of buttons on its grouping strip ToolStrip the pattern toolbars, the SONG rows, the player's and the RECORDER's groups A recessed panel for a work area Well the RECORDER's input, tuner, effects, the lists An action ActionButton everywhere (squared, the standard height) An action that cannot be undone (asks twice) ConfirmButton DELETE, REMOVE, CLEAR SONG, FORMAT, EJECT A state (on/off with an LED, or one of a set) Chip / StripButton modes, tabs, banks, sorts The way out CloseButton (the ✕) every dialog (DialogHeader) and every full page An empty list or view EmptyNote every list and grid A dialog's title row DialogHeader every dialog The way a file leaves the device: a SEND… button opening the destinations (USB sticks, the computer, the phone by QR code) SendPopup ( QrPopup for the phone) the FILES browser (every kind), VIDEO SAVED, the music player's tracks, the presets dialog, the sound picker

Squared ActionButton : it does something once and leaves no state. LOAD, CLEAR, SAVE, RENAME, NEW, −/+, ◀ ▶, PLAY FROM HERE, TRIM, TO PADS, the transport keys, a picker showing its current value (it opens a list). Rounded Chip / StripButton : a state you can see. It stays lit while the state is on, so it always binds checked , or is checkable. Checked: chip-shows-state . An on/off toggle wears its LED: SET, STEP, LIVE, S/M, MONITOR, REPEAT. One choice out of a set wears none: BANK A–D, the views, SORT, the input tabs, KEEP TAKES IN. ConfirmButton for what cannot be undone: the first tap arms it (AGAIN? and a countdown bar), a second one within three seconds does it. All of them at the standard size (see Button sizes). Checked: actions-are-actionbuttons (no bare QQC.Button ).

One height: Rave.controlHeight (36 px) for every button, action or state, so a row of them lines up and a finger always finds the same target on the 1280×800 touch screen. A smallest width: Rave.controlWidth (48 px, square) for a glyph (◀ ▶ − + ⟳ ✕), and Rave.actionMinWidth (88 px) for a word (LOAD, SCAN, SAVE). A short word is no smaller a target than a long one, and a longer label grows past it. ActionButton applies both on its own ( minimumWidth ). A button may ask for more, never less: the dialogs' main action, SAVE at 150, or SCAN at 130 so SCANNING… doesn't shift the row. A row that wants bigger buttons sizes them all from one property (the SONG page's rowButtonHeight , wordButtonWidth ), never with numbers on each button. Checked: button-standard-size (no number under the standard on a button's height or width).

h: Controls in a group take the device knobs
t: Dials, switches (WaveCycler) and sliders that sit together are a KnobGroup , with them as its targets . The group takes the focus: a tap on it, or ◀ ▶ between groups. The device's three small knobs then drive its controls in order, and the big knob one more. Each control wears its KnobBadge (1, 2, 3) saying which knob moves it, with the pick-up diamond on the fixed-pot kit. A group shows its frame while it has the knobs. The models: ParamCard (the MODS and SOUND EFFECTS cards), and the header's TEMPO, FX SENDS and MASTER. So nothing a finger can turn is out of reach of the hardware, and the badges say which knob is which without a manual. Checked: grouped-controls-take-knobs (a file with dials, switches or sliders and no KnobGroup).

h: Rows of controls sit on bands (dialogs and pages)
t: A page's or a dialog's row of controls sits on one ToolStrip : the darker rounded band a pattern toolbar is, with the preset, OCT and undo / redo on one band. One row, one continuous band , never split into a band per group. The groups in it (a GroupLabel first, then its chips) are told apart by the space between them, as the toolbar's are. In the presets and sounds dialogs (ChoicePopup), SOURCE at the left and LOAD at the right share their row's band. GROUP and SORT share theirs: the groups wrap in what SORT leaves them, and SORT keeps the top right. A row of one group hugs it: SAVE PATTERN AS's KEEP, NamePopup's options under optionsLabel . A page's toolbar rows too: the SONG page's top bar (its title, SWITCH, PLAYS), its section and song rows, the pattern toolbars. So a dialog reads in rows and groups at a glance, as a page does, and a wrapping row never leaves a lone chip on a line of its own. Checked: dialog-groups-on-bands (a GroupLabel in a *Popup.qml outside a ToolStrip); one band per row is the reviewer's to see.

One ✕, the CloseButton , everywhere. A dialog gets it from DialogHeader ; a full page puts it at the end of its header's first row. Checked: close-is-closebutton . A view under the header has no ✕ (the SONG page, the MIXER): the header stays on screen, and the control that opened the view closes it (the project plate, ✱), as BACK does. No CLOSE / CANCEL / DONE buttons: the ✕ and BACK already leave. A button that stops work under way (CANCEL an export) is an action, and a question's answers (NO / YES while pairing) are answers; both are listed as exceptions. Checked: no-close-text .

Every page wears a Chassis in its own finish. Checked: page-wears-chassis . A page that takes the whole window (MUSIC PLAYER, RECORDER) has a PageHeader like the dashboard's. Checked: full-page-has-header . Row 1: its transport, a HeaderPlate saying what's on, its own toggles, and the ✕. Row 2: its deck of grouped controls, on ToolStrip s. The view sits under it, on the Chassis . Its controls go on ToolStrip s by group, its work areas in Well s.
An empty list or view says why and what fills it, with an EmptyNote ("no recordings yet · ● REC records the input as played"), never a Text of its own. Checked: empty-says-why .

Every page has a finish of its own in Rave.qml ( Rave.machines , songFinish , playerFinish , recorderFinishes ): chassisTop , chassisBottom , rail , well , ink , dim , accent , glow , dark . A new one:

h: Palettes › Starts from a researched palette, not a guess
t: Starts from a researched palette, not a guess. Pick its family from a reference palette set: the Radix, Tailwind or Material colour scales, Adobe Color's or Coolors' tested schemes, or a brand's own. Then map its steps: Colour Step chassis 950–900, dark well one step darker than the chassis rail a mid step of the same hue ink 50 dim 400 accent 400–500, or its complement for contrast glow a lighter step of the accent - Is readable (WCAG 2.x contrast), against both chassis colours. Checked: palette-readable , which prints the ratios when it fails. - ink ≥ 7:1 (AAA body text); - dim ≥ 4.5:1 (AA text); - accent ≥ 3:1 (AA for non-text), on the chassis or the well it lights in. - Is distinct from the pages beside it: the player is violet, the RECORDER's inputs wine, amber and teal, the SONG page a matte slate night.

h: Text is translatable, keys are not
t: Every text a screen shows goes through i18nc , with a context ( Translations ). A key that's stored or compared stays English, and is translated where it's drawn: the Rave display helpers, with Rave.kli18nc to mark it. The device's printed key names and the product names stay as printed. Translations run longer , Spanish by about a third. ActionButton and Chip shrink their text to fit, down to 75 %, so give words room and look at every new screen in Spanish. Checked: text-translatable , a text: given a literal string without i18n… , outside the keep list in tools/ui-rules.json.

Write it here, under its heading, with why. Add it to tools/ui-rules.json : a pattern (a regex no QML may match) or a check (a function in tools/check-ui.py , registered in CHECKS ), with the files allowed to break it and why. A known breach still to fix is allowed with "migrate": true : it shows as a warning, and the list only ever shrinks. Run python3 tools/check-ui.py --verbose ; fix what it finds or list it.

The recipes for growing ravving. Read architecture.md first for the layers; this is the how-to. The code rules hold throughout: reuse a part before writing a new one; keep each class to one job; give every public API its QDoc block in the .cpp ( writing-code-docs.md ); give every non-obvious line an inline comment that says why.
The drums and the bass share everything except what is specific to them. A new machine (CHORDS, LEAD, SAMPLER) follows the same path.

In src/backend/machine.h . It inherits the pattern, bars, presets, level, pan, pause, mute, effects, LIVE play and STEP entry. Implement: onAttached() : write the machine's own state into its libzynthbox pattern; refresh() : publish the bar on screen to QML (its own Q_PROPERTYs + stepsChanged ); revoice() : rewrite every step's velocity (mute/solo/kick modes changed); clearOwnSteps() , applyChart(chart) , chart() : its preset format (a chart is a map of strings, one character per step, so preset files stay readable); placeHit(position, key, accented) , liveNotes(key) , liveVelocity(key, accented) : what a live key writes and plays (a list of notes: one for a row or a mono note, a whole chord for ChordMachine). Saving and opening state() : everything it keeps (call Machine::state() and add to it: its steps, kit, sound…); a project file is exactly this, so it must be complete; restoreContent(state) : take that back while running (opening a project) and write the pattern. An empty state means its defaults: the default preset, kit and sound. In a state, a missing key means "default", and a present but empty one means "empty", so a cleared pattern stays cleared. Call restoreContent from the constructor too, so start-up and opening share one path, as MonoMachine and ChordMachine do. Write steps through addSubnote / setSubnoteMetadata : velocity −1 is silent, and the duration is in pattern ticks via stepTicks() . Call markEdited() after a user change.

an entry in kits.json's machines : key , kind , track , zynthianChannel , engine , sound , presets , defaultPreset , baseNote … Tracks and channels must be unused. a presets file, data/<machine>-presets.json ( {presets: [{name, genre, chart}]} ), installed by CMakeLists.txt. A new instance of an existing kind, like another mono synth, needs nothing else in C++.

In studio.cpp 's loadKits() , a new kind is one more kind == branch creating it. addMachine() then wires it up generically ( attachMachine() ): saving, ❚❚, the track lane, sends, the engine, DRIVE, SOUND MODIFIERS and expressions. It appears as studio.machines.<key> .

Like MonoMachinePanel.qml and ChordMachinePanel.qml , with the toolbar and editor as children. Override what MachinePanel declares: stepLeds , and liveKeyDown/Up : what pads do while LIVE; stepKey , and moveSelection(dy) : ▲ ▼ in the editor, false at the edge; keyForNote / padForKey : what a keyboard note plays and which pad lights. Light live notes from heldKeys .
A MachinePage declaring its panel (see pages/ChordsPage.qml ); it forwards the device and an external keyboard to it.

Add the C++ files to src/backend/CMakeLists.txt and the QML files to src/CMakeLists.txt ( RAVVING_QML_FILES ). Add a screenshot step in src/main.cpp , and the machine to Rave.machines , with its finish colours as strings.

Engines are SoundEngine subclasses ( soundengine.h ): start() , reconfigure(config) , midiInputPort() , audioOutputPorts() (left, right), optional setControl(symbol, value) , and the started signal. SoundEngine::createEngine() picks one by the type of the kits.json engine object: "jalv" ( JalvEngine ): any LV2 instrument , e.g. {"type": "jalv", "uri": "http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi", "controls": {"volume": 75}} . Ports and control indexes come from lv2info (cached per URI); a mono output is sent to both sides. Nothing else is needed for a new LV2 synth. "fluidsynth" ( FluidSynthEngine ): soundfonts (the drum kits). A new kind (setBfree, sfizz, a sampler…) is one more subclass run through ConsoleProcess (libzynthbox's ProcessWrapper: restarted on a crash, startup commands, a console prompt) and one more type in createEngine() . Choose an engine by measuring it first ( debugging.md : synthprobe/analyse): velocity response, glide, CPU ( top ), level.

h: SOUND MODIFIERS: an engine's own controls
t: A machine's SOUND MODIFIERS are data: its sound in kits.json, which Machine turns into a SoundControls ( machine.sound ). Cards of knobs, each driving an engine port by its LV2 symbol, a 0..1 knob mapped onto min..max (linearly, or "curve": "log" for ports the engine treats as logarithmic), with a 0..1 default: "sound": [ { "title": "FILTER", "knobs": [ { "name": "CUTOFF", "symbol": "cutoff", "min": 300, "max": 9000, "curve": "log", "default": 0.55 } ] }, { "title": "TONE", "knobs": [ { "name": "WAVE", "default": 0, "choices": [ { "label": "SAW", "controls": { "osc1waveform": 0, "osc1pw": 0.5 } }, { "label": "JUNO", "controls": { "osc1waveform": 0.5, "osc1pw": 0.75 } } ] } ] } ] A knob with choices is a switch: its value snaps to choice i of n at i / (n − 1). It shows as a WaveCycler , which draws SAW, SQR, TRI and SIN. Each choice sets its controls (several ports; give every choice the same ports) or a value for the knob's symbol . Ports with no knob go in engine.controls . A live control a page plays , like the ribbon's vibrato, is an expression : "expressions": {"vibrato": {"symbol": "lfo2pitch", "max": 60}} , played with machine.setExpression("vibrato", amount) .

h: Get the ports right from the mods
t: Every engine Zynthbox ships has an engine mod whose docs/RESEARCH.md decodes its ports from the engine's own source: which ports are logarithmic; how enums quantise (TAL: i / den , rounded, 1-based); which envelope drives what (Calf: EG1 → cutoff, EG2 → amp); what a port called volume really does. Read it before writing a machine's engine.controls and sound , and record what ravving relies on in engines.md . Read a plugin's port ranges with lv2info , and check what the numbers mean in its source: an LV2 range isn't always the unit its own GUI shows. Studio connects the controls to the engine, and sends them all whenever it starts or restarts. The values are saved with the machine.

On the track lane (EQ, COMPRESSOR, SIDECHAIN, PAN): an entry in EffectChain::effects() (name, knobs, defaults, shared or per machine) and its mapping in TrackEffects::apply() onto the JackPassthrough lane's properties. An insert (DRIVE): a JalvPlugin per machine, created in Studio::attachMachine() . It goes to TrackEffects , which maps the knobs onto its controls and starts it on first use, and to JackWiring::addSynth(…, insert) . TrackEffects::driveSwitched → JackWiring::setInsertActive() puts it in the path only while it's on, so the dry sound never depends on the extra process. Calibrate its gain staging with lv2probe.sh . A send (REVERB, DELAY): one shared JalvPlugin in GlobalEffects , fed from every lane's wet outputs ( JackWiring::addSends ) and returned with addEffectReturn . On the master (LIVE FX: CRUSH, PHASER, STUTTER/LOOP): LiveFx and JackWiring::setMasterInserts , which takes any AudioInsert . Your own DSP (BeatRepeat): an AudioInsert subclass opening its own JACK client (libjack, linked through pkg-config; PipeWire's at run time). Keep the process callback lock-free: atomics from the GUI thread, buffers allocated in the constructor, no Qt calls. For musical timing, ZynthboxBridge::timerTickAtFrame(jack_frame_time()) gives the transport position sample-accurately.

Handle keys with the Hardware attached property (like Keys ); an unaccepted event bubbles to the parent. See architecture.md for the signal list. A machine's vertical order (strip → SOUND MODIFIERS → editor → SOUND EFFECTS) lives in MachineModule : pages only call focusUp() / focusDown() at their editor's edge. Knob-driven controls go in a KnobGroup (targets need value , from , to , knobStep , fineStep , knobBadge , knobPending : RaveKnob , RaveFader , WaveCycler have them). Menus: RaveComboBox (drop-downs) and ChoicePopup (grids: kits, presets) already take the arrows, the big knob, SELECT and BACK, and hand the focus back on close.

Build clean, with no warnings. Run the desktop screenshots, with no QML warnings. Deploy, and check on the device: a screenshot and a measurement. Update the docs this change touches, and the webpage's features or shortcuts. Rebuild the site's pages, then commit. A gotcha met on the way goes to notes/ for the maintainers, not into these docs. A change the user can undo goes through the project's history: see "The undo history" in architecture.md .

h: Reporting a problem to the issues center
t: Every component owns a check pass: at start, and whenever something fails or recovers, it tells the center ( src/backend/diagnostics.h ): #include "diagnostics.h" Issues::report(QStringLiteral("wiring"), QStringLiteral("sound"), QStringLiteral("warning"), QStringLiteral("Some audio connections are missing"), // the title, the user's words QStringLiteral("some ports never appeared…"), // the detail: what was seen QStringLiteral("Pick the sound again, or restart ravving."), // what to do QStringLiteral("restart")); // an action button, or "" Issues::clear(QStringLiteral("wiring")); // once it works again Rules: A stable id per problem. Reporting it again updates it and counts it. The level: error when something doesn't work, warning when it works worse or will stop, and notice for what's worth knowing, like a desktop without device keys. Always a suggestion the user can follow. Clear it from the same place that would see it recovered. A library's stderr line can become an issue through StderrWatch 's pattern table (src/stderrwatch.cpp). tools/issues-test.sh exercises the center over the fifo.

How to write the pages people read: the manual, the webpage's FEATURES and SHORTCUTS, and the README. The rules come from plain-language and documentation research (sources at the end); tools/check-guide-style.py checks the ones a script can measure.
Talk to the reader. Write "you", in the active voice: "Hold the step key for half a second and it latches." Not "a step key held past half a second latches its pad".
Easygoing, not vague. Friendly and relaxed, with the right musical terms as musicians say them: bar, beat, swing, quantise, root, scale, velocity, accent, cutoff, envelope, send.

h: Voice › Only what the app does
t: Only what the app does. Check every term and claim against the code or the API reference before writing it. No guessing, no comparisons from the requests that created a feature, no design references, no history, no internal names (classes, files, PipeWire, JACK).

Concrete, concise, familiar words. "Hold the key for half a second", not "sustain the input briefly". Plain everyday words over jargon; a musical term only where it is the right one. No filler ("simply", "just", "very", "in order to").
Inclusive and constructive. Gender-neutral (you, they), and phrased to help: say what to do ("Tap LOCK to edit while it plays") rather than what went wrong.

Casual on purpose. Writing courses prefer formal language for academic texts; these pages are not academic, so they stay relaxed and friendly, never sloppy. On-screen names as the screen shows them , in capitals (SELECT, LOCK, SOUND EFFECTS), and the device's keys as printed (MENU, ALT, MODE, BACK, PLAY, STOP).
Focus and unity. Each section and each paragraph is about one thing, and every sentence in it serves that thing. A sentence that belongs elsewhere moves there.

h: Organisation › Pick the order that fits the content
t: Pick the order that fits the content. Steps and anything that happens over time go in time order (first, then, finally). Features and options go in order of importance: what most people need first, special cases last. The screen or the device's front panel is described in space order (top to bottom, left to right).

One page per job. Keep the four kinds apart: a first walk-through (learning), how to do one thing (a task), what every key or knob does (reference), and why it works this way (explanation). Link between them instead of mixing them in one section.
Start from what the reader wants to do , not from the screen's layout: "Move notes after you've written them", not "The SELECT button".

h: Headings and order › Most important first
t: Most important first. The first sentence of a section says what it is for; details and exceptions come after.

h: Headings and order › A heading every 100–200 words
t: A heading every 100–200 words. Readers scan the headings and the left edge of the text. So make each heading say what the section does ("Save your project"). Start paragraphs and list items with the words that carry the meaning.

h: Paragraphs and sentences › One idea per paragraph, one to three sentences
t: One idea per paragraph, one to three sentences. A paragraph over about 60 words wants a list, a table or a split.

h: Paragraphs and sentences › One idea per sentence, about 20 words, never over 35
t: One idea per sentence, about 20 words, never over 35. A semicolon chain or a third parenthesis is a sign to split.

h: Paragraphs and sentences › Link the sentences
t: Link the sentences. Each one follows from the last: repeat the key word, or use a signal word that says how it connects. Time: "first", "then", "finally". Adding: "also". An example: "for example". A contrast: "but", "instead". Place on the screen: "above", "below", "at the right". A list keeps its items the same shape.

h: Paragraphs and sentences › Short paragraphs on purpose
t: Short paragraphs on purpose. Writing courses ask four sentences or more of an essay paragraph. A manual on a screen is scanned instead, so its paragraphs stay at one to three sentences, and lists, tables and the next heading carry the rest.

Steps are numbered , one action each, starting with a verb, and say what happens: "1. Tap LOCK. The grids accept edits again." Parallel facts are a bulleted list , each item bold on its first words when the list is long. Keys, knobs and settings are a table : what you press, what it does, its range.

h: Lists, steps and tables › No more than one level of nesting
t: No more than one level of nesting.
Lines of 50–75 characters. The docs column is capped at 70ch.
White space between blocks. Short paragraphs, a blank line before and after lists and tables. Screenshots only where they help a step , and retaken when the screen changes.

Grammar, punctuation and spelling are part of being trusted. Before committing a page: Proofread it once for meaning and once for typos. Read it aloud: a sentence you run out of breath on is too long. Run the spelling pass (below) when a British English dictionary is installed: ravving's pages spell British (colour, quantise, organise).

python3 tools/check-guide-style.py reports, for the user pages: sentences over 35 words, paragraphs over 60 words, sections over 200 words without a heading, and lines that chain more than two semicolons. Run it before committing a guide page. --spell adds a spelling pass with hunspell's en_GB dictionary (install hunspell-en_gb ), skipping code, key names and words in capitals.

Federal Plain Language Guidelines and the archived plainlanguage.gov quick tips : "you", active voice, sentences around 20 words, short sections, many useful headings. Australian Government Style Manual: plain language . Nielsen Norman Group's eye-tracking work on scanning, as summarised by Newcastle University's readability guidance and UXPin : most readers scan; headings and the left edge carry the page. Diátaxis, as adopted by Canonical : tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanation kept apart. Google developer documentation style guide: procedures : numbered steps, an imperative introduction, shallow nesting. How to format a blog post for readability and I'd Rather Be Writing : lines of 50–75 characters, white space, paragraphs of one to three sentences. The properties of a well-written text, as taught in writing courses: the Quizlet study guide "Key Properties of a Well-Written Text" and an overview . Organisation: focus, unity, development and patterns. Coherence and cohesion: signal words of time, sequence, space, illustration and contrast. Language use: concrete, concise, familiar and inclusive words. Mechanics: proofreading, reading aloud, grammar and spell checkers.

ravving's C++ is documented with QDoc, Qt's own documentation tool: the app in src/ , the backend library in src/backend/ , and the setup program in setup/ . It's published as the API reference beside these pages, in site/api/ , generated by tools/build-api-docs.py . The QML in qml/ is not documented there yet: it moves into plugin base types first.

h: What to write › Document with QDoc
t: Document with QDoc. Every public item has a /*! ... */ block: a class, struct or namespace: \class ( \struct , \namespace ), \inmodule Ravving , its \ingroup and a \brief ; a Q_PROPERTY: a \property block; a public method, slot, Q_INVOKABLE or signal: a block; a public enum: an \enum block, with a \value for each value. Be concise, precise and technical about what the current code does: its inputs and outputs; units: dB or linear gain, milliseconds or seconds, steps or ticks, 0..1; ranges and clamping; the thread it runs on: the GUI thread, the audio thread, a worker; who owns what it hands out, its invariants, and its side effects (what it saves, emits, starts).

Never write history or AI-style context , in a QDoc block or in any // comment: no used to , was changed , previously , no longer , or now X instead of Y ; no dates ( found 2026-10-12 ), no the user asked , no story of a past bug or of why something changed; no bug report numbers, on milo , or measured on / measured with ; no paths to docs or notes pages; no lineage ( the way zynthbox-qml does , as easyrave's… , ported from ), and no wording from the request that created a feature. Keep a zynthbox-qml or libzynthbox reference only as a contract the code depends on.

A // comment is welcome when it explains a non-obvious technical reason that's true of the code as it is: "muted rather than unlinked, so the jacks' sink keeps clocking the graph". A measurement that justifies a constant is a fact, and may stay, stated plainly: "30 %: the lowest still readable in a lit room".

h: Comments, overviews and commits › A class overview describes the class, not the screen
t: A class overview describes the class, not the screen. No pages, dialogs, rows, toasts, toolbars or "on screen" in a \class block. What QML sees is its context property, and the meaning of its properties and signals. Every new or changed C++ API comes with its QDoc in the same commit. Run python3 tools/build-api-docs.py so site/api/ follows; it's committed, like site/docs/ . ctest checks both (below).

The documentation lives in the .cpp files, next to the definitions, as Qt's own sources have it; the headers hold the declarations and short // notes on private members only. A block right before a function's definition documents that function. Parameters are named with \a , every one of them (QDoc warns about a missing one), and a function that returns something says so with "Returns". What has no definition in the .cpp gets a block anywhere in the .cpp , with \fn and the full signature, or \variable . That's a signal, a pure virtual, an inline function in the header, or a static constant. The class's own block, its \property , \enum and \fn blocks go together after the includes. When the definition's parameter names differ from the header's, start the block with the \fn signature as the header has it, so \a names what the reader sees. A header with no .cpp of its own ( audioinsert.h , zbcall.h , filesuffixes.h ) is documented in doc/src/header-only.qdoc ; the header says so in one line. Overrides of Qt's virtuals ( rowCount() , data() , paint() ) and of ravving's own base classes are \reimp , with a line on what this one adds when it adds something. /*! \class History \inmodule Ravving \ingroup ravving-studio \brief The project's undo history, published to QML as \c studio.history. Participants register once with add() and report each change with record(). ... */ /*! \property History::undoText \brief the name of the step undo() would undo; empty when there is none. */ /*! \fn void History::undone(const QString &what) Emitted after undo() went back over a step; \a what is its name. */ /*! Registers \a participant. Its state now is where its history starts. The participant must outlive the history or be removed with remove() first. */ void History::add(HistoryParticipant *participant)

A property's \brief is a noun phrase that QDoc puts after "This property holds": "the name of...", "whether ...". The groups ( \ingroup ) are the areas of the reference's landing page: ravving-app , ravving-studio , ravving-machines , ravving-engines , ravving-audio , ravving-system , ravving-setup (defined in doc/src/index.qdoc ).

python3 tools/check-cpp-docs.py (ctest cpp-docs ): It finds every public class, struct, namespace, property, method, signal, enum and free function that the headers of src/ and setup/ declare, and fails on any without a QDoc block. A documented property's READ, WRITE and NOTIFY members, destructors and deleted functions are exempt. It also reads every comment of src/**/*.cpp|h and setup/ for history: dates, used to , previously , no longer , any more , was changed / replaced / removed , now X instead of Y , the user asked , found on ... , fixed in , regression and the like. The list is BANNED in the script. --rule api or --rule comments runs one rule; --list prints every entity with its state. python3 tools/check-docs-history.py (ctest docs-history ) applies the same list to the published docs and the webpage, outside code spans. python3 tools/build-api-docs.py --check (ctest api-docs-current ) generates the reference into a temporary folder. It fails when QDoc prints a warning (an undocumented parameter, a link to nothing, an \fn that matches no declaration), or when site/api/ differs. It's skipped (exit 77) where no Qt 6 qdoc is installed, or when another qdoc version made the committed pages ( site/api/qdoc-version.txt ).

python3 tools/build-api-docs.py # site/api/, from doc/ravving.qdocconf python3 tools/build-api-docs.py --check # what ctest runs It needs Qt 6's qdoc (Arch: qt6-tools ; Debian: qdoc-qt6 ). It uses the first that reports a 6.x version: $QDOC , then Qt 6's host bin or libexec folder ( qmake6 -query ), then qdoc6 or qdoc on the PATH. /usr/bin/qdoc is Qt 5's on some systems. QDoc parses the headers with clang, so the include paths of Qt, KF6 (KI18n, BluezQt), JACK and the project go in a generated cxx-includes.qdocconf . Without them, a class page silently loses its members. doc/ ravving.qdocconf the project: sources, headers, the include paths global/ravving.qdocconf shared settings (warnings, the template) global/html-ravving.qdocconf the page chrome: the webpage's top bar, the sidebar, the footer global/style/ravving.css the theme: site.css's tokens and fonts, a light and a dark mode global/ravving-api.js the theme switch, the sidebar (nav.js) and the search (search.js) src/index.qdoc the landing page and the class groups src/header-only.qdoc the header-only classes and functions The generator: runs QDoc; wraps each documented member in a box, since QDoc writes them as loose siblings; writes nav.js (the sidebar: the classes by area) and search.js (every class, property, function, signal and enum) from QDoc's index file; copies the script beside the pages. The pages reach the webpage's fonts and wordmarks through ../assets/ , so site/api/ works on the public page and on the copy the device serves alike.
Everything ravving builds on comes from the device. Nothing is bundled, by the AppImage either.

The Zynthbox QtQuick Controls style ( qml-style-zynthbox ), picked by name in main.cpp . There's no build-time check: a missing style shows the Basic look and unthemed controls. io.zynthbox.ui (ZUI, from qml-module-zynthbox ), which that style imports. Button, CheckBox, Switch, Menu and TextField read their theme from it. The KDE Frameworks the style draws with: Kirigami, KSvg, Plasma.

h: The engine and the build order
t: The audio engine comes from libzynthbox ( io.zynthbox.components ) and zyncoder , both loaded at run time. So the order is: libzynthbox + zyncoder, qml-module-zynthbox, qml-style-zynthbox, then ravving. On a stock Zynthbox, these are the installed libzynthbox , qml-module-zynthbox and qml-style-zynthbox packages. A rebuilt module or style must be installed before ravving is tried.

The music player plays through Qt Multimedia : qt6-multimedia-dev to build, and libqt6multimedia6 with its FFmpeg plugin at run time, both on the image. Its sound goes out through PulseAudio, so ravving's service wants pipewire-pulse.service , which a Zynthbox has but leaves off. The player's stream runs at its own adapted quantum, and leaves the graph at 256 frames, 48 kHz. The exports use TagLib ( libtag1-dev ), zlib , and libsndfile with its FLAC, Vorbis and LAME encoders.

The sound comes from programs and data the Zynthbox image ships. ravving starts and wires them at run time, and nothing bundles them: jalv , the LV2 host, with the LV2 plugins the machines and effects name by URI in data/kits.json and src/backend/ : TAL NoiseMaker, DISTRHO Nekobi, Calf Monosynth, Calf Crusher and Phaser, Dragonfly Room Reverb, TAP Echo. tools/lv2probe.sh checks a URI on the device. FluidSynth 2 , for the drum kits and the soundfont sound sources. The soundfonts under /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts : the SFZ Drum Machines kits, and SF2 Instruments with FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 and ACBass.sf3 . PipeWire's JACK ( pw-jack ), with Zynthbox's MIDI routing (ZLRouter, a2j). A machine whose plugin or soundfont is missing starts silent, and says so in the journal. engines.md has what each engine does and expects.

On the device (Debian 13 arm64, as a Zynthbox image is) the build needs, by Debian name: For Packages the toolchain cmake , ninja-build , g++ , pkg-config Qt 6 (Core, Gui, Qml, Quick, QuickControls2, Concurrent, Network, DBus, Multimedia) qt6-base-dev , qt6-declarative-dev , qt6-multimedia-dev Bluetooth (KDE's BluezQt over BlueZ's D-Bus API) libkf6bluezqt-dev the audio processors and the graph probe (JACK's API; PipeWire's library at run time) libjack-jackd2-dev exports: the audio files, their tags, the .ravv bundles libsndfile1-dev , libtag-dev (TagLib 2; libtag1-dev on older images), zlib1g-dev the tools ( tools/*.py ) and syncing a checkout python3 , rsync Everything else ravving needs, it finds at run time on a stock Zynthbox: libzynthbox and zyncoder; qml-module-zynthbox and qml-style-zynthbox , with the KDE Frameworks they draw with (Kirigami, KSvg, Plasma); libqt6multimedia6 , with its FFmpeg plugin; PipeWire, with pipewire-jack ( pw-jack ), pipewire-bin ( pw-loopback , pw-link , pw-dump , pw-top ) and pipewire-pulse (left off by the image; ravving's service wants it); udisks2 and util-linux , for USB sticks ( udisksctl , lsblk ); jalv with the LV2 plugins, and FluidSynth with the soundfonts named below. Bluetooth needs three packages the image lacks, bluez-obexd , libspa-0.2-bluetooth and libkf6bluezqt6 , plus two drop-ins ravving installs. tools/bluetooth-setup.sh does all of it ( packaging.md , "Bluetooth on a fresh device"). tools/device.sh deploy # from the laptop: sync, build, install, restart, wait # or by hand (rsync without -a: older laptop mtimes would make ninja skip changed files) rsync -rlp --checksum --exclude build --exclude .git ./ root@milo.local:/root/ravving/ ssh root@milo.local cd /root/ravving cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr cmake --build build && cmake --install build systemctl --user daemon-reload systemctl --user start ravving # try it once: stops zynthbox-qml (the services conflict) systemctl --user start zynthbox-qml # and back To make ravving the device's UI (it starts at boot, and zynthbox-qml is masked so nothing brings it back), and to return to stock Zynthbox with nothing of ravving left in systemd: /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh ravving /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh zynthbox # add --purge to uninstall ravving too /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh status From the laptop, tools/device.sh default ravving|zynthbox|status does the same. default-app.sh run ravving|zynthbox switches for the session only (the boot default stays), which is what ravving's own menu offers under POWER → ZYNTHBOX.

The QML is compiled into the binary (the Ravving QML module: qmlcachegen bytecode and C++ for typed bindings), so a QML change is a rebuild like any other, and QML errors show at build time. To try QML on the device without rebuilding, copy the qml/ folder over and start ravving with RAVVING_QML_DIR pointing at it.

cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_STYLE=Basic ./build/ravving # or straight from the source tree's QML, no rebuild between QML edits: RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_STYLE=Basic RAVVING_QML_DIR=$PWD/qml ./build/ravving On a desktop without a terminal, Qt logs to journald; add QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 to see QML warnings. Keys send the same events as the device: Key Device 1 – 5 the number keys q w e r t y u i a s d f g h j k the 16 step keys arrows, Enter , Esc arrows, SELECT, BACK Space , Backspace , o , m play, stop, metronome, MENU z / x , c / v , b / n knobs 1–3, down and up , / . the big knob

Variable Effect RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 windowed instead of fullscreen RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 skip libzynthbox (UI only) RAVVING_STYLE Quick Controls style (default Zynthbox ) RAVVING_QML_DIR read the QML from this folder (a source tree's qml/ ) instead of the copy compiled in RAVVING_DATA_DIR read kits.json and the theme ( plasma/desktoptheme/ ) from this folder (desktop: $PWD/data ; the plasmarc then comes from build/config/ ) RAVVING_HOME one folder for everything ravving writes ( config/ , state/ , cache/ , library/ ), for a sandboxed run RAVVING_LIBRARY the library alone (projects, presets, samples, recordings) somewhere else RAVVING_PROJECT_DIR the session folder alone (default ~/.local/state/ravving ) RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR capture every page to PNGs there, then quit RAVVING_GDB=1 (service) run under gdb, backtrace to the journal QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true" log every hardware event (CUIA, knobs) For the service, set them with systemctl --user set-environment NAME=value and clear them with unset-environment .

One CMake project, its targets each with the CMakeLists.txt of their sources (the source files themselves are where they were: the split is of the CMake files only): File Owns CMakeLists.txt the project: version, C++ standard, AUTOMOC, qt_standard_project_setup , the dependencies ( find_package Qt6 / KF6BluezQt / ZLIB, pkg_check_modules jack / sndfile / taglib), RAVVING_DATA_INSTALL_DIR and RAVVING_THEME , the build options ( RAVVING_QML_AOT , RAVVING_PCH , RAVVING_TIME_TRACE , RAVVING_UNITY , RAVVING_IWYU , RAVVING_TESTS ) with ravving_build_settings(<target>) , their per-target side; the add_subdirectory calls; the generated files ( VERSION , config/plasmarc ) and the install rules of the project as a whole ( data/ , the theme, systemd and WirePlumber drop-ins, the desktop entry and icons) src/backend/CMakeLists.txt ravving_backend , the static backend library ( src/backend/* and src/zynthboxbridge.* ): its sources, its PUBLIC include directories ( src/ , so the app includes backend/xxx.h ; src/backend/ , so its files include each other bare), its PUBLIC link set (the Qt modules, JACK, sndfile, TagLib, zlib, BluezQt), the RAVVING_* compile definitions, the unity build src/CMakeLists.txt ravving , the app: src/*.cpp , the Ravving QML module over qml/ at the repository root (each file's path from there is its resource alias, so the resources stay qrc:/qt/qml/Ravving/qml/… and the module's qmldir stays at build/Ravving ), RAVVING_QML_AOT , the branding resources and the shaders, the link to ravving_backend , the binary's install rule; the binary itself stays at build/ravving setup/CMakeLists.txt ravving-setup , the AppImage's setup program ( build/setup/ravving-setup ) tests/CMakeLists.txt the laptop-side tests, built with -DRAVVING_TESTS=ON Target names, options, output paths and the install layout are those tools/device.sh , tools/build-appimage.sh , tools/static-analysis.sh and tools/build-profile.sh rely on; a new backend class goes into src/backend/CMakeLists.txt , a new QML file into src/CMakeLists.txt 's RAVVING_QML_FILES .

Folder Where What for Settings build/ laptop and device the development loop: tools/device.sh deploy , ctest RAVVING_QML_AOT=OFF , RAVVING_PCH=ON build-release/ device the Store AppImage ( tools/build-appimage.sh , configured there on each run) Release at -O2 (no debug information; binaries stripped at install), RAVVING_QML_AOT=ON , RAVVING_PCH=ON , prefix /usr The tools never remove either one: device.sh deploy syncs the source with --exclude '/build*' , so its --delete leaves both alone on the device; REMOVE RAVVING and the release check uninstall only what cmake --install put on the system; the AppImage build clears only its staging trees ( build-release/stage , build-release/appimage ). Keeping them is what keeps builds incremental.

The development build ( build/ ) compiles about twice as fast as the release build: the QML as bytecode only and the Qt headers precompiled. The device (a Pi 5, 4 cores) takes about as long as a 4-core laptop for the same work. RAVVING_QML_AOT (default ON). qmlcachegen compiles each QML file's bindings into C++, which then has to be compiled: on the Pi that is 40 % of a build. OFF keeps the QML precompiled but as bytecode only ( --only-bytecode ): the bindings run in Qt's interpreter and JIT, which is fine to develop with; a release keeps ON ( build-release/ ). RAVVING_PCH (default ON): the Qt headers nearly every file includes (QObject, QString, QVariant, the containers, QDebug, QJsonDocument…) parsed once instead of in each of ~90 files. ccache is used when it is installed ( CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER ): a file compiled before with the same flags comes from its cache (after a reconfigure, switching branches). The device builds at the lowest priority ( nice -n 19 ionice -c 3 in device.sh deploy ): not faster, but a build beside the music does not take the audio's time.

h: Where the backend lives › The backend is a library of its own
t: The backend is a library of its own. src/backend (and zynthboxbridge ) build as the static library ravving_backend , outside the QML module. A backend header edit recompiles no QML. Qt's type registration reads the metadata of every QObject class in the QML module's target. A backend header inside it would regenerate every QML file's compiled C++. QML reaches the backend through context properties ( studio , ravving …), which need no registration. The LOOP / SONG values of Sections are two numbers in Rave.qml ( Rave.sectionsLoop , Rave.sectionsSong ).

h: A corrupted ninja log rebuilds everything
t: ninja: warning: premature end of file; recovering means build/.ninja_deps was cut short (a build killed mid-run, two builds at once in one folder): ninja then trusts nothing it built and plans every step on every build. ninja -C build -t recompact , then one full build, puts it right. Never run two builds in one build folder; let a build finish rather than kill it.

tools/build-profile.sh [OUT_DIR] [-- cmake options] builds ravving from clean with clang and -ftime-trace ( RAVVING_TIME_TRACE ) in analysis/build-profile/build (never build/ ), then: analysis.txt , ClangBuildAnalyzer 's report: the slowest files to parse and to compile, the most expensive headers (where they come from, how often), the costliest template sets and functions; trace.json , ninjatracing over .ninja_log : the build's timeline, one lane per job. Open it in https://ui.perfetto.dev (or chrome://tracing) to see what holds the four cores up: moc's mocs_compilation.cpp , a slow file at the end, qmlcachegen's steps. The tools: clang (Arch's), ClangBuildAnalyzer and ninjatracing in ~/.local/bin (built from their git checkouts in ~/.local/src ), include-what-you-use from the AUR ( yay -S include-what-you-use ). include-what-you-use : cmake -B analysis/iwyu -DRAVVING_IWYU=ON -DRAVVING_PCH=OFF , then build ravving_backend there. Each file's compile prints what to add, what to remove, and which includes a forward declaration would replace ( analysis/iwyu.log ). Precompiled headers must be off, or it reports their includes as unused everywhere. Read it with care: it knows no Qt mapping, so it would swap <QVariantMap> for Qt's internal <qvariant.h> : ignore those; it doesn't see moc's generated code. So it calls a header unneeded where a Q_PROPERTY exposes a pointer to that class ( machine.h 's SoundControls and TrackEffects, devicecontrols.h 's Wifi). moc needs the complete type there.

RAVVING_UNITY is for measuring, not on by default. Many backend files define file-local constants with the same names ( MaxBars , AuditionMs …), which collide once a batch merges them. It covers the backend only. The app target carries qmlcachegen's and rcc's generated sources, and AUTOMOC's mocs_compilation.cpp stays out of the batches on its own.

site/ is the page ravving serves at http://<device>:8098/help/ (the shortcuts, the features and the documentation; site/README.md says how it is made and how to retake a screenshot). It is installed as it is ( install(DIRECTORY site …) , this README left out), so it must be plain static files with relative references, and its documentation pages are generated into the repository: python3 tools/build-site-docs.py # guide/*.md, docs/*.md, data/secret/README.md → site/docs/*.html python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --list # the pages python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --plain # the script's own converter, as on a machine without python-markdown The same run writes site/docs/search.json , the index behind the SEARCH box in every docs page's sidebar: every section, with its heading and text. The search runs in the browser alone, so it works on the public page and on the device's own copy without internet. --check (the site-docs-current test) compares the pages and the index with what the markdown gives.

The user guide ( guide/ : Get ravving, The machines, Your first beat), the manual ( docs/manual-interim.md ), the developer docs ( docs/ ) and the packs page. The script never reads notes/ , guide/_material/ or .claude/ , and these tests keep the pages honest: docs-fences ( tools/check-docs-fences.py ): no page in PAGES lives in those folders, and no rendered page links or includes anything from them; docs-history ( tools/check-docs-history.py ): no page in PAGES, and not the webpage, tells history or carries the wording of the requests behind a feature. That's dates, used to , found on milo , the design reference's name…: tools/check-cpp-docs.py 's BANNED list and a few more. guide-style ( tools/check-guide-style.py --strict ): every published page, the README and the webpage follow writing-the-guide.md . guide-labels ( tools/check-guide-labels.py ): every on-screen name the guide and the manual quote exists on screen: in po/ravving.pot, the setup page, the nameplates, or tools/guide-labels.json. features-current ( tools/build-features.py --check ): the webpage's FEATURES are what data/features.json gives. Each feature links to one section that exists. The classes or QML files in its code still exist in site/api/ or qml/. Edit the JSON, then run the script without --check to rewrite the page.

The page is public at https://ravving.github.io/. Run sh tools/publish-site.sh once site/ is committed: It copies site/ (this README left out) into a clone of the ravving/ravving.github.io repository, with the stylesheet and scripts versioned by content. It commits it under the source commit, and pushes. That repository's workflow deploys its own content as the Pages artifact on every push. Nothing there needs access to this repository, and no secret is kept anywhere. The rule ("The documentation rules", below): the docs and the page follow every change, in the same commit; python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --check (ctest site-docs-current ) fails when the rendered pages do not match the markdown. The C++ API reference is site/api/ , generated by QDoc from the sources' /*! */ blocks with python3 tools/build-api-docs.py (Qt 6's qdoc), and committed the same way. Its --check is ctest api-docs-current . writing-code-docs.md has the rules and the details. Run it after editing a doc and commit site/docs/ with the markdown. It uses python-markdown when it is installed (Arch python-markdown , Debian python3-markdown ) and its own small converter otherwise; PAGES in the script lists the documents, their groups and blurbs.

h: The documentation rules › The docs and the page follow every change
t: The docs and the page follow every change. A feature added, changed or removed isn't done until the same commit updates what says it: the developer docs ( docs/*.md ) it belongs in; the manual ( docs/manual-interim.md , until the user guide in guide/ replaces it); the page in site/ : the SHORTCUTS row of a key, or the FEATURES highlight or grouped item of a feature, translated through po-site/. Then run python3 tools/build-site-docs.py , push, and sh tools/publish-site.sh puts it at https://ravving.github.io/. The device's copy follows the next deploy. - The docs say what the code does now. No dates, no history, no measurements of the day, no traps met, and no wording from the requests behind a feature. Those go to notes/ for the maintainers; ctest -R docs-history enforces the phrases. - Every new or changed C++ API comes with its QDoc in the same commit ( writing-code-docs.md ; ctest -R cpp-docs , ctest -R api-docs-current ). - Every release has its translations reviewed ( translations.md ).

ravving reaches a device as an AppImage in the Store's Apps category, installed as the Store installs any app: The Store downloads the file into ~/.local/share/zynthbox/apps/<author>/<name>/ . It registers it with libappimage: a desktop entry in ~/.local/share/applications . It extracts it next to itself with --appimage-extract , as an <md5>.AppDir . From then on, zynthbox-qml launches that AppDir's AppRun when the entry is tapped. The bundle is for the Zynthbox device only . It's built on the device, for its architecture, against the Qt, libzynthbox, zyncoder and Zynthbox QML modules the device already has. So it bundles no libraries at all: just ravving, the setup program and the data. The device must have, as every stock Zynthbox does: qml-style-zynthbox , the Zynthbox QtQuick Controls style ravving selects at startup; qml-module-zynthbox , which it imports ( io.zynthbox.ui ). building.md , "What ravving is made of", has the whole chain. What the AppImage starts isn't ravving but ravving-setup ( setup/ ): a page over zynthbox-qml that installs ravving from the bundle and picks which UI the device runs.

The bundle carries no libraries, so what ravving needs from the device is listed in one place, data/requirements.json (installed with the data, and in the bundle), and checked twice: The setup page, before installing ( default-app.sh deps DIR [--install] [--json] , which runs check-requirements.py from the bundle). It checks every requirement, and every library the bundle's ravving links to ( ldd 's "not found"). The page lists what's missing, the feature each costs, and the Debian package that brings it, with INSTALL MISSING PACKAGES (apt-get, online). A startup requirement or library missing means ravving can't start there. TRY IT and MAKE IT THE DEFAULT stay dimmed, and the list says why. ravving, once started ( Requirements , four seconds after the first frame). It checks the feature requirements by files and programs only: no process, microseconds. Each missing one is a warning in the issues centre, like "MUSIC PLAYER will not work", with what it costs and the package for the device's admins. What ravving needs that a Zynthbox image may not have: Needed for What How it gets there everything the Qt 6 Zynthbox style ( qt6/qml/Zynthbox ) and QML module ( io.zynthbox.ui ) not packaged yet : built from qml-style-zynthbox and qml-module-zynthbox's dev/qt6-port (the Debian packages are Qt 5) everything Qt Quick Shapes, Virtual Keyboard, Kirigami, KSvg (Qt 6 QML) qml6-module-qtquick-shapes , -virtualkeyboard , qml6-module-org-kde-kirigami , -ksvg starting at all libraries ravving links to: Qt 6 Multimedia, KF6 BluezQt, TagLib 2, LAME, Vorbis, libsndfile libqt6multimedia6 , libkf6bluezqt6 , libtag2 , … ( requirements.json "libraries") MUSIC PLAYER Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend libqt6multimedia6 BLUETOOTH speakers / SEND PipeWire's Bluetooth plugin, BlueZ's obexd libspa-0.2-bluetooth , bluez-obexd (and tools/bluetooth-setup.sh 's service steps) BLUETOOTH, INPUT ravving's WirePlumber settings (A2DP endpoints, one name per sound card) in the bundle ( etc/wireplumber/… ): install puts them in /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ , applied from the next start synths, effects, drums jalv, lv2info, FluidSynth, the LV2 plugins and soundfonts the Zynthbox image's own packages SAMPLE KING one-shots libzynthbox's fix for notes cutting each other (exclusivity group −1) a libzynthbox patch not in a stock libzynthbox: there a one-shot is cut when the next starts; not detectable from ravving Adding a feature that needs something new: add it to data/requirements.json (its files, programs, package, the feature and its effect), and to this table.

AppRun nx-apphub's launcher: exec usr/bin/ravving-setup ravving.desktop, ravving.png the entry the Store lists (Name "Ravving", the icon: a 256 × 256 PNG, .DirIcon also .DirIcon, from which libappimage makes the thumbnail zynthbox-qml's Apps grid shows; a PNG, since an SVG one renders blank) usr/bin/ravving the app usr/bin/ravving-setup the page the AppImage opens usr/share/ravving/ kits.json, engines.json, the presets, requirements.json, check-requirements.py, start.sh, default-app.sh, VERSION usr/share/applications, icons the desktop entry and icon, where they came from etc/systemd/user/ravving.service etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/50-ravving-*.conf Bluetooth, sound card names usr/bin/ravving , usr/share/ravving and the unit are exactly what cmake --install puts on the device: default-app.sh install DIR copies them from the bundle to the system paths.

Four choices, each a default-app.sh command on the bundle's own copy of the script (so the script always matches the files it installs): Choice What it runs Effect TRY IT (LAUNCH RAVVING once installed) install , then run ravving ravving now; Zynthbox at the next boot, or from ravving's POWER → ZYNTHBOX MAKE IT THE DEFAULT install , then ravving ravving at every boot (zynthbox-qml masked) ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN zynthbox zynthbox-qml at boot; ravving stays installed REMOVE RAVVING (press twice) zynthbox --purge the same, and ravving's program and data leave the system; projects, takes and recordings stay The cards above them come from default-app.sh status , re-read after every action: the installed version, what starts at boot, and what runs now. The two installing tiles read by what the device has: Installed The tile reads nothing "Install this bundle and …" another version "Update the installed X to this bundle's Y and …" this version "ravving Y is already installed: …", and the install step is skipped (TRY IT reads LAUNCH RAVVING) A tile that would change nothing is dimmed: MAKE IT THE DEFAULT while ravving already boots, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN while Zynthbox does, and REMOVE while nothing is installed. The AppImage itself stays in the Store's list until it's removed there. Switching stops the UI that's running, and everything it started: the setup page under zynthbox-qml, or the script itself under ravving's ZYNTHBOX button. So the script re-runs the switching commands in a transient unit of its own ( systemd-run --user --wait ), and only then touches the services. run APP switches for the session only. The boot default stays; a masked zynthbox-qml is unmasked for the start and masked again. ravving and zynthbox change what boots.

The builder is NX AppHub CLI ( nx-apphub-cli build ), the tool the Zynthbox kit's other apps use, driven by packaging/appimage/ravving.yml.in , modelled on the kit's vvave bundle (UriHerrera/storage, AppImages/vvave/app_arm64.yml ): deps is empty, so nothing is downloaded; the zbkit repo entry is the kit's and goes unused; our binaries get into the AppDir through the scripts/ folder next to the YAML, which nx-apphub copies into usr/bin before it looks for binarypath ; the data, desktop entry, icon and unit come from the install staging tree, through prebuild-commands ; binarypath and exec are ravving-setup : nx-apphub patches that binary's RPATH (with patchelf; the paths it adds do not exist in this bundle, which is harmless) and writes the AppRun for it; runtime: go (go-appimagetool, a type-2 AppImage that --appimage-extract understands). The tool is an AppImage itself and the device has no FUSE 2, so it runs with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 , and needs ARCH set because AppRun is a script. From the laptop: tools/device.sh appimage [OUT_DIR] # default OUT_DIR: the Store packages folder beside the repo syncs the source, and installs nx-apphub on the device if it's missing ( tools/install-nx-apphub.sh : patchelf and the Python dependencies from Debian, the CLI from its git checkout into a venv). Then it runs tools/build-appimage.sh there, and copies ravving-<version>-aarch64.AppImage back. On the device itself: cd /root/ravving && tools/build-appimage.sh dist
The version is project(ravving VERSION …) in CMakeLists.txt. It names the file, fills usr/share/ravving/VERSION and shows on the setup page.

Next to the AppImage, the Store listing wants an icon and a gallery: device.sh appimage also renders ravving-icon-512.png from data/icons/ravving.svg (the icon the bundle carries: the 808 plate, the big knob lit in the drums' orange over a step row) into the same output folder; device.sh gallery [OUT_DIR] screenshots each of the five pages of the ravving that is running on the device ( ravving-1-drums.png … ravving-5-sampler.png , 1280 × 800, by the number keys) into the Store packages folder's gallery/ ; pick three for the page. Load a project worth showing first: the shots are of whatever is on screen.

Every release has its translations reviewed: someone who reads the language reads what changed in po/ and po-site/ since the last release; the screenshot tour is taken in Spanish and Japanese; ctest -R translations-current passes: no fuzzy or untranslated text, every placeholder kept, the translated pages rendered. Translations has the steps.

Run it after any release-worthy change (a version bump, a change to the setup page, the scripts or the unit), from the laptop: tools/appimage-test.sh # build on the device, install like the Store, walk everything tools/appimage-test.sh --no-build # the AppImage already in the device's dist/ tools/appimage-test.sh --keep # leave the entry in the device's Apps list afterwards Run it on a freshly booted device. It switches between the two UIs six times in a few minutes. Several walks in a row can leave zynthbox-qml hung loading its sketchpad ("Starting engine …"): a Zynthbox and PipeWire wedge after many fast restarts, which only a reboot clears. It: builds the AppImage ( device.sh appimage ); installs it as the Store would ( tools/store-register.py install ): it registers with libappimage, extracts the AppDir, and points the desktop entry at its AppRun; checks the AppDir's contents; walks the page and ravving by touch, asserting default-app.sh status after each step: TRY IT from a purged system: ravving runs, installed is the bundle's version, /usr/bin/ravving is byte for byte the bundle's binary, the boot default is untouched; ravving's POWER → ZYNTHBOX: zynthbox-qml runs; MAKE IT THE DEFAULT: ravving runs and boots, zynthbox-qml is masked; ZYNTHBOX again: zynthbox-qml runs and stays masked for boot; ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN: zynthbox-qml boots, ravving still installed; REMOVE RAVVING twice, CLOSE: nothing of ravving left, the page gone.

The launch: tools/store-launch.sh starts the page in zynthbox-qml's own service cgroup, on the device's display. That's exactly a Store launch, so a switch that kills zynthbox-qml kills the page too, as in real use. The record: screenshots and the status after every step go to analysis/appimage-test-<date>/ . Eyeball the page shots for dimmed tiles and messages. Your data: the user's ravving settings ( ~/.config/ravving ) and live session ( ~/.local/state/ravving ) are copied aside before the walk's purge, and put back at the end, even after a failed step. The device's state is put back at the end: a dev install by cmake --install , or ravving as the boot default by default-app.sh ravving . The Store entry is removed, unless --keep . A failed assertion stops the run and prints the device's status. The device is then left mid-walk; tools/device.sh default zynthbox or ravving brings it back by hand.

h: Testing an AppImage without the Store
t: By hand on the device, the pieces the release check uses: tools/store-register.py install dist/ravving-0.3.0-aarch64.AppImage camiloh "Ravving 0.3.0" # → prints the AppDir; the entry shows in Apps at once tools/store-launch.sh "$APPDIR" # the page, as zynthbox-qml's Apps list would start it tools/store-register.py remove "~/.local/share/zynthbox/apps/camiloh/Ravving 0.3.0/ravving-0.3.0-aarch64.AppImage" store-register.py does what registerAppImage / unregisterAppImage in zynthbox-qml's zynthian_gui_main.py do, minus the UI. Or, in zynthbox-qml: SCREEN_MAIN_MENU ( tools/device.sh cuia ), tap Apps, tap Ravving. The page is touch only, and tools/device.sh tap X Y drives it. The tiles are the four quarters of the lower half: Tile X Y TRY IT 337 390 MAKE IT THE DEFAULT 943 390 ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN 337 600 REMOVE 943 600 CLOSE 1160 736 A desktop look without a device: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_BUNDLE_DIR=<a staged bundle> \ RAVVING_SETUP_SHOT=setup.png ./build/setup/ravving-setup

A stock Zynthbox (Debian 13, BlueZ 5.82, PipeWire 1.4, WirePlumber 0.5) cannot start bluetooth.service and registers no A2DP endpoints: Problem Cause Fix (shipped by ravving) bluetooth.service fails at boot (status 203/EXEC), the adapter stays DOWN, the control center says "its service is not running" zynthian-sys's drop-in /etc/systemd/system/bluetooth.service.d/01-disable-sap-plugin.conf starts /usr/lib/bluetooth/bluetoothd , which Debian 13 moved to /usr/libexec/bluetooth/ data/systemd/50-ravving-bluetoothd-path.conf , installed to the same drop-in folder: the same flags ( --compat --experimental --noplugin=sap ) with the path that exists a speaker or headphones pair but will not connect: org.bluez.Error.Failed br-connection-profile-unavailable ; the adapter's UUIDs ( bluetoothctl show ) list no Audio Source / Audio Sink WirePlumber's Bluetooth monitor ( monitors/bluez.lua ) waits for a logind "active" seat before creating the BlueZ handle that registers the A2DP endpoints; the root startx session never reports one, so the monitor never starts and BlueZ has nothing to connect the device to data/wireplumber/50-ravving-bluetooth.conf , installed to /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ : wireplumber.profiles.main.monitor.bluez.seat-monitoring = disabled no audio over Bluetooth at all libspa-0.2-bluetooth (PipeWire's A2DP / HFP plugin with the SBC, aptX, FastStream, LDAC codecs) is not installed apt install libspa-0.2-bluetooth , then a WirePlumber restart (it loads the plugin at start) no file transfer bluez-obexd (the OBEX daemon, obex.service in the user session, D-Bus activated as org.bluez.obex ) is not installed apt install bluez-obexd the Qt side ravving links KDE's BluezQt ( libkf6bluezqt6 , present on the image; libkf6bluezqt-dev to build) — tools/bluetooth-setup.sh does all of it on a device and checks every step ( --check only checks); cmake --install puts the two drop-ins in place as well. After the setup bluetoothctl show lists Audio Source, Audio Sink, Handsfree and Handsfree Audio Gateway. cmake --install puts ravving's two drop-ins in place. tools/bluetooth-setup.sh does the rest, and the setup program, or the AppImage's first start, should run it: the packages ( bluez-obexd , libspa-0.2-bluetooth , libkf6bluezqt6 ) and the service restarts. --check verifies it afterwards. After the setup, bluetoothctl show lists Audio Source, Audio Sink, Handsfree and Handsfree Audio Gateway. ravving's WirePlumber drop-in also sets: bluetooth.autoswitch-to-headset-profile = false , so recording from headphones never switches them to HFP; bluez5.enable-sbc-xq . One more setting is the device's own, set by hand on a new image, since BlueZ reads no drop-in folder: FastConnectable = true under [General] in /etc/bluetooth/main.conf . With it, a speaker or headphones paging the device connect within a fraction of a second.

The tools that drive, hear, measure and watch ravving on a Zynthbox, from the laptop. The pieces are small scripts in tools/ ; this page is the recipe book that strings them together. For the build loop see building.md ; for what each backend piece does, architecture.md ; for the device recipes and the code checks, debugging.md and quality.md . The rule for every test: iterate with a local build ( tools/device.sh deploy ), never the AppImage; the AppImage and its release check ( packaging.md ) are for minor releases.

Like zynthbox-qml, ravving reads CUIA commands from webconf's fifo ( echo cuia/SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED > /tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo ), and the call , get and set lines below; tools/device.sh writes them over ssh. Tool What it does tools/device.sh deploy rsync the source, build on the device, install, restart, wait until the audio is wired tools/device.sh cuia NAME… press device keys by CUIA name through the remote-control fifo ( SWITCH_NUMBER_5_RELEASED , SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED , SWITCH_STEP5_PRESSED + _RELEASED , SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED = LIVE, KNOB0_UP … KNOB3_DOWN , SWITCH_ALT_PRESSED / _RELEASED , SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED , SWITCH_STOP_RELEASED , SWITCH_BACK_RELEASED , SWITCH_SELECT_RELEASED ) (object names) a machine key, studio , ravving , input , take , or a dotted path into an object's properties: pads.kit , bass.sound ; any other name is a QML item's objectName ( padsModule , samplerModule , padsWaveEditor , samplerWaveEditor ): set padsModule modifiersExpanded true , call padsWaveEditor open 16 , set ravving currentPage 4 , set ravving samplerMachine 1 ; mouse is the MouseWatcher ( get mouse hasMouse ). QML items are found in the item tree (a page's items are visual children, not always QObject children), popups in the object tree. A QML function is called through the script engine, so its arguments arrive as plain numbers, booleans or text ( call chordsModule moveView 1 , call padsWaveEditor open 16 ); a C++ method gets its arguments converted to the parameter types tools/device.sh set OBJECT PROPERTY VALUE set a backend property ( set pads selectedPad 3 ); plain setters are not reachable by call , properties are tools/device.sh get OBJECT PROPERTY read a backend property ( get pads muted , get studio playing ): ravving logs it, the script reads it back tools/device.sh call OBJECT METHOD ARGS… call a backend method: a machine by its kits.json key ( pads , sampler , drums1 , bass , chords , lead ), studio , input , take , exporter , music (and music.library ), profile , drives (USB sticks: call drives eject /dev/sda1 ), usb (the USB page: call usb scan , call usb importEntry samples /media/root/EVS/x.wav , call usb exportEntry soundfonts /zynthian/…/x.sf2 ; usbPopup opens it: call controlCenter run usb ), bluetooth ( call bluetooth startDiscovery , get bluetooth devices , call bluetooth pair AA:BB:… , call bluetooth useAsOutput AA:BB:… true , call bluetooth sendFile AA:BB:… /path ), or a QML item by objectName ( window showPlayer true , window showRecorder true , exportPopup open , settingsPopup open , bluetoothPopup open , projectPicker open then projectPicker actionTriggered 4 for IMPORT (the index counts the dividers: NEW 0, TEMPLATES 1, IMPORT 2, SAVE AS NEW 4, EXPORT 6), playerPage , controlCenter ); any Q_INVOKABLE or slot, arguments converted ( call pads loadSample 0 /path.wav , call pads setFlag 0 looping true , call pads loadPreset "Boom Bap" , call input record , call input record true for a RECORDER take; set input.effects preset OVERDRIVE ; get input.tuner frequency ; call ravving setLogRules "ravving.cuia.debug=true" turns a log category on while running: each key, who took it and the focus chain), video ( set video countdown 0 , call video start / stop / toggle , get video state / lastFile / lastInfo , set video quality high ) and computer ( call computer setup HOST USER PASSWORD 22 , check , send /path , forget ), files (the FILES browser: get files kinds , call files entries videos , call files presetFile "pattern::bass-presets.json::My Bassline 1" ; filesPopup open , filesPopup showKind presets , filesPopup openFolder BASS : the drawer's dialogs open by script only once the MENU drawer has been shown since the start, so press MENU twice first); the journal logs each call tools/device.sh tap X Y a touch at a screen pixel (the panel is 1280 × 800); a hold is xdotool mousemove X Y mousedown 1; sleep 1; xdotool mouseup 1 over ssh with DISPLAY=:0 XAUTHORITY=/root/.Xauthority tools/device.sh shot FILE.png a screenshot, copied here (crop with ImageMagick to read details) tools/device.sh animations every running animation and repeating Timer, with its item, whether it is shown, its QML file and position: what keeps the window drawing (an idle screen should draw nothing) tools/audio-impact.sh [SECONDS] [idle\|playing\|both] what the screen, polls and watchers cost the sound: frames/s, CPU per thread group, realtime-thread page faults, xruns ( quality.md );
