idle presses nothing, so it is safe while someone plays tools/device.sh gallery [DIR] one screenshot per page tools/device.sh log [SECONDS] ravving's journal tools/device.sh bt [ADDR] [SINCE] / bt capture [SECONDS] [FILE] why a Bluetooth device does (not) connect or play, read-only (tools/bt-diagnose.sh: config, endpoints, codecs, the device's journal and a tally of failures), and an HCI trace with btmon while you connect it ( debugging.md ) tools/device.sh play FILE.mid play a MIDI file into ravving as an external keyboard ( tools/midifile.py makes one) tools/device.sh default … switch between ravving and zynthbox-qml, install, purge, status tools/meter.py (on the device: tools/device.sh tools copies it to /tmp ) pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py PORT --seconds 2 : RMS, brightness and crest of a JACK port tools/record.py , tools/analyse.py , tools/repeatcheck.py record ports to numpy, analyse, check periodicity tools/soundfont.py presets · ranges · render · categorise FILE… look inside an SF2 / SF3 before making it a kits.json sound source ( categorise --json proposes the entries, a category from the name and folder: Strings, Organ, Keys, Bass, Guitar, Winds, Voices, Synth, Alien for the drones, Drums, Other; mute fonts left out): its presets (bank:program), the key and velocity ranges of its zones (a velRange 0–0 font is mute everywhere: SynStrings, LaString, MelloString, Organ on the image), and an offline render of one chord through fluidsynth with the level every quarter second tools/mididump.py PORT SECONDS (on the device, pw-jack python3 ) what an engine really receives on a JACK MIDI port: notes, controllers, program changes, bends (the clock and ticks with --clock ) tools/profile-taps.sh , tools/qml-profile.sh , tools/boot-timing.sh responsiveness, QML profiling, start-up time ( quality.md ) tools/static-analysis.sh clang-tidy / clazy tools/pads-test.sh the PAD SAMPLER feature suite (below) tools/sections-test.sh SECTIONS heard: sections picked at random moments while the master records, tools/sections-test.py checks every 8th sounds once and on time, a change only on a bar line, a rest in whole bars (below) tools/bluetooth-setup.sh [--check] set a device up for Bluetooth (packages, the two drop-ins, services) and check every step ( packaging.md ) tools/soundfont-check.sh every soundfont kits.json uses, checked on the device: exists, can sound, the preset exists, a chord comes out offline ( quality.md ) tools/drums-test.sh the DRUMS page suite (60 checks: 55 on the device, 5 timing checks on the laptop from a recording of the lane): a new project starting clean on every page, the grid (toggle, accent, undo / redo, clear, bars, view bar, cursor and STEP entry), the kit (another loaded, reset), the row mix heard (mute, solo, level, accent, the machine's mute and pause), LIVE (a pad heard, hits recorded while playing), presets (save, load, remove), every SOUND EFFECT on and off with its knobs read back and DRIVE / COMPRESSOR / EQ / PAN heard, the kit's MODS, and tools/hits-timing.py (shared with the chords suite): every 8th within 12 ms, accents louder. It works in a project of its own and puts the previous one back tools/chords-test.sh the CHORDS page suite (54 checks: 50 on the device, 4 timing checks on the laptop): the key and chord sets (names follow ROOT and the set), the CHORDS view (chords, runs, undo / redo, clear), NOTES (toggle, a step's notes, custom voicings), SLOTS (arm, fill, bars, clear, the steps rebuilt), the octave, the sound source (a soundfont, back to TAL), heard (mute, pause, LIVE keys, a hit recorded), presets, every SOUND EFFECT with EQ / PAN / DRIVE heard, and hits-timing.py on two bars of piano stabs (every 8th within 20 ms) tools/video-test.sh the video recorder suite ( architecture.md , "Live recordings"): a recording over the fifo while playing, its MP4 (streams, starts, length, frame rate), the ring's dropped frames, the graph's xruns meanwhile, RECORD / STOP by the keys, the TIMER and its cancel, VIDEO off tools/share-test.sh [FILE] the phone share (SEND… → PHONE · QR CODE) with the laptop as the phone: the newest video (or FILE) offered over the fifo, its link fetched with curl and compared with the device's file (size, md5), a Range request → 206 of the right length, HEAD, a wrong token and the root → 404, the deliveries counted, the help page at /help/ (200 text/html, its CSS, a missing file and ../ → 404, not an attachment, not counted), the library's pages (openBrowse → the index, a kind's page, a DOWNLOAD link as an attachment, a wrong kind and token → 404, closeBrowse → 404), stop → the link 404 while the help page stays; runs on the laptop (it must reach the device's address, as a phone would) tools/computer-link-test.sh the computer link end to end against the device's own sshd (a throwaway local user as the computer): set-up with the password, the key installed, Downloads found, a wrong password told apart, a file sent, the key removed → refused tools/video-voice-check.sh the voice-over mix of a video: the transport playing, tools/tone.py's 1 kHz bursts into the tap's mic ports as the voice, the file measured second by second (the music DUCK dB quieter while the tone is on, the tone LIFT dB louder); DUCK=18 LIFT=0 for other settings; the device must be idle tools/video-sync-check.sh , tools/video-encode-impact.sh , tools/video-mic-check.sh the video sync mechanism alone; the encoder tiers' cost while playing; a recording with the RECORDER's mic heard and measured tools/export-test.sh the exports and music player suite (below): a project saved, changed and reopened, a short track export (WAV, then FLAC) checked to the sample, its tags and cover, a .ravv bundle and its import, the player's queue, playback, pause, seek and stop tools/examples/lofi-say-it.sh a whole project built by script ("Building a project by script", below): the recipe for making music over the fifo tools/appimage-test.sh , tools/store-register.py , tools/store-launch.sh the Store AppImage release check ( packaging.md ) Environment switches: QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true" (set with systemctl --user set-environment and a restart) logs every hardware event with whether it was accepted and the focus chain it travelled; ravving.midi.debug=true the MIDI input.

A machine's track after its effects is TrackPassthrough:Channel{track+1}-lane1-dryOutLeft . kits.json gives the track: Machine Track drums 0–2 bass, chords, lead 3, 4, 5 SAMPLE KING, PAD SAMPLER 6, 7 the input monitor 9 The master is GlobalPlayback:dryOutLeft . Always compare runs (silent, playing, silent again), never a single number: a track playing a beat is about 0.02–0.2 RMS, and silence is 0.0.

sh tools/pads-test.sh runs every PAD SAMPLER backend feature as a check on the device, and exits with the number of failures. Each line reads PASS, FAIL or SKIP, with the level measured. Playing: load, one-shot, NOTE ON, LOOP + latch + stopAll, MUTE, and the samplers' exclusivity. Editing: the pattern on both tracks, erase, halve and double, copy, and a card value. Recording and files: a take with SMART stop when a signal is present, and the folders. When: after any change to the machine, the wiring, the paths or libzynthbox. Add a check for every new feature. It needs the reference audio in the library, and a kick sample in the device's sketchpads.

sh tools/sections-test.sh , from the laptop, builds a test project on the device: DRUMS 1 alone, a bar of 8ths at 100 BPM, section A a kick, B a closed hat, and REST with DRUMS 1 resting. It records the master while A and B are picked 24 times at random moments, 0.6–2.6 s apart. Some land, and some are replaced before their bar. Then it picks A and REST in turn. tools/sections-test.py checks the recordings by their onsets, a kick dark and a hat bright: every 8th plays once: no gap near 600 ms, none under 200; on time: each onset within 15 ms of one grid fitted through them all; the sound changes only on an onset that begins a bar; the rests are whole bars from a bar line. What was open before is opened again, saved first if it had changes. Read the timing against the grid, not gap by gap. The detector reads a kick 2.7 ms early and a hat 3.0 ms late (each ±2.6 ms), so a gap across a change carries both errors.

sh tools/export-test.sh runs 27 checks of the exports and the music player on the device, against whatever project is open: The profile: the author fallback. A 2-bar WAV export: it starts busy, plays the transport and stops it. It lasts exactly 2 bars + 1 s at the project's tempo, to the sample, and is 24-bit at the engine's rate. Its metadata: the tags (python3-taglib reads them back), the cover PNG, and a sidecar saying the start was placed on the audio clock ( headFrom: clock ).

A 1-bar FLAC. A .ravv bundle: project.json, metadata.json, cover.png and the samples, with the zip's integrity checked by Python. It's imported as a new project, with its sample paths rewritten. The music player: the library lists the tracks, playNow sounds on the master (meter.py), the position moves, and pause, resume, seek, enqueue and stop work. It removes its "Export Test" files at the end: the exports, the imported project and its samples. A track export by hand over the fifo (JSON in one argument; no | inside): ssh root@milo.local "printf '%s\n' 'call|exporter|exportAudio|{\"title\":\"My Track\",\"artist\":\"Me\",\"format\":\"flac\",\"bars\":8,\"loops\":2,\"tail\":2}' > /tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo" tools/device.sh get exporter phase # preparing · recording · cutting · tagging · done tools/device.sh get exporter lastFile

On the laptop, every change of text: run sh tools/i18n-extract.sh , translate what it marks, then ctest -R translations-current . tools/check-translations.py checks the templates are current, the catalogs compile, nothing is untranslated or fuzzy, placeholders and markup are kept, and the translated pages are rendered. A language on the device: device.sh set localization language es ( ja , en , or empty for the system's), then run the page suites in it. A suite that reads a display text instead of a key fails there.

A project names what it plays instead of holding it: each instrument's sound source and factory sound, by name; its MODS knobs as "CARD/KNOB"; a drum kit or a sample by path; automation lanes by knob. A change to data/kits.json , data/engines.json or the device's files can leave a saved project pointing at nothing. It then opens on another sound, silently. Three checks catch it: On the laptop, every change: ctest -R projects runs tools/check-projects.py over data/demos against the repo's kits.json and engines.json (sources, MODS knobs, automation lanes, kit roles, sections and the song). Over the device's saved projects: tools/device.sh projects ( -v for every project) runs it on the device, against the installed data and files too. That's the kit soundfonts, the samples, imported soundfonts and the TAL factory sounds. An older take outside samples/takes/ is found there, as ravving finds it. Run it after a data change, and before a release.

The machines note what they couldn't resolve as they restore it ( ProjectCheck , Machine::checkSaved() ). Nothing is read twice, and nothing runs after. The issues centre shows one warning listing it, like "5AM: 2 of what it plays is missing". The next project that resolves clears it.

h: Recipes › A sampler pad from a script
t: A sampler pad from a script. Load, play, loop, latch, stop: sh tools/device.sh call pads loadSample 0 /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/samples/refs/movie-intro-16s.wav sh tools/device.sh call pads audition 0 # one pass sh tools/device.sh call pads setFlag 0 looping true sh tools/device.sh call pads setLatched 0 true # held looping, as a long press does sh tools/device.sh call pads stopAll # what STOP does

h: Recipes › A pattern on the pads
t: A pattern on the pads. Fill pads 1–4 with a kick, snare, hat and clap from the device's library ( find /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/samples -iname "*kick*.wav" | head -1 ), then call pads loadPreset "Boom Bap" , cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED , meter the lane, cuia SWITCH_STOP_RELEASED . The step keys write the selected pad's row with LIVE off and play the pads with LIVE on ( SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED toggles it; a step key held past half a second latches its pad).

h: Recipes › A take into a pad
t: A take into a pad. With something on the input jack ( INPUT sets MIC, GUITAR or LINE): call pads setSelectedPad 2 , then call input record . With SMART on ( studio.input.autoStop , on by default), the take ends by itself half a second after the sound stops. Otherwise, call input stop . The processed take lands on the pad, trimmed to its last burst, and the journal shows takeReady . Without a signal, the take never stops by itself: that guards against stopping before anything was played.

Switch the trace on, then cuia SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED step by step, and read which item accepted each key. ALT + ▲ must land on the header from anywhere. Key 5 opens page 5, and pressed again toggles between SAMPLE KING and the PAD SAMPLER. The choice survives restarts, so check the nameplate in a screenshot before sending taps at a panel. A hold on the wrong one writes a step. Reference audio for sampling tests lives in the library's samples/refs/ folder ( /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/samples/refs/ ).

tools/device.sh graph all -s 60 checks the PipeWire / JACK graph ravving runs in: rates and periods against the driver's; linked nodes that aren't running; the audio threads' priorities; xruns over a minute; the ravving links. routing.md has the map of what ravving wires, and the tools: pw-top, pw-dump, pw-dot, jack_iodelay… tools/issues-test.sh checks the issues center end to end (reports over the fifo, order, dismiss, clear, the drawer card and the dialog).

The basic checks: sh tools/bluetooth-setup.sh --check . With a device at hand, over the fifo: tools/device.sh call bluetooth startDiscovery; sleep 10; tools/device.sh get bluetooth devices tools/device.sh call bluetooth pair 84:D3:52:35:80:99 # a speaker pairs without a prompt tools/device.sh get bluetooth pairing # a phone: {kind confirm, passkey} → answerPairing true tools/device.sh call bluetooth useAsOutput 84:D3:52:35:80:99 true tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED # heard on the speaker tools/device.sh call bluetooth sendFile AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF "/zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/exports/Lo-fi Say It.wav" What to measure: Metric How, on the device signal (RSSI, dBm: −30 excellent, −67…−70 good, below −80 drops) bluetoothctl info ADDR (RSSI while scanning), hcitool rssi ADDR once connected link quality / packet loss hcitool lq ADDR (255 = best); btmon -w /tmp/bt.snoop during playback and count retransmissions A2DP codec and latency pw-cli info <bluez sink id> ( api.bluez5.codec : SBC by default, aptX / LDAC when both sides have it); pw-top for the sink node's quantum and the graph's (the studio stays at 256 / 48000; the Bluetooth node runs its own) OBEX throughput transfer.transferred over time ( get bluetooth transfer ) what BlueZ sees btmon (HCI trace), busctl --system tree org.bluez , journalctl -u bluetooth what WirePlumber does journalctl --user -u wireplumber , with systemctl --user set-environment WIREPLUMBER_DEBUG=3 and a restart for the monitor's own lines

Tool What it does tools/video-test.sh the feature suite on the device (41 checks): a recording over the fifo while playing, the MP4's streams, starts, length and frame rate, the ring's dropped frames, the graph's xruns meanwhile, RECORD / STOP by the device keys (the music goes on), the TIMER and its cancel, VIDEO off, the computer link's state tools/computer-link-test.sh the computer link end to end against the device's own sshd (21 checks): a throwaway local user stands in for the computer (set up with the password, the key installed, Downloads found, a wrong password told apart, a file sent and compared, the key removed → refused); the user is removed and the previous computer put back tools/share-test.sh [FILE] the phone share from the laptop (31 checks): the newest video offered over the fifo, fetched with curl and compared (size, md5), a Range → 206, HEAD, 404s, the deliveries counted, stop → connection refused tools/video-mic-check.sh [SECONDS] a recording with the mic while the music is stopped, its audio measured (speak when told) tools/video-sync-check.sh the sync mechanism alone (a synthetic audio feeder + x11grab + the remux), PASS when both streams start together tools/video-encode-impact.sh [SECONDS] the tiers' cost while playing; mirror any change to the encoder arguments here and re-measure Scripts: set video countdown 0 , call video start , get video state , call video stop , get video lastFile , get video lastInfo , call video toggle , set video quality high , set video source camera , get video cameras ; call computer setup HOST USER PASSWORD 22 , call computer check , call computer send /path/file , call computer forget .

Everything a finger does on the device, a script can do through the remote-control fifo: load samples, write patterns, pick sounds, set the key and the tempo, and save the result as a project. Two complete ones to copy: tools/examples/five-am/ : the 5AM demo, with sections and the song by script. build.py writes the lines, and run.sh sends them. tools/examples/lofi-say-it.sh : a lo-fi hip hop project on the changes of "Say It (Over and Over Again)". A shell loop that reads a file line by line and calls tools/device.sh loses all but the first line, since the ssh inside reads the loop's stdin. Send the lines from one script on the device (run.sh), or use ssh -n .

FIFO=/tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo send() { timeout 2 sh -c "echo \"$1\" > $FIFO"; sleep 0.2; } call() { local line="call"; for a in "$@"; do line="$line|$a"; done; send "$line"; } setp() { send "set|$1|$2|$3"; } get() { send "get|$1|$2"; journalctl --user -u ravving --since '-5s' --no-pager | grep 'fifo get' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*= //'; } A script runs on the device; copy it there, as the example does with itself. Every call is one line on the fifo and takes about a fifth of a second, so a full project is a few hundred lines and a couple of minutes. tools/device.sh call|set|get do the same, one at a time, from the laptop.

Step Calls keep what is there, start clean get studio.projects dirty , call studio.projects saveAs NAME ; call studio.projects newProject tempo, swing, key set studio bpm 74 , set studio swing 0.58 (and set studio swingEighths true for jazz: the off-beat 8ths swing, not the 16ths; the header's SWING 8 / 16, tapped), call header setKey ROOT SCALE (root 0–11 from C, scale an index into Rave.scales: 0 natural minor, 1 major, 2 Dorian…). NEW resets the key to C minor : set it before writing anything in a key drums call drumsN clear , call drumsN toggleStep ROW STEP , toggleAccent STEP ; rows by get drumsN rows ; call drumsN saveAsPreset keeps the beat as "My Beat N" chords set chords bars 8 (the most a pattern holds), set chords viewBar B , then per step call chords setStepNotes STEP "48,52,55,58" (MIDI notes; a note outside the key makes the voicing chromatic). A run of the same voicing on consecutive steps is one held chord ; an empty step ends it. Diatonic shortcuts: setChord STEP DEGREE , or SLOTS: assignSlot SLOT DEGREE + cycleSlotBars SLOT . saveAsPreset keeps a chart as "My Progression N" (a longer form = several presets to switch between) bass, lead set bass bars 8 , set bass viewBar B , call bass setNote STEP NOTE (MIDI; C2 = 36 for the bass, C4 = 60 for the lead, see kits.json baseNote ), setNoteLength STEP STEPS (a note lasts one step unless set: a half note is 8, up to 64, into the next bars), toggleAccent STEP , toggleSlide STEP ; any note is accepted, in the key or not, and a preset keeps it exactly (the chart's ALTER and HOLD lanes) drum kits call drums1 loadKit PATH : a kit file, or a preset inside a soundfont with chosen rows ( …/FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3#128:32?CYMBAL=51&HAT=44 , the Jazz kit with its ride and hi-hat foot; engines.md ); call drumsN setRowLevel ROW 0..1 sounds call bass chooseSoundSource Upright (names from get bass soundSources ), call chords loadSoundPreset NAME for TAL's factory sounds, call bass.sound setValue CARD KNOB 0..1 for the synth's own SOUND MODIFIERS pads call pads clearPad N , call pads loadSample N PATH [start length] , call pads chopRegions N COUNT FIRSTPAD , set pads selectedPad N + call pads setValue MIX VOLUME 0.95 , set pads bars 8 , set pads viewBar B + toggleStep PAD STEP ; a long one-shot (a 16 s intro) needs a loop long enough not to retrigger it: 8 bars at 74 BPM is 26 s SAMPLE KING call sampler loadSample SLOT PATH ; set ravving samplerMachine 1 puts the pads on key 5 save call studio.projects saveAs NAME (a name typed in the dialog would do the same); get studio.projects current to check sections and the song the section on screen is what the calls above edit; call studio.sections rename s1 DROP , duplicate s1 (a copy, placed after the section ON SCREEN, which it becomes), setBars ID 1–8 , set MACHINE paused true (it rests in this section), move FROM TO (the list), removeFromSong 0 / appendToSong ID / setRepeats INDEX N (the song), set studio.sections mode 1 (SONG), pick ID (the one on screen when saved)

How to test and debug ravving on the device with the tools in tools/ . Everything here runs from the laptop against the device ( root@milo.local by default; set DEVICE= for another). The device's root shell is zsh: it does not split $var into words (pass a stored argument list as ${=var} ).

Tool Runs on What it does tools/device.sh laptop deploy, press keys (CUIA), tap, screenshot, play MIDI, read the log tools/midifile.py either write a MIDI file holding a note or a chord, to play in as a keyboard tools/meter.py device level, brightness and crest factor of any JACK ports tools/synthprobe.py device play a scripted note list straight into an engine and record it tools/analyse.py device measure a synthprobe recording: segments and a pitch track tools/lv2probe.sh device try an LV2 effect on a live signal before wiring it in tools/record.py device record JACK ports to a numpy file tools/repeatcheck.py either how exactly a recording repeats at a given length (STUTTER / LOOP) tools/default-app.sh device make ravving the device's UI, or go back to zynthbox-qml ( device.sh default … ) tools/boot-timing.sh laptop time ravving's start by phase over restarts or reboots tools/qml-profile.sh laptop record and summarise a QML profiler trace of a start tools/qml-profile-summary.py laptop read a .qtd trace: self time per type, file and event tools/static-analysis.sh laptop clang-tidy and clazy over src/ tools/bt-diagnose.sh device why a Bluetooth device does (not) connect or play, read-only ( device.sh bt [ADDR] ); device.sh bt capture records an HCI trace tools/audio-impact.sh laptop what the rest costs the sound: frames/s, CPU per thread group, realtime page faults, xruns, idle and playing The quality and performance checks (what to run when) are in quality.md , the test suites in testing.md . sh tools/device.sh tools copies the device-side ones to its /tmp . They need python3-jack and numpy there and must run under pw-jack : a plain JACK client (jalv over ssh included) would start its own jackd and break the session's audio.

The service comes back on its own: Restart=always , at most 5 starts in 2 minutes. startx leaves with 0 even when ravving dies under it, so on-failure would never fire. The next start tells the issues center how the run before ended ( src/backend/lastrun.h ): ravving keeps a marker, ~/.local/state/ravving/running , while it runs, and removes it on a clean exit (SIGTERM, a normal return). data/start.sh writes last-exit as " ", with 128 + n for signal n. Each ending reads as what it was, with the journalctl line to look at: a crash (signal 11 or 6), or a kill (9); a failure (exit 1), often the display going away; the session ending first: no exit written, because X stopped. To try it: pkill -SEGV -x ravving brings ravving back 3 s later with the issue "ravving stopped unexpectedly" (error). systemctl --user restart ravving reports nothing.

Deploy and wait. sh tools/device.sh deploy syncs the tree (not build/ ), builds, installs, restarts the service and returns once the journal says audio and MIDI wired , plus a moment for the window. Keys sent while ravving boots are lost.

Go somewhere and look. sh tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_NUMBER_3_RELEASED # page 3 (BASS) sh tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED sh tools/device.sh tap 255 766 # the bass's DRIVE chip sh tools/device.sh shot /tmp/bass.png # 1280 × 800; crop with PIL to read details The CUIA names are zynthbox's: SWITCH_STEP5_PRESSED / _RELEASED (a step key held, then let go), SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED (LIVE), SWITCH_SELECT_RELEASED , SWITCH_BACK_RELEASED , KNOB0_UP … KNOB3_DOWN (knobs 1–3 and the big one). A step key with LIVE off edits the pattern on release : switch LIVE on (MODE) before using step keys as a test signal, and off again after.

Call a backend method. For example sh tools/device.sh call pads loadSample 0 /zynthian/…/x.wav , call pads audition 0 , call pads setFlag 0 looping true or call input record . It's the fifo's call|OBJECT|METHOD|ARGS… line ( src/cuiafifo.h ). The fields are split on | , so paths keep their slashes. It invokes any Q_INVOKABLE or slot on a machine (by its kits.json key), studio , input or take , converting the arguments. The journal logs each call, with its arguments and whether it was found.

h: Recipes › Play notes as a keyboard
t: Play notes as a keyboard. python3 tools/midifile.py /tmp/c2.mid 36 , then sh tools/device.sh play /tmp/c2.mid . A chord: midifile.py /tmp/c.mid 40 52 67 . The notes go in through Midi Through (14:0), which ravving reads like any controller. The bass plays them when it's LIVE, or with nothing LIVE while its page is on screen.

While a note plays ( aplaymidi -p 14:0 /tmp/c2.mid & on the device): pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py TrackPassthrough:Channel4-lane1-dryOutLeft # rms 0.0256 hf 0.001 crest 3.44 Compare runs, never single numbers: an effect off, on, off again (the last run must match the first, or something else changed). hf/rms is brightness, crest falls with saturation or compression. Ports worth knowing: Port What it carries ravving-<machine>:<out> the engine itself ( ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 ) TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-dryOutLeft a machine's track after its EQ/compressor/pan (bass: Channel4) TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-wetOutFx1Left / Fx2 its reverb / delay send ravving-reverb:lv2_audio_out_1 , ravving-delay:outputleft the send effects GlobalPlayback:dryOutLeft the master, before the LIVE FX inserts Reference levels: the bass track ~0.026 RMS for a held C2, the drums 0.15–0.17 playing, reverb return 0.04 with a send on. A soloed machine (S) mutes the others' sends too: check the INSTRUMENTS chips before suspecting an effect.

h: Measure a sound › Check the wiring
t: Check the wiring. ssh root@milo.local 'pw-jack jack_lsp -c' lists every connection; follow a machine from its engine: ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 → SynthPassthrough:Synth4 → TrackPassthrough:Channel4-lane1 → AudioLevels:Channel4 → GlobalPlayback , with DRIVE on ravving-bass-drive between the engine and the synth slot. JackWiring logs audio and MIDI wired when every connection it wants exists, or some ports never appeared after 20 s.

h: Measure a sound › Try an engine
t: Try an engine. Before choosing one, run it alone and probe it: pw-jack jalv -n probe http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi & # on the device pw-jack python3 /tmp/synthprobe.py probe:lv2_events_in probe:lv2_audio_out_1 \ --notes "0.2:36:40:0.2 0.8:36:127:0.2 2.6:36:100:0.4 2.9:48:100:0.3" python3 /tmp/analyse.py --segment "plain:0.2:0.4" --segment "accent:0.8:1.0" --track "slide:2.85:3.15"

h: Measure a sound › Try an effect
t: Try an effect. lv2probe.sh URI SOURCE MIDIFILE sym=val … runs a throw-away copy of an LV2 fed from a port and measures it, one setting per call; DRIVE (Calf Saturator: input gain, saturation, makeup) is calibrated with runs like lv2probe.sh http://calf.sourceforge.net/plugins/Saturator ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 /tmp/n36.mid level_in=16 drive=5 . lv2info URI lists a plugin's ports and ranges; lv2ls | grep -i word finds plugins.

Record the master after the repeat while holding a pad, then check the repeat: pw-jack python3 /tmp/record.py ravving-repeat:out_l --seconds 4.5 & , hold STUTTER ( xdotool mousemove 400 113 mousedown 1; sleep 1.5; xdotool mouseup 1 ; the transport must play), then python3 /tmp/repeatcheck.py --file /tmp/record.npy --bpm 120 --length-steps 1 : ~0 live, 1.000 while held. Dragging a held pad is xdotool mousemove steps of 5 px while the button is down.

~/.local/state/ravving/session.json is the whole session, in the same format as a project: machines : each one's steps or line , bars , kit , sound , effects , level , paused , preset … bpm , swing , master , liveFx , globalEffects , ui . It's written 1.5 s after a change, and on exit. Projects are in /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/projects/ , where .current names the open one. To check a save and open round trip: copy session.json, SAVE, NEW, open the project again, and compare the two files' machines . Every machine should be identical. From QML: give studio.uiValue() its fallback with ?? , since a JS object doesn't convert to the C++ default; a JS object passed to C++ arrives as a QJSValue. setUiValue unwraps it, or it would save as null.

Logging. Categories are off by default: ssh root@milo.local 'systemctl --user set-environment QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true;ravving.midi.debug=true" && systemctl --user restart ravving' sh tools/device.sh log 30 ravving.cuia prints every key with where it landed ( accepted / unhandled ) and the focus chain; ravving.midi every external MIDI message. systemctl --user unset-environment QT_LOGGING_RULES turns them off again.

h: Read the saved state › Screenshots without the device
t: Screenshots without the device. RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR=dir RAVVING_STYLE=Basic RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/ravving captures every page and a few scripted states (src/main.cpp: add a step there, and find items by objectName with findItem() ). It also shows QML warnings: a clean run prints nothing.

Read both channels while someone plays or touches the plug's tip (a finger on a working input hums around −30 dBFS; an open one sits near −75): pw-jack python3 /tmp/record.py "Built-in Audio Stereo:capture_FL" --seconds 10 --save /tmp/l.npy amixer -c 3 sset "ADC Left Capture Source" "VINL1[SE]" # try the ADC's other inputs Two cards are called "Built-in Audio Stereo": the HiFiBerry, and a Dummy at −180 dBFS. Which one gets the number suffix ( capture_FL-92 ) changes between boots . Check with pw-dump , where the port alias names the card, or ravving's journal line input ports . ravving finds them itself ( InputPorts ).

h: Why a Bluetooth device doesn't connect or play
t: The report is read-only: nothing is connected or restarted, so it's safe while someone listens. sh tools/device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 # one device; no address: every known one sh tools/device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 -1d # only the last day of the journals sh tools/device.sh bt capture 60 /tmp/lg.snoop # btmon for 60 s: connect the device meanwhile btmon -r /tmp/lg.snoop | less # or open it in Wireshark The report has: the adapter and main.conf ; the A2DP endpoints PipeWire registered, one per codec, shared by every device; WirePlumber's Bluetooth drop-ins, and the PipeWire Bluetooth objects (card, sink, codec); ravving's loopback; per device: its record (keys hidden), its cached A2DP endpoints decoded (which codecs it takes), and the bluetoothd, WirePlumber and ravving journal lines; a tally: link up, Unable to select SEP , create-socket, page-timeout, profile-unavailable, A2DP transports opened. What each failure means is in "Bluetooth troubleshooting" below and in the Bluetooth page . In a capture: a page that's never answered shows as Create Connection , then Connect Complete … Page Timeout ; a link refused for lack of an endpoint shows the AVDTP Discover and Get Capabilities , then a disconnect with no Set Configuration .

Symptom Look at Likely control center: "its service is not running" / bluetooth.state unavailable systemctl status bluetooth → 203/EXEC the bluetoothd path drop-in missing (run the setup) the adapter shows but Powered: no after a power on rfkill list (soft blocked), bluetoothctl power on rfkill: rfkill unblock bluetooth the link comes up, then COULD NOT CONNECT · br-connection-create-socket and DISCONNECTED a second later journalctl -u bluetooth : Unable to select SEP ; device.sh bt ADDR another audio device streams the same codec (SBC): one local endpoint per codec. Disconnect it; ravving hands the link over itself when you connect from the dialog COULD NOT CONNECT · br-connection-page-timeout (bluetoothd: Host is down ) is the device on, in Bluetooth mode, not connected to a phone? device.sh bt capture while connecting it did not answer the page; ravving pages it again for about 37 s ("waking…"). A speaker that was last used with a phone connects only once milo pages it pairs but br-connection-profile-unavailable on connect bluetoothctl show has no Audio Source / Sink WirePlumber's monitor not running: the seat drop-in missing, or WirePlumber started before libspa-0.2-bluetooth was installed (restart it) connected, but no bluez_output.* node in wpctl status journalctl --user -u wireplumber the device connected HFP only, or the A2DP transport failed: disconnect and connect again the issues center: "… plays no sound" (or it went quiet and came back by itself) the journal: "plays silence: routing to it again", then "the output plays again" or not; pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py ravving-out:output_FL against ravving-phaser:out_l the loopback passes silence though every node runs and every link is there (after a codec switch replaced the sink): ravving routes again once by itself; if that fails, pick the jacks and the device again, or turn the device off and on PLAYING THROUGH says so but nothing is heard pgrep -af pw-loopback , pw-link -l \| grep -A1 ravving-phaser:out_l (should show ravving-out:playback_FL ), pw-top (the bluez sink R, the HiFiBerry S) the loopback did not start (pipewire-bin missing?) or its links failed: pick the jacks and the device again; the journal has "master linked to ravving-out" when it worked sound from the device and the Bluetooth device wpctl status (is the jacks' sink muted?) the jacks were not muted: pick the jacks and the device again glitchy sound over Bluetooth pw-top : is the bluez sink the driver of ravving's nodes? the default sink was switched by hand ( wpctl set-default ): put the jacks back as default, ravving routes through the loopback instead; Wi-Fi on the same antenna also costs (the Pi's radio is shared) sending fails at once: "COULD NOT REACH" busctl --user list \| grep obex , systemctl --user status obex obexd missing or not activatable; the phone must have OBEX push enabled (Android: accept the incoming file prompt) a phone cannot see milo bluetoothctl show → Discoverable: no VISIBLE lasts three minutes; press it again

The checks to run on ravving every so often (and before a release) and what each tool is for. All the tools live in tools/ ; the laptop ones need no libzynthbox (ravving builds without it), the device ones run against root@milo.local ( DEVICE= for another). When Run Look at after C++ changes tools/static-analysis.sh new lines in analysis/summary.txt against the accepted findings (§1) after changes to a shell script ( tools/*.sh , data/start.sh ) tools/static-analysis.sh shell (ShellCheck, here or on the device) analysis/shellcheck.log : the scripts are kept at zero findings; a finding that is the script's intent (a remote command built on the laptop, a deliberate word split) gets a # shellcheck disable= line with the reason above it after adding a pointer handler (Tap / Drag / Pinch / Point / Wheel) to a page or the header tools/static-analysis.sh handlers zero: each binds enabled: … !Session.inputBlocked , else a drag on a dialog reaches it (§1, "Handlers under dialogs") after QML changes the screenshot tour (§4) QML warnings in its output; pixel diffs against a reference tour after anything that touches startup tools/boot-timing.sh restart 5 the medians against the previous run's before a release tools/boot-timing.sh reboot 3 , tools/qml-profile.sh boot to first frame; what QML creates before it after any UI, animation, poll or watcher change, and in every phase pass tools/audio-impact.sh (§9) idle 0 frames/s; playing ≈ the playhead and meter rates; 0 RT-thread faults from ravving's own code; 0 xruns

tools/static-analysis.sh # both; or `tidy` / `clazy` alone It configures a separate build folder with a compile database: BUILD , by default /tmp/ravving-analysis , so the normal build/ is never touched. It generates moc and the QML type registration, then runs two tools over src/ only, in parallel: clang-tidy , with the repo's .clang-tidy ; clazy , levels 0–2, without the Qt-idiom noise listed in the script. Reports go to REPORTS (default ./analysis ): clang-tidy.log , clazy.log , and summary.txt with one count per check. Arch packages: clang (clang-tidy, run-clang-tidy) and clazy . A newer clang-tidy brings new checks. Decide for each whether it finds something or restates the house style, and turn the latter off in .clang-tidy , with a line saying why.

tools/static-analysis.sh shell runs ShellCheck 0.10 at -S style over every shell script; the baseline is 0 . ShellCheck is on the device ( apt install shellcheck ); on a laptop without it the script sends the files there.

The modal dimmer stops items, not pointer handlers. Qt Quick still hands a press to every handler under it after the dialog's button or field took it, and a page's DragHandler then takes the drag over past its threshold. Disabling the page while a dialog is up is no way out: a disabled ComboBox closes its own list at once. So: the modal layers (dialogs, the MENU drawer, a drop-down's list) register in Session.overlays , by identity, so a repeated open can't leave the page blocked; every handler on a page or the header binds enabled: !Session.inputBlocked ; tools/check-handlers.py ( static-analysis.sh handlers , also in all ) fails on a new one that doesn't.

What is left is known and accepted; anything not in this list is new and worth reading. Check Count Why it stays bugprone-implicit-widening-of-multiplication-result 12 soundfont record offsets ( index * Size ) and the track lanes: int-sized files and lists bugprone-signed-bitwise 11 MIDI status / channel and LED colour byte masks on int ; values are 0..255 bugprone-incorrect-roundings 3 int(x + 0.5) on frame counts, which are never negative bugprone-multi-level-implicit-pointer-conversion 2 jack_free(ports) and QMetaObject's void * arguments: the C APIs' own types bugprone-inc-dec-in-conditions 1 m_editGroup > 0 && --m_editGroup == 0 : the decrement is meant to be guarded readability-redundant-nested-if 1 LiveFx: the two conditions read as two decisions clang-analyzer-cplusplus.NewDeleteLeaks 1 false: the QFutureWatcher is parented to the machine and deleteLater() s itself clazy range-loop-detach 24 loops over temporaries ( toList() , split() ) on load paths; a member list looped often would be worth fixing (DrumKit::rows() was) clazy writing-to-temporary 2 QSettings(...).setValue() : the temporary's destructor writes it clazy connect-non-signal 2 clazy cannot follow a for over signal pointers (Studio); its own message calls it a clazy bug clazy qproperty-without-notify 1 HardwareEvent::accepted: a per-event object, never bound

main() writes the phases of a start to the journal ( src/startuptimer.h ): ravving: startup main 0 ms process up (after startx, X and the binary loading) ravving: startup application 18 ms QGuiApplication ravving: startup libzynthbox 649 ms libzynthbox's singletons and engines ravving: startup studio 2922 ms machines, effects, the session (Studio) ravving: startup qml 3681 ms Main.qml created ravving: startup first-frame … the first frame on screen ravving: startup wired … audio and MIDI connected tools/boot-timing.sh restart 5 # service restarts: CSV + medians, ms from the service starting tools/boot-timing.sh reboot 3 # reboots (ravving the default UI): also kernel boot → first frame tools/boot-timing.sh last # the last start, without restarting anything Compare medians, never single runs: the first frame moves by up to 3 s between runs because kwin starts beside ravving ( start.sh ) and the window is not shown before kwin manages it. The start depends on the page the session restores, since only the page on screen is built first. DRUMS is the heaviest (all three drum machines' step grids), and BASS a typical one. Compare runs on the same restored page: "page" in the session.json, 0 drums … 4 sampler. Before blaming a change for a slower start, compare against an old build (a git worktree , deployed) on the same day, project and page. The device's state moves the times too.

Restart sparingly. Every restart stops and starts the HiFiBerry's PCM, and after a few dozen in a session the Pi's RP1 audio DMA driver can oops (the device reboots itself). Prefer 3–5 runs per measurement, and take boot-timing.sh last after a start that happens anyway.

rsync -a keeps the laptop's modification times. A file edited before the device last built another tree then arrives older than that build's objects, and ninja skips it. tools/device.sh deploy syncs with rsync -rlp --checksum . After switching trees by hand, run find src qml -exec touch {} + on the device before building.

Only the page on screen is built before the first frame (Main.qml's PageLoader ). Once the first frame is up, the other four pages and the mixer are built, one per 40 ms tick. The page is restored (in main.cpp) before the QML loads, so the first page built is the right one. KnobBadge builds its drawing on first show ( shown , not visible ): most badges stay hidden. The LV2 ports are cached on disk (JalvPlugin::readPorts, ~/.cache/ravving/lv2-ports.json ) instead of lv2info running for each plugin built at start. Each entry carries its bundle's and binary's modification times; an installed or upgraded plugin does not match and is asked again. Delete the file to force a full re-read. Imported soundfonts cost next to nothing : only each font's preset list ("pdta") is read, found by walking the RIFF chunk headers ( SoundFontFile::presetData , which steps over an unpadded odd-sized chunk too). The journal says what it cost: ravving: kits N ms, imported soundfonts: F fonts, S sources, M ms (also after a USB import, refreshImported ); that line is the check after adding a font whose writer is new.

tools/qml-profile.sh NAME # ./NAME.qtd and ./NAME-summary.txt tools/qml-profile-summary.py NAME.qtd --type Creating --top 40 tools/qml-profile-summary.py NAME.qtd --from 2 --to 4 How it works: A systemd drop-in sets RAVVING_QML_DEBUG=10002,block . main.cpp opens the QML debug server, and waits for qmlprofiler before loading any QML. The script attaches on the device, waits for startup wired , and flushes the trace. It removes the drop-in and restarts ravving. The summary lists self time per event type, per file and per event. Look at Creating first, how many of what were built, and at the call counts: 1436 calls of one component is the finding, not its 0.1 ms each. Never probe the debug port by connecting to it: the server takes the first connection as its client.

RAVVING_STYLE=Basic QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 \ RAVVING_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data RAVVING_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/tour/project RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR=/tmp/tour/shots \ build/ravving 2>&1 | grep -v -i jack It visits every page and a few dialogs, saves PNGs and quits (main.cpp). Start from an empty project folder each time, since the tour turns knobs and the session keeps them. Build the reference from the previous commit the same way, and compare with compare -metric AE ref.png new.png null: (ImageMagick). QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING matters: without a terminal, Qt logs to the journal and the run looks silent. The Zynthbox style isn't on the laptop, hence RAVVING_STYLE=Basic .

tools/device.sh default ravving # or on the device: /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh ravving tools/device.sh default status tools/device.sh default zynthbox # back to stock; add --purge to uninstall ravving too default-app.sh masks zynthbox-qml in root's user units (a --user disable cannot undo its global enable in /etc/systemd/user , and updates re-enable it globally; the mask wins over both) and enables ravving. Going back unmasks and starts zynthbox-qml, disables and resets ravving, and drops the development environment ( RAVVING_GDB , RAVVING_QML_DIR ).

h: 6. The Store AppImage: the release check
t: tools/appimage-test.sh builds the AppImage on the device and installs it the way the Store does. Then it walks every choice of the setup page and ravving's ZYNTHBOX button by touch, asserting the device's state after each step. Run it after a version bump, or any change to setup/ , tools/default-app.sh , data/ravving.service or packaging/ . It takes about eight minutes, with results in analysis/appimage-test-<date>/ . Details are in packaging.md .

h: 7. Soundfonts and engines: when one is added
t: sh tools/soundfont-check.sh , run on the device from the laptop, takes every soundfont data/kits.json names: the drum kits, the machines' default engines, and every FluidSynth sound source. It checks each one: the file exists; its zones can sound. A font whose instrument zones declare a velocity range of 0–0 is mute at any velocity. SynStrings, LaString, MelloString and Organ.sf3 on the image are like that, and are left out; the preset the entry asks for (bank:program) exists in the font; a chord rendered offline through fluidsynth on that preset actually comes out: a kick, snare and hat for a kit, low notes for a bass, three seconds for pads that swell slowly. It prints PASS or FAIL per font, and exits with the number of failures. Run it after editing the sources in kits.json, after an image update (the fonts live in /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts ), and before a release.

tools/soundfont.py (presets · ranges · render · categorise) looks inside one font, and proposes kits.json entries for new ones ( categorise --json ). tools/mididump.py shows what an engine's JACK MIDI port really carries, for a source that stays silent in ravving but sounds offline ( testing.md ). A new engine type (a SoundEngine subclass) gets the same treatment. Its sources go into kits.json, the check runs, and pw-top shows its nodes' rate and quantum against the graph's (48000 / 256 on the device).

ravving's music player needs pipewire-pulse , since Qt's audio output on Linux is PulseAudio, so the unit wants it. Its stream runs at its own adapted quantum, and leaves the graph at 256 / 48000. The graph's rate is pinned ( clock.allowed-rates = [ 48000 ] ), so a 44.1 kHz file can't switch it. After a PipeWire update, check with pw-top -b -n 2 : idle, with an MP3 playing, and with the MP3 plus the transport. The driver must stay at 256 / 48000, with its xrun count unchanged.

h: 8. The audio graph: routing, clocks and xruns
t: When an engine, insert or route is added or changed, and in every phase pass: tools/device.sh graph all -s 60 # rates, idle-but-linked nodes, threads, xruns over 60 s, the links Expected on a Zynthbox: the driver is the sound card's playback node, at 48000 / 256; every ravving-* audio node is at 48000, with a period of 256 (jalv), or 512 (FluidSynth's stream, by design); no node with links is not running; 0 xruns in 60 s, idle and with the reference project playing. Run it twice, once with device.sh cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED first. Any steady xrun rate means a stall somewhere. Check first systemctl --user show-environment for RAVVING_GDB=1 (gdb costs 20–40 a minute). Then graph-check.py threads , for a render thread without realtime priority, or one above PipeWire's data loops. What each column means, and the tools behind it, are in routing.md .

h: 9. What the rest costs the sound
t: The sound comes first on this device: a feature, a poll, a watcher or an animation may not cost the audio anything it can hear. ravving's audio threads run at realtime priority, so other work can't preempt them directly. What it can do is: load the CPUs and the memory bus they share; stall a cycle with a page fault on a realtime thread; hold a lock the audio side needs. Measure it, before and after: tools/audio-impact.sh # 30 s idle, then 30 s with the transport playing tools/audio-impact.sh 20 idle # only the idle window (no keys pressed: safe while someone plays) tools/device.sh animations # what keeps the window drawing, item by item audio-impact.sh prints, per state: the frames per second the window put on screen ( Ravving.framesSwapped , counted on the render thread); CPU in % of one core, for the render thread, the GUI thread, ravving's realtime threads (policy FIFO / RR: the JACK clients, SyncTimer, MidiRouter…) and the rest; the page faults the realtime threads took; the graph's xruns over the window ( graph-check.py xruns , summed over the nodes, so one graph-wide dropout counts once per node). playing presses PLAY and STOP, so never run it while someone plays. idle only reads. What healthy looks like (a Pi 5, a full project): idle playing frames/s 0 16 (the 16ths' playhead and the 10 Hz meters) render / GUI thread 0 % / 3 % about 13 % / 10–15 % realtime threads about 14 % about 20 % RT page faults / 20 s 0–2 (PipeWire's own data loops) some in libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread, none in ravving's code xruns 0 0

An idle screen draws nothing. Before shipping UI work, tools/audio-impact.sh 20 idle must read 0 frames/s; if not, device.sh animations names the item. No Animator (Opacity/Scale/Rotation/XAnimator…) inside a Behavior : use NumberAnimation . No Behavior on something the transport changes at every step or every meter reading: those values change instantly. Anything fed by the audio side (positions, levels) is published at the rate the eye needs (15 Hz for a moving line, 10 Hz for meters), never per audio block. An infinite animation ( loops: Animation.Infinite ) runs only while its state lasts (a take waiting, a latched pad) and only while its item is shown. A grid, a play position or a progress reads the step playing only while visible : the hidden pages stay built in their StackLayout and must not follow the playhead. A poll that forks or blocks runs only while what it feeds is on screen, unless it watches for something that has to be noticed at once (a USB stick); measure it with this tool.

Views fed a plain list (a QVariantList from the backend, a JS array) rebuild every delegate whenever the list is set again. On the Pi, a row with a Zynthbox Button costs about 1.4 ms to make (five SVG frames). The long or often-updated lists go through KeyedListModel (src/, tests in tests/: cmake -DRAVVING_TESTS=ON build && ctest --test-dir build ). It applies a new list as the fewest row changes, matched by a key. The longest also set reuseItems . Its roles only grow , since a reset would rebuild everything, and a test keeps it so. Small fixed lists , like the banks and the kinds, stay plain. AFTER=script tools/qml-profile.sh profiles an interaction instead of a start.

Every phase of a feature ends with this pass. Run the suites with ravving under gdb on the device: systemctl --user set-environment RAVVING_GDB=1 , then a restart. start.sh prints a backtrace to the journal on a crash.
